Program, texts and objectives: Official language(s) of teaching and assessment: ITALIAN, ENGLISH
Specific learning objectives: The Master's Degree Course in Medical and Pharmaceutical Biotechnologies aims to train a professional figure with a solid cultural background and high levels of practical competence, who will be able to perform roles with responsibilities, in compliance with the areas of competence provided for by current regulations, in research, scientific innovation and the technical-productive development of biotechnologies applied in areas of interest to medicine, such as the prevention, diagnosis and treatment of human diseases, and in areas of interest to the pharmaceutical industry, such as the design, clinical testing, production and monitoring of drugs and biotechnological/diagnostic products at various stages of production/authorization for use.
The cultural, theoretical and practical profile of the graduate in Medical and Pharmaceutical Biotechnologies is also suitable for access to higher levels of university and specialist education.
The learning objectives are achieved through an advanced training program, which includes a first common year and a second year structured in differentiated curricula: the degree course is structured on cultural and methodological aspects of disciplines characterizing the 'LM-9 class of Master's Degrees in medical, veterinary and pharmaceutical biotechnologies' (the functional areas for the specificity of the course are the following: Basic disciplines applied to biotechnologies; Morphology, function and pathology of cells and complex organisms; Common biotechnological disciplines; Laboratory medicine and diagnostics; Medical-surgical disciplines and human reproduction; Pharmaceutical disciplines) and is completed with knowledge and skills acquired in related and complementary training activities, which develop specialist aspects of some scientific sectors, even if not characterizing the LM-9 degree class, but consistent with the proposed objectives.
In particular, the learning objectives are achieved through an advanced training program which, in the first common year, will allow the graduate to:
- have knowledge of the fundamental and molecular, immunological, physiological mechanisms underlying human diseases, of congenital or acquired origin, and skills to design, develop and apply strategies for scientific development and innovation based on the qualitative/quantitative assessment of physiological and/or pathogenetic determinants of biological processes of human interest;
- have in-depth knowledge of the function and analysis of (macro)biological molecules and the cellular processes in which they are involved; knowledge and mastery of the use of biochemical-molecular technologies and bio-informatics methods/tools for the management and access to databases for an interdisciplinary and holistic approach to the study of complex biological systems and, through the management of DNA/protein engineering technologies and computational analysis technologies, for the development of scientific innovations that evaluate the dynamic interactions through which biological macromolecules produce functional properties in living organisms;
- have knowledge of the principles for the definition of epidemiological investigation designs and the ability to apply statistical methods in the biomedical field and in epidemiological studies in order to acquire the scientific method of investigation, the mastery of the principles of experimental design on biological systems and skills to organize and manage data from observational studies;
- have knowledge of the biotechnological methodologies applied to the biological and chemical-toxicological analysis of drugs, diagnostics, vaccines, chemotherapeutic agents and other biologically active molecules, and used for therapeutic purposes;
- have methodological knowledge and skills for the use of advanced biotechnological technologies for the study of the morphology and function of cells and/or cellular and subcellular structures (also in relation to their organization in organs, systems and organs) for the understanding, manipulation and dissection of complex biological mechanisms, through research and experimentation strategies, in compliance with the principles relating to bioethics, and based on more traditional systems (in vitro models) or on more complex systems (in vivo models), and to address specific biomedical issues, also for application purposes, in the medical and pharmaceutical fields.
To guarantee a scientific investigation method based on the use of integrated approaches and with complementary functions, this knowledge and skills can be integrated, also through the specificity of related and complementary disciplines, with the fundamental and conceptual and methodological principles of innovative and/or specialist techniques/approaches for the dissection of biological phenomena related to the evolution of genes and, more generally, of gene expression.
The first year will also include the acquisition, within the scope of activities related to related and complementary disciplines, of knowledge and methodologies for the management and enhancement of intellectual property and projects resulting from scientific innovation.
In the second year, the degree course will be structured in differentiated courses (curricula) which, by deepening and integrating the professional aspects already acquired in the first year, provide more specific knowledge and skills for some application/employment areas of the graduate in Medical and Pharmaceutical Biotechnologies: the objective will be achieved both through some scientific-disciplinary sectors of the areas of the class, which already characterize the common path, but contribute to the specificity of the curriculum, and through areas of the class (in particular Laboratory Medicine and diagnostics, Medical-surgical disciplines and human reproduction and Pharmaceutical disciplines) to which a different weight is given according to the specific skills proposed in the curricula. The specialist nature of related and complementary activities can also contribute to the different curricular paths.
In detail, in the second year the graduate acquires a solid cultural and methodological preparation through training courses that have a more diagnostic and/or more translational and/or more pharmaceutical character.
The more diagnostic character of the training will be characterized, mainly, by cultural and methodological aspects of the disciplines of the 'Laboratory Medicine and diagnostics' and 'Medical-surgical disciplines and human reproduction' areas and will focus on knowledge and technologies, both conventional and advanced, applied in the various areas of laboratory medicine, used in a professional context in the diagnostic process, in laboratory diagnostics and for the development of screening/validation and toxicological monitoring strategies for diagnostics, vaccines and drugs.
The more translational character of the training will be characterized, mainly, by cultural and methodological aspects of the disciplines of the 'Medical-surgical disciplines and human reproduction' area, projected towards the transfer of the results of basic research to the development of diagnostic, prognostic and therapeutic systems applicable to clinical practice, with particular attention paid to translational/clinical aspects of personalized medicine, molecular diagnostics and/or therapies and/or reproductive biotechnologies and/or regenerative medicine: the training program allows the graduate in Medical and Pharmaceutical Biotechnologies to acquire skills to operate/manage technologies, in compliance with the areas of competence and in support of professionals also in the medical/clinical area, diagnostic and therapeutic strategies applied to clinical practice.
The more pharmaceutical character of the training will be characterized, mainly, by cultural and methodological aspects of the 'Pharmaceutical disciplines' with particular attention paid to aspects fundamental to the management of the entire scientific and technical-productive development process of drugs and innovative biotechnological products: the training objective in the pharmaceutical field aims at learning more modern methodologies and techniques used in the "drug discovery" phase, in the industrial phase and in the development and optimization phase of a drug, contributing to the acquisition of specialized skills in the fields of scientific/innovation research and development in the pharmaceutical and therapeutic field.
The training objectives are completed with practical-experimental activities, provided for in various training units, training internships carried out at the University or at bodies/research institutes, universities, companies or abroad (according to international agreements in the Erasmus program and/or agreements established by the University) and the preparation, in a laboratory, of an experimental thesis presented in the final examination: the training experiences listed allow to contextualize, in a laboratory/production reality, the knowledge and skills acquired.
The training program provides for flexibility in the choice of courses, among the activities included in the University's training offer and seminar-type courses (with final verification and according to the methods specified in the didactic regulations of the degree course), also in English, proposed by internal/external experts to the University and highly qualified, in order to integrate, in agreement with the training objectives of the degree course, the knowledge of advanced topics and specialized skills.
Lectures (in Italian and for some courses in English), laboratory exercises, consultation of teaching material, understanding and critical analysis of scientific literature, in-depth/autonomous bibliographic research on/of advanced scientific articles and texts, open group discussions on topics of the course of study, as integral parts of the learning methods, and intermediate and final verification tests and the preparation/discussion of the degree thesis, as verification methods, will contribute to the development/exercise/verification of the ability to learn and deepen, even autonomously, one's own knowledge, autonomy of judgment, aptitude for teamwork, acquisition of mastery and tools for communication and ability to present/transmit/disseminate one's knowledge.
The training program includes, in the Further linguistic knowledge, a course in English, at least at level B2, which guarantees, to the student who does not have these skills at the entrance, the achievement of a level of understanding of the English language that is suitable and essential both for the training experience provided in the activities proposed in English and for integrating communication skills in the language predominantly used in the international scientific field.
Dublin Descriptors: I - Knowledge and understanding The training program of the Master's Degree Course in Medical and Pharmaceutical Biotechnologies is structured in activities that allow the graduate to acquire:
Knowledge and understanding
- of statistical and epidemiological methods applied to medical-experimental biotechnological sciences
- of the fundamental and pathogenetic mechanisms of human processes, of different origin, with particular regard to the identification of potential targets to be used in investigation and therapeutic strategies, in acquired and genetic diseases;
- of the biochemical and molecular biology methodologies, for the study/analysis/characterization of biomolecules/biological macromolecules and of the bioinformatic methodologies for the management of biological data present in databases;
- of the mechanisms underlying the interactions between drugs/toxins and biological systems and of the methodologies for biological and chemical-toxicological analysis for the therapeutic and toxicological evaluation of drugs and xenobiotics;
- of the principles that regulate the management and enhancement of innovation and intellectual property;
- of the principles and regulations underlying bioethics in the development of experimental protocols;
- of advanced biotechnological technologies and experimental models for the study of the morphology and function of cells and their organization in organs, systems and organs.
In relation to the more diagnostic and/or translational and/or pharmaceutical character of the curricular paths offered
- of the culture, molecular, serological methods for the diagnosis of infections from pathogenic microorganisms, for humans;
- of clinical-diagnostic pathology and biochemical-molecular/omics technologies applied to the study of nucleic acids and proteins and used in laboratory medicine;
- of methodologies for the production of biologically active molecules for the development of innovative drugs;
- of the different classes of therapeutic proteins, monoclonal antibodies and innovative vaccines of the methodologies for the study to define their pharmacodynamic and pharmacokinetic profile;
- of the different phases and biotechnological skills required by the industrial production and marketing process of biopharmaceuticals;
- of molecular analysis methodologies and advanced biomedical technologies, applied in clinical practice in the medical, toxicological, therapeutic and reproductive field (including cell systems, bio-artificial tissues, gene therapy, etc.).
The acquisition of knowledge will be guaranteed by the following learning methods:
- Lectures (also with computer support) of training activities (characterizing and related and complementary), some organized in teaching units, and teaching material (textbooks, scientific articles/reviews, teaching material provided by the teacher).
- Laboratory exercises, provided in some teaching/training units, with theoretical/practical lessons that may also involve the use of computer programs - Seminar-type courses (with final verification) also in English, chosen by the student, for the in-depth/integration of advanced topics in the biotechnological/medical/pharmaceutical field.
The acquisition of knowledge will be verified through the following verification methods:
- Final exam (written or oral) individual aimed at verifying the knowledge provided in the various training activities.
- Intermediate tests provided in some teaching/training units for the purpose of in-course evaluation and/or feedback on the learning results expected.
II - Ability to apply knowledge and understanding The training program of the Master's Degree Course in Medical and Pharmaceutical Biotechnologies is structured in activities that allow the graduate to acquire:
- ability to apply knowledge of key aspects of cellular and molecular biology involved in pathological processes, of human interest and of different origin, to innovative approaches especially in the scientific/technological development in the biomedical field and in the design of biotechnological strategies in the clinical/experimental and pharmaceutical field;
- skills and competencies in recognizing elements of innovation, limitations and potential in the development projects of biotechnologies and in the design and application of new diagnostic strategies;
- ability to critically analyze the information provided by laboratory medicine;
- critical ability to process data in the application of molecular biology, biochemistry and bioinformatics methodologies;
- ability to monitor advanced technologies applied in the clinical/experimental field and apply molecular technologies and recombinant DNA and advanced biotechnologies for personalized therapeutic and diagnostic approaches;
- ability to evaluate compliance with the main aspects of bioethics in the development of experimental protocols;
- ability to organize and plan research or development activities of biotechnological products, demonstrating methodological application skills;
- ability to evaluate with competence the use of biopharmaceuticals, the various phases of clinical testing and validation and to discuss the key aspects leading to specific choices;
- ability to integrate biological, physiological, pathological, statistical, analytical, legislative data in the design/application of biotechnological/biomedical/pharmaceutical models/methodologies;
- ability to develop study methods and appropriate methodological paths, to select and interpret data and information and to work towards specific objectives;
- ability to make autonomous judgments and to learn autonomously, which supports the ability to operate with a critical and motivated approach to the choices made
- ability to present/transmit/disseminate one's knowledge, actions and information;
- critical and creative ability to plan strategies to be undertaken, to identify the appropriate resources/approaches to be applied, to monitor the impact of actions taken in order to achieve specific objectives or solve problems/questions.
The acquisition of the ability to apply knowledge and understanding will be guaranteed by the following learning methods:
- Lectures on the strategies and theoretical basis of biotechnological methodologies and/or advanced biotechnological approaches/models
- Laboratory activities (also with computer support), part of some teaching/training units, and the preparation of the degree thesis, within a Research Project.
The acquisition of the ability to apply knowledge and understanding will be assessed through the following verification methods:
- Exam (written or oral): in the final exam, for the verification of the acquired knowledge, the student's critical ability to interpret/understand/elaborate/discuss/analyze/choose/apply the knowledge acquired in the various training units is also verified through the solution of practical/applicative questions. This verification method may also be applied in intermediate tests where provided in some teaching/training units.
- Evaluation of the degree thesis: in the final examination, the critical ability and originality of the student in the project/experimental approach and in the choice of investigation tools and methodological approaches contribute to the evaluation.
III - Autonomy of judgment The training program of the Master's Degree Course in Medical and Pharmaceutical Biotechnologies aims to acquire the ability to autonomous reflection, development of critical sense and observational spirit in order to guarantee that the graduate can exercise the profession, in the various work contexts, medical-pharmaceutical in which he/she may operate, in full autonomy, with consistency and responsibility.
The graduate in Medical and Pharmaceutical Biotechnologies is able to:
- devise and formulate hypotheses and independently identify the most appropriate methodological approach to achieve the objective;
- use methodologies/procedures in the field of biotechnologies and evaluate their applicability in different contexts;
- collect, analyze, interpret and apply data in the considered 'systems';
- interpret sources and scientific literature
- in compliance with their own skills and with scientific-technological and ethical requirements, demonstrate the ability to make effective and quality choices.
The training objectives of the degree course, both in the more theoretical training activities and in the training activities of a more practical nature; the rigor and variety of the learning methods (lectures, teaching material, seminar courses) aimed at providing tools for a critical approach to advanced topics in the biotechnological/medical/pharmaceutical field; an interactive teaching that provides for discussions and comparison based also on research, understanding and autonomous elaboration of bibliographic material taken from the scientific literature of the sector; laboratory and internship activities that, through a scientific and analytical approach, provide interpretative hypotheses to be verified in relation also to potential/constraints/limits deriving from contextual factors; participation in a research project for the experimental degree thesis represent the tools that will guarantee, to the student guided by tutors/teachers/supervisors, the development of critical sense, autonomy of judgment, ability to support a dialectical confrontation on their theses, even in collective contexts, decision-making ability and ability to apply, in a consistent manner, the acquired knowledge.
Written and/or oral verification exams, intermediate tests will provide feedback on the student's ability to understand/deepen/elaborate and the ability to apply the acquired knowledge to the planning and implementation of theoretical/practical/applicative problem-solving in the medical-pharmaceutical field.
The final examination with the evaluation of the critical ability and originality of the student in the preparation of the experimental degree thesis, within a Research Project, will represent a further method of verifying the acquired autonomy of judgment.
IV - Communication skills The graduate in Medical and Pharmaceutical Biotechnologies acquires at the end of the training program:
- communication skills adaptable to both interlocutors with the same or different specialist training in the sector and to different scientific/business/cultural contexts;
- ability to disseminate with appropriate language and synthesis skills the experimental data/results of their activity and to draw up reports suitable for the operational contexts in which they operate;
- ability to manage tools for presenting scientific information;
- relational skills in the context of discussions (also in groups), on projects/protocols/experimental results, in biotechnological/business/biomedical contexts both nationally and internationally.
The acquisition of these skills will be developed/evaluated
- in the frontal teaching and in the practical experience in the laboratory, in which the student is involved in participating with colleagues and communicating with appropriate language
- in the internships carried out in research laboratories/companies in which the student can also communicate with figures from different professional contexts;
- in the seminar activities held by experts in the field (also in English)
- in the use of conventional teaching, learning and verification tools (in written and oral form that involve the student for the development of communication skills and appropriate vocabulary) and of a more IT nature through the aid of multimedia systems (which, through the production of personal or group elaborations/presentations, stimulate not only the research, elaboration and presentation of knowledge, but also interpersonal communication);
- in the discussion of the degree thesis and during the carrying out of verification tests in which the student will have to use appropriate language, demonstrate mastery of appropriate terminology and ability to present/transmit/disseminate their knowledge.
The knowledge of the English language, provided for in the training program, will integrate the ability to communicate also in the language predominantly used in the international scientific community.
V - Learning ability The Master's Degree Course in Medical and Pharmaceutical Biotechnologies provides the tools to acquire a study method, critical ability and learning skills suitable for dealing with scientific, technological and cultural problems in specialized biomedical, clinical and pharmaceutical fields, also in an autonomous way and with the ability to update their knowledge on innovations, regulations, methods, technologies/tools in a constant manner (through the reading of scientific articles, consultation of national and international bibliographic sources, consultation of databases and bioinformatic resources, etc.), to compare their knowledge with the knowledge of experts in the field and/or in related fields and to design/develop/organize their activity, both in the professional world of reference in rapid and continuous evolution, and within university training programs of the third level (PhD, second-level master's degree, specialist school) with a flexible mentality, with competence and with a critical approach to knowledge.
The degree course, through conventional teaching tools and/or IT and multimedia equipment, seminars, studies/reports/personal presentations, laboratory and tutorial activities and experimental work in research groups, offers culturally versatile experiences that promote and stimulate the development of critical skills and flexible learning skills that will allow to carry out/conduct research and studies on medical-pharmaceutical or related sectors and, in general, to continue autonomously the training and updating even after obtaining the degree.
The assessment of learning in progress (partial tests, PowerPoint seminar presentations, etc.), the profit exams in writing and/or orally, the individual work for the preparation of the degree thesis will allow the verification of the ability to learn and the ability to update, also autonomously, the knowledge.
Professional role in the working context.
Professional role in the working context:
The biotechnologist specialized in the medical and pharmaceutical field will be able to use the knowledge and skills acquired in the training program in areas of research, development, production and services in public and private structures and biotech companies.
- The biomedical culture on the relationships between structure/function of biological macromolecules and the human organism, at different organizational levels and in physiological and pathological conditions, and the knowledge of advanced and specialized techniques fundamental in the fields of biotechnologies applied to "human health", acquired also on the basis of a solid practical laboratory experience;
- the ability to apply knowledge of key aspects of cellular and molecular biology involved in processes of human interest and of different origin, to innovative approaches especially in the scientific/technological development in the biomedical field and in the design of biotechnological strategies in the clinical/experimental and pharmaceutical field;
- the ability to integrate biological, biochemical, statistical, analytical data for the design and/or application/transfer, in clinical/therapeutic practice, of methodologies and/or diagnostic, vaccine and biotechnological products;
- the ability to apply advanced biotechnological techniques in laboratory medicine for the study and analysis of "determinants" of physiological and pathological alterations for diagnostic, preventive purposes and for the monitoring/validation of the effect of biopharmaceuticals, diagnostics and vaccines;
- the ability to organize and manage observational studies in research, in clinical/pharmacological experimentation and in the quality control of products and services, and production processes, and the knowledge of cultural contexts, with particular reference to the themes of the enhancement of intellectual property;
allow the graduate in Medical and Pharmaceutical Biotechnologies to carry out tasks that promote the development, scientific and technological-productive innovation of biotechnologies applied in the experimental, diagnostic, therapeutic, management and production field.
The knowledge and skills acquired allow the biotechnologist specialized in the medical and pharmaceutical field to carry out the following functions:
- organize, design with operational autonomy and coordinate interdisciplinary protocols of basic and applied research, aimed at expanding and innovating scientific knowledge and its application in the scientific and technical-productive field of sectors such as the chemical-pharmaceutical, therapeutic and medical-diagnostic sector;
- organize and carry out laboratory activities, basic and advanced diagnostic investigations requiring the use of innovative biotechnological methodologies (molecular, genetic, cellular, omics and bioinformatic);
- assist, within the areas of competence provided for by current regulations, professional figures in the medical area in the development and experimental testing of innovative diagnostic/therapeutic products also involving the manipulation of genetic/biological material/engineered cells;
- develop, design, formulate and experiment, on the basis of chemical, biological and toxicological aspects, new biotechnological products and biopharmaceuticals collaborating, also in the management of innovation projects and in activities of marketing, in teams with other professional figures with specific backgrounds for the discipline;
- participate and carry out functions and activities of evaluation, monitoring and validation of clinical studies in various therapeutic areas according to current regulations;
- participate in the development and/or evaluation to proceed with the application of patents in the biomedical field;
- conduct and coordinate programs for the development, monitoring and prevention and diagnosis through the management of advanced biotechnological/biomedical technologies;
- deal with scientific dissemination and/or consulting activities with public and private bodies/biotech companies.
Skills related to the function.
Skills related to the function:
The graduate in Medical and Pharmaceutical Biotechnologies has advanced knowledge and high levels of competence in the promotion and development of scientific and technological-productive innovation of biotechnologies applied in the medical and pharmaceutical field.
The graduate in Medical and Pharmaceutical Biotechnologies has:
- theoretical, scientific, methodological knowledge for the study of the morphology, function and pathology of cells of complex organisms, knowledge of the principles for the definition of investigation designs and mastery of technologies and principles of experimental design on biological systems, in order to design and develop experimental research, using in vitro and in vivo models, for the study of indicators of cellular and molecular pathogenetic alterations of diseases, congenital or acquired, for the development/monitoring of new biotechnological drugs and, in compliance with the areas of competence and in support of professionals also in the medical/clinical area, to participate in translational projects;
- advanced knowledge and ability to apply the principles of biochemistry, cellular biology, molecular biology and recombinant DNA for the management of both technologies applied to laboratory medicine and in the technical-productive field and of advanced technologies, for the development, validation and application of tools for investigation and treatment of alterations in the human organism;
- solid knowledge of the analysis and function of biological macromolecules and cellular processes in which they are involved and biochemical-pharmaceutical skills for the formulation and design, with advanced technologies and on chemical/biological/toxicological bases, of bioactive molecules, drugs, vaccines, xenobiotics;
- mastery of bio-informatics methodologies, for the organization/construction/access to databases, knowledge of advanced recombinant DNA technologies, proteomics and skills in pharmaceutical disciplines to collaborate, in concert with professional figures in the medical, statistical and chemical-pharmaceutical sector, in the development and validation of new personalized therapies based on the use of new molecular target drugs based on the screening of the most modern platforms and on technologies for profiling genes;
- knowledge of activities of pharmaceutical marketing and knowledge relating to the management of intellectual property/innovation projects, for the dissemination of scientific/technological information; to coordinate/participate in activities of development and consulting within the framework of programs for monitoring; to design and develop biotechnological products and proceed with their application in the industrial field collaborating/contributing also to projects for the enhancement and management of intellectual property in the area of biotechnologies;
- ability to learn autonomously and to understand and elaborate scientific literature in the sector, which supports the ability to operate in a professional context not only on standardized situations and models, but to guarantee a critical and motivated approach to the theoretical/practical/applicative choices made
- communicative and relational skills in the biotechnological-pharmaceutical area that allow to expand the comparison with the world of research and national/multinational companies, to relate to health professionals and/or specialists and non-specialists in the biomedical/pharmaceutical field and to disseminate scientific data.
Professional status conferred by the degree.
Employment opportunities:
The employment opportunities for graduates in Medical and Pharmaceutical Biotechnologies are in public and private bodies and companies, in areas with a predominantly biotechnological, pharmaceutical and biomedical character, exercising their function in autonomy and/or in support of other professional figures.
In particular, graduates in Medical and Pharmaceutical Biotechnologies will exercise the profession in:
- Universities, public and private research institutes, institutions (e.g. Ministry of Health)
- Public and private health structures
- Biotechnology industries and service centers
- Pharmaceutical industry and control
- Diagnostic and pharmaceutical research and industry
- Biotech industry
- Companies for the development, marketing and management of biomedical equipment
- Bodies responsible for the preparation of health regulations and monitoring of clinical studies
- Scientific publishing companies;
- Scientific dissemination and information sectors.
The graduate in Medical and Pharmaceutical Biotechnologies can also:
- follow the enabling process for teaching and according to current regulations, which regulate access to the various classes of competition and may require the integration of training with specific skills, exercise their professional function in educational and school structures.
- pursue an academic career in universities according to current regulations that regulate access to it.
According to current regulations, some professional roles, especially in the medical-health field and/or for higher levels of responsibility, require (in the public sector and also in some regions in the private sector), in addition to registration in the reference professional register (see regulations for registration in the National Order of Biologists), also the possession of further skills acquired in post-graduate training programs, such as, for example, Specialist School of the Health Area reserved for Non-Doctors, professional courses, second-level master's degrees, PhD, to which the graduate in Medical and Pharmaceutical Biotechnologies can access.

Program, texts and objectives: Official language(s) of teaching and assessment: ITALIAN.
Degree awarded: Master's Degree in LITERARY AND CULTURAL STUDIES.
Specific learning objectives: The Master's Degree in Literary and Cultural Studies, in full accordance with the professional profiles and employment opportunities envisaged for its graduates, aims to provide the philological-literary, linguistic and historical tools that enable its students to achieve a thorough awareness of the complexity and problematic nature of texts, both literary and non-literary, which will be examined, analyzed and interpreted through the critical use of the bibliographic tools of the relevant field. Most of the disciplines are therefore in the literary, critical-literary, linguistic-philological area. Historical, philosophical, anthropological and geographical disciplines are added to complete the program.
Starting from a broad base of fundamental teachings in literary, philological and linguistic culture, and from the substantial coincidence of the methodologies applied, two curricula are proposed, focusing on the specific characteristics of the ancient world and the modern and contemporary eras, respectively. In particular, the classical curriculum gives priority to the area of learning related to the Greek and Roman philological and historical field, enhanced by teachings in the ancient, but also medieval and modern, literary and historical field; the modern curriculum is aimed at the knowledge and understanding of the Italian literary landscape and the evolution of the Italian language, placed in the broader context of Italian, European and extra-European historical and cultural development.
The study plan concentrates most of the characterizing exams in the first year, and reserves the second year for the student's elective courses, thus allowing the possibility of dedicating a good part of their time to research and the writing of the thesis, for which 30 CFU are reserved. The related courses are also included in the first year; they allow for some optionality, which enables students to deepen a specific area and/or complete the requirements for a specific teaching qualification.
The teaching activities are organized on a semester basis; lectures are supplemented by seminars and supplementary activities aimed at stimulating students' critical participation and in-depth study of specific interests; up to 6 CFU are also planned for internships and traineeships.
Dublin descriptors: I - Knowledge and understanding: The knowledge that forms the core of the course of study concerns the procedures for interpreting texts, and is acquired through the teachings of the literary and general linguistics sectors (L-FIL-LET and L-LIN/01). Valid support for both the historical, geographical, anthropological and aesthetic-philosophical contextualization and the acquisition of technical skills will be provided, depending on the chosen curriculum, by the M-GGR, M-DEA, M-FIL, M-STO and L-ANT sectors. The acquisition of these skills is assessed, for students of both curricula, through written or oral reports given by students in the individual courses, through the final exam of each course, and through the final exam.
Graduates will also acquire knowledge and skills aimed at using the main computer tools and telematic communication. The achievement of this objective is the purpose of the inclusion in both curricula of the teachings of the ING-INF/05 sector, Information Processing Systems.
II - Ability to apply knowledge and understanding: The graduate in Literary and Cultural Studies, within the scope of his/her field of study and in a research context, is able to use the tools at his/her disposal in the best and most autonomous way, to master different critical methodologies in the study of texts (from linguistic and philological analysis to historical and cultural analysis), to identify and develop original research topics.
In addition, the graduate will be able to apply methods and tools for the linguistic, philological and historical analysis of texts, both literary and non-literary; and to interpret them in their multiple aesthetic, cultural and symbolic aspects. This competence will be useful to understand and enhance literature and, in general, the humanities in the current global context, in which cultural production and all of the imaginary take on multiple forms and are transmitted through increasingly complex technological media.
The ability to apply knowledge and understanding must also be supported by adequate linguistic skills (at least level B2) in at least one language of the European Union in addition to Italian; and may also be supported by adequate computer skills.
- In order to achieve the ability to apply knowledge and understanding, attention is paid to the methodological and applicative aspects of the knowledge acquired. The student will be constantly confronted with recent scientific results through the use of simulation strategies that openly require the implementation of application and problem-solving skills. The knowledge and skills are acquired, as regards the procedures for interpreting texts, through the teachings of the L-FIL-LET and L-LIN/01 sectors. Valid support for both the historical, geographical, anthropological and aesthetic-philosophical contextualization and the acquisition of technical skills will be provided, depending on the chosen curriculum, by the M-GGR, M-DEA, M-FIL, M-STO and L-ANT sectors. This will be made possible mainly through lectures and exercises; participation in seminars or workshops, bibliographic research on specific and complex topics; use of databases, dictionaries, etc. This will allow students to formulate updated and conscious judgments, to develop autonomous reflections and to apply the knowledge acquired in an original way. This independence of judgment will have positive repercussions on the student's future professional activity.
- The verification of the acquisition of the ability to apply knowledge and understanding takes place jointly with that of the knowledge and skills of understanding, and specifically through written or oral reports given by students in the individual courses, the final exam of each course, and the final exam, to which a significant weight is given. The final exam involves the preparation of a thesis to be discussed before a commission that makes a judgment based on the student's career and the discussion itself.
- The verification of the ability to apply linguistic skills at level B2 in at least one foreign language will take place through the certification of training credits in the activity "further language skills". Finally, the ability to use computer tools can be assessed, in addition to the suitability in "computer and telematic skills", also through the examination of the teaching in the ING-INF/05 sector, Information Processing Systems, provided among the related courses.
III - Autonomy of judgment: Starting from the interpretation of the knowledge acquired (notions and fundamental methods in the field of the various humanities), through diversified analysis and comparison tools, the master's graduates in Literary and Cultural Studies develop the ability to formulate autonomous opinions and judgments. The critical reading of texts and contexts translates into a methodological attitude of thought that will allow them, also in the future, and more generally, an analytical look at reality and a coherent reflection even on social, ethical, political issues. In particular, the knowledge of the ancient world and its texts, in the case of the classical curriculum, promotes the understanding of current themes and problems, but with origins that lie in our cultural tradition of ancient Greece and Rome. Graduates in the modern curriculum can interpret and understand texts and facts of today, often offshoots of the most recent cultural history of our country.
- In order to achieve autonomy of judgment, the use of dialogical and interpretative methodologies, both written and oral, will be encouraged. Specifically, the skills described, such as the ability to independently interpret the results of textual and literary analysis, to grasp the meaning of a series of information and to interpret texts using contextual elements, to synthesize the results of the analysis, etc., will be verified through written reports, short essays and essays, as well as the work presented in the final exam. The idea is to encourage the active participation of each student and to provide for the development of an autonomy of judgment based on the critical reworking of the knowledge acquired. In this sense, ad hoc exercises will be prepared on texts and sources of particular relevance (linguistic, literary, historical, etc.), conferences and seminars of high scientific value will be organized, led by national and international experts; students will be able to prepare original and methodologically correct reports. The knowledge and skills will be verified through the exams, including the final exam.
IV - Communication skills: At the end of the training course, the master's graduates in Literary and Cultural Studies acquire the ability to communicate, in both oral and written form, information, ideas, problems and solutions, to specialist and non-specialist interlocutors. They must be able to use both disciplinary-specific vocabulary and translate specialist topics into more accessible forms. This objective is mainly achieved through the linguistic and literary training activities, as well as the mastery of a European language (in addition to Italian), study stays abroad and the acquisition of computer skills for the humanities. Clarity in presentation, ability to synthesize, coherence in argumentation are requirements required in disciplinary exams, in seminar activities with the preparation of short papers and oral presentations in class during the courses, in the moments of discussion and comparison often present also in the frontal teaching activities, and in the written preparation of the final exam.
- The verification of the communication skills acquired takes place through the profit exams distributed along the sessions provided during the academic year; on the occasion of other training activities, also chosen on the basis of the curriculum, which provide for oral communication in public, written elaborations in the form of short papers, descriptive, summarizing, explanatory texts; with the final exam. In addition, the communication skills at level B2 in the foreign language will be certified through a specific language test at the University Language Center or through the recognition of credits on certifications issued by accredited bodies. The ability to communicate through current computer technologies will be verified, in addition to the suitability in "computer and telematic skills", the examination of the teaching in the ING-INF/05 sector, Information Processing Systems, also on the occasion of laboratory, seminar, internship activities that provide for the use of the main applications of word processing, data entry and processing, interactive and multimedia presentation.
V - Learning ability: The master's graduate in Literary and Cultural Studies, at the conclusion of the university course, will have developed the ability to use autonomously strategies for a careful exegesis of texts (not only literary) in order to identify their different components, which in turn allow their framing in the historical and cultural contexts of reference. The course of studies also allows its graduates to develop learning skills suitable for undertaking further training paths: specialized internships, research doctorates, related or divergent master's degrees. The teachers of each discipline, in fact, apply themselves not only to transmit updated content and to use new tools of investigation, but also to stimulate cultural awareness and a high degree of autonomy of their students in researching objects of interest, supplementary study paths, their own forms of expression.
The verification of the learning skills acquired, in addition to throughout the course through the profit exams, is the subject of particular evaluation within the final exam.
Function in a working context:
Function in a working context:
The master's graduate in Literary and Cultural Studies will be able to perform various functions, also differentiated according to the different knowledge and skills deepened in the two curricula provided for by the Course. The figure of the Operator of editorial, documentary and cultural services, in fact, depending on the knowledge and skills deepened in the two paths, can be specified as follows:
1. Operator of editorial and documentary services. With reference to this figure, the master's graduate in Literary and Cultural Studies may perform functions such as:
- editor, chief editor, publisher in publishing houses, radio-television stations, magazines and newspapers, both on paper and on the web (after passing the suitability exam for access to the profession of journalist);
- head of library and archive, head of the documentation system, of the consultation, loan and access service.
2. Operator of cultural services. With reference to this figure, the master's graduate in Literary and Cultural Studies may perform functions such as:
- promoter, organizer and manager of conferences and cultural events for the transmission and dissemination of humanistic knowledge in public and private bodies;
- promoter, organizer and manager of events in the field of arts and entertainment.
Skills associated with the function:
Skills associated with the function:
The functions that the master's graduate in Literary and Cultural Studies can perform are linked to different skills. Each curriculum allows for the deepening of knowledge and skills more targeted to specific functions, specific professional and employment opportunities.
With reference to the functions related to the figure of Operator of editorial and documentary services: solid and in-depth philological, linguistic and humanistic skills in the field of Greek and Latin languages and literatures and the political, social and artistic history of antiquity (classical curriculum); solid and in-depth philological, linguistic and humanistic skills in the field of Italian literary history (seen in its relationship with the overall historical and cultural development) and the history of the Italian language, placed in the broader context of Italian, European and extra-European historical and cultural development (modern curriculum); linguistic skills at least at level B2 in at least one language of the European Union in addition to Italian; advanced skills in managing and interpreting texts; skills in the critical use of bibliographic tools and multimedia sources; high ability to conceptual elaboration and elaboration of argumentative, expository, popular texts; solid skills in documentary classification; full mastery of the most common word processing, editing and layout programs.
With reference to the functions related to the figure of Operator of cultural services: solid and in-depth philological, linguistic and humanistic skills in the field of Greek and Latin languages and literatures and the political, social and artistic history of antiquity (classical curriculum); solid and in-depth philological, linguistic and humanistic skills in the field of Italian literary history (seen in its relationship with the overall historical and cultural development) and the history of the Italian language, placed in the broader context of Italian, European and extra-European historical and cultural development (modern curriculum); linguistic skills at least at level B2 in at least one language of the European Union in addition to Italian; advanced skills in managing and interpreting texts; skills in the critical use of bibliographic tools and multimedia sources; high ability to conceptual elaboration and elaboration of argumentative, expository, popular texts; ability to design, direct and carry out cultural events; solid organizational and responsibility skills in the field of theater, cinema and entertainment; full mastery of the most common word processing, editing and layout programs.
In addition, the master's degree in Literary and Cultural Studies allows you to acquire skills and credits useful for continuing in the further paths provided for by current legislation on training and access to the roles of secondary school teacher.
Professional status conferred by the degree:
Employment opportunities:
- Publishing houses and service agencies; private companies and public bodies operating in the publishing sector; newspapers on paper and on the web; radio and television broadcasters;
- Research and study centers, public and private;
- Institutions responsible for the preservation of documentary assets, archival research (libraries, archives);
- Public and private bodies, in the cultural services sectors; Italian and foreign cultural bodies interested in promoting a more widespread knowledge of Italian literary production, past and present;
- Companies in Italy with international relations.

Program, texts and objectives:
Official language(s) of teaching and assessment: ITALIAN
Degree awarded: Master's Degree in HEALTH AND NUTRITION BIOLOGY
Specific learning objectives:
The Master's Degree in Health and Nutrition Biology aims to train graduates with advanced and practical skills in the field of biomedical sciences and nutrition, combined with in-depth scientific and practical training in the disciplines that characterize the curriculum.
Theoretical preparation is complemented by extensive experience in applied aspects. In the second year of the degree course, approximately half of the student's teaching workload is focused on the thesis. The aim is to provide students, through significant experimental work in a laboratory, with the opportunity to acquire both the cultural tools and the critical analysis skills necessary for research activities or to take responsibility for projects and structures.
The training program is divided into two curricula, "Biosanitary" and "Nutrition," and aims to achieve: - adequate cultural preparation in the biological field with training activities aimed at acquiring knowledge and statistical, computer, chemical, biochemical, molecular genetics, pharmacological-toxicological, and anatomo-pathophysiological tools, as well as achieving a good mastery of the techniques useful for their understanding in relation to various applications in the field of biomedical research;
- solid knowledge of the properties of nutrients and non-nutrients contained in food and any related modifications during technological processes, the biochemical and physiological mechanisms of digestion, absorption, and metabolic processes related to nutrients, as well as the ability to assess, using the main laboratory techniques, the composition and body metabolism and energy expenditure, and to recognize the effects of quantitative and qualitative malnutrition.
- adequate theoretical and practical preparation on the investigation methods used in the biosanitary field, including computer tools for support;
- knowledge of the influence of food on well-being and the prevention of diseases and the safety levels of food during technological and/or biotechnological processing, as well as the toxicological levels, acceptable daily intakes, and the risk that can be assessed in the consumption of substances contained or conveyed by the diet; knowledge of the pharmacology of nutrient substances, food supplements, various substances of natural origin, minerals and vitamins, the effects of drugs on nutritional status and nutrient absorption, on taste perception, on hunger and satiety, and on malabsorption mechanisms, as well as the relationships between nutrition and drug action.
- adequate mastery of the scientific method of investigation, allowing participation in the design of experiments and having acquired a level of knowledge of the English language and scientific literature that allows the use of computer communication techniques and the presentation of one's results in an international environment;
- knowledge of the main industrial technologies applied to the preparation of food; knowledge of the methodologies used in biochemistry, microbiology, genetics, pharmacology, toxicology, molecular biology, genetic and protein engineering, in metabolic and nutritional analysis, as well as in the analysis and manipulation of biological macromolecules, cells, microorganisms, and complex organisms; knowledge of the criteria and methods of biological and quality control of conventional and/or bioproducts.
- the ability to hold positions of responsibility in both the public and private sectors; having the cultural basis to access Biosanitary Specialization Schools recognized by the Ministry of Health, necessary for a managerial career in the laboratory and biosanitary field, both public and private, in Research Doctorates in the biomedical field, and in Second-level Masters.
For the training objectives that characterize the study course, reference is made to the principles of European harmonization, which encourage the alignment of the skills of graduates in the Master's Degree Course with the specific requirements identified by the Dublin Descriptors system according to the Tuning Table prepared at the national level (CBUI College) for the LM-6 class, as reported below.
Dublin Descriptors: I - Knowledge and understanding: Acquisition of integrated cultural skills with reference to the biomedical, nutritional, and other application sectors; acquisition of advanced scientific preparation at the morphological/functional, chemical/biochemical, cellular/molecular, physiopathological, microbiological, pharmacological-toxicological levels, of the mechanisms related to the physiology, pharmacology, pathology, and Nutrition.
Learning methodologies: The aforementioned knowledge and understanding skills are acquired through participation in lectures, exercises, and seminars, guided personal study, and independent study, as provided for in the training activities.
Verification of learning: The achievement of the specific training objectives of each teaching activity will be verified through tests, written or oral, for each course, which contain questions aimed at stimulating the critical re-elaboration of knowledge.
II - Ability to apply knowledge and understanding: Acquisition of in-depth multidisciplinary skills for biological analysis, of a methodological, technological, and instrumental type (instrumental methodology, analytical instruments, data acquisition and analysis techniques, computer and mathematical tools for support, scientific method of investigation).
Learning methodologies: These skills will be acquired in the training activities related to the courses of the characterizing and related and integrative areas, which will be carried out in the classroom, in the laboratory, and including independent study of research publications, as well as the practical application of scientific experiments carried out under the guidance of teachers.
Verification of learning: The evaluation of the acquired application skills and the ability to understand will be carried out through tests that provide for the solution of technical-scientific problems through written and/or oral tests, laboratory experiences, and the preparation and discussion of reports on experiments carried out.
III - Autonomy of judgment: Acquisition of conscious autonomy in areas related to the management of projects, the responsibility of structures and personnel, the identification of innovative development perspectives and strategies, and the evaluation, interpretation, and re-elaboration of literature data, professional ethics, and a critical and responsible approach, even towards bioethical issues.
Learning methodology: Autonomy of judgment is developed in particular through exercises, seminars organized within the courses of the characterizing and related integrative disciplines, in which emphasis is placed on acquiring mastery in the management of experiences and data obtained and on the occasion of the activity assigned by the teacher for the preparation of the final test.
Verification of learning: The verification of the acquisition of autonomy of judgment takes place through the evaluation of the degree of autonomy and the ability to work, even in a group, during the ongoing activity and the final test.
IV - Communication skills: Acquisition of adequate skills and tools for communication, with particular regard to fluent practice in a language of the EU, with specific attention to disciplinary vocabulary, the preparation/presentation of research projects, the guidance of research groups, and the illustration of research results.
Learning methodology: Written and oral communication skills will be developed in seminars, exercises, and training activities that also include the preparation of written reports and documents and the oral presentation of the same.
Verification of learning: examination tests and presentation of the degree thesis.
V - Learning ability: Acquisition of skills that promote the development and deepening of skills, with particular reference to the consultation of specialized databases, the adoption of innovative technologies, and the use of advanced knowledge tools for the continuous updating of knowledge.
Learning methodology: Learning skills are acquired in the study path as a whole, with particular regard to the individual study provided, the preparation of individual projects, and the activity carried out for the preparation of the final test.
Verification of learning: These skills will be verified by passing the relevant profit exams. In particular, the demonstration of having fully acquired the required learning skills will be required for the successful completion of the final test.
Function in a work context:
Function in a work context:
The main skills of the Master's Degree in Biology in the field of Health and Nutrition concern:
- basic or applied research activities in the biomedical sectors in public or private research institutions;
- autonomous professional activities in the fields of nutrition and food safety in the health, public administration, and industry sectors;
- planning of nutritional interventions for individuals and populations;
- promotion and scientific and technological innovation in the field of genetics and biological-molecular biology, in cell biology and technology, in metabolic and nutritional assessments, in the analysis and development of biomolecules for biomedical and industrial applications;
- research and marketing activities in the pharmaceutical industry (applied research, drug-clinical research, data control and management) and in the biomedical equipment industry;
- professional activity in public and private laboratories for biological, microbiological, sero-immunological, genetic, pharmacological-toxicological, biochemical, and cytological analyses, and for the identification of infectious pathogens and the control and activity of antibiotics, hormones, sera, and vaccines;
- design the development of biological and biochemical applications in the health field;
- educational and divulgation activities related to neuroscience.
Skills associated with the function:
Skills associated with the function:
After registration in the Register of Biologists, Section A, the graduate may carry out the activities listed in the Main functions of the professional figure and the list of skills associated with the function with the professional title of biologist.
Professional status conferred by the degree:
Professional opportunities:
The course prepares for the profession of biologist, biochemist, pharmacologist, bacteriologist, and related professions, food biotechnologist, researcher, graduate technician, and related professions.

INFORMATION ON STUDY PLANS AND COURSES General information relating to the current academic year.
