Admission requirements:
Required qualifications: [TSS].
High school diploma: [L2].
Fees and contributions: For information on fees and amounts, please consult the page: https://www.univaq.it/section.php?id=55
Dates and deadlines: Online registration: 18/07/2024 - 20/12/2024.
Deadline for submitting self-certification: 17/07/2024 - 20/12/2024.
Deadline for choosing the course online: 18/07/2024 - 19/07/2024.
Roles: Study plan approval manager: ANGELO ANTONIO D'ARCHIVIO, President: ANGELO ANTONIO D'ARCHIVIO.
Program, texts and objectives: Official language(s) of teaching and assessment: ITALIAN.
Degree awarded: Master's Degree in CHEMICAL SCIENCES.
Specific learning objectives: The Master's Degree in Chemical Sciences aims to integrate and strengthen the basic skills acquired in the first cycle in the various fields of chemistry in order to provide students with advanced training for carrying out activities aimed at scientific and technological innovation in the chemical field. The degree course also offers the possibility of acquiring specialized skills in specific areas of chemistry.
In addition to the general training objectives of the class, the areas of specialization of the Master's Degree in Chemical Sciences, which will correspond to specific orientations or alternative curricula within the graduate's training program, aim to:
- provide advanced skills for understanding and predicting the reactivity of molecules and for designing complex syntheses. In this context, students will consolidate their skills in reaction mechanisms in order to develop the ability to understand, design and carry out syntheses of organic, inorganic and organometallic molecules. Particular emphasis will be given to the role of catalysis as an essential tool for preparing high value-added compounds, taking into account the economic efficiency and environmental sustainability of the synthetic processes.
- provide advanced skills that enable the Master's graduate to identify and apply the most suitable computational and experimental methods for the characterization of a chemical system or for the solution of problems arising from the various sectors of research and industry. In this context, specialists will be provided with advanced skills in modern instrumental techniques and at the same time the ability to critically evaluate the quality parameters of experimental data as a function of the nature of the problem. It will also be essential to have the ability to process the data by means of statistical treatments, in order to identify and represent the information contained in them, and to apply computational methods that can support the experiments.
The proposed curriculum includes core courses in basic chemical disciplines (Physical Chemistry, Inorganic Chemistry, Organic Chemistry, Analytical Chemistry) and in Industrial Chemistry, which aim to complete the basic training acquired with the Bachelor's degree and to introduce the most advanced specialized knowledge, and courses that allow the student to receive training relevant to the chosen path.
The core courses common to all the proposed specialist courses, for the most part concentrated in the first year of the course, will allow the student to:
- acquire advanced knowledge in the field of coordination compound chemistry.
- consolidate knowledge on the properties, mechanisms and syntheses of organic compounds, as well as their structural characterization by means of advanced spectroscopic techniques.
- acquire solid skills in quantum mechanical calculation methods and advanced chemical-physical investigation techniques.
- know the criteria for establishing the quality of analytical data and the procedures for the development, validation and optimization of analytical methods.
- enrich knowledge related to the reactions and processes of organic and inorganic chemistry of industrial interest. The differentiation of the proposed courses will take place from the second semester of the first year through the introduction of some courses considered specific for a certain area of specialization. The student will be able to further personalize their training by choosing some courses from a list of advanced courses considered consistent with the specificities of the chosen path or capable of providing transversal skills to the different paths.
The student will be able to opt for a specific area of specialization by selecting, with the presentation of the study plan, one of the proposed courses and the optional courses for that course.
The Master's Degree in Chemical Sciences also includes a period of practical training to be carried out within the University, at Companies or Public Research Bodies in the national or foreign territory, within the scope of specific agreements, as an integral part of the training program.
Ample space is devoted to the preparation of the thesis, which completes the training, in which the student, by addressing an original research topic, learns to use the theoretical knowledge acquired and consolidates his experimental and/or computational skills, as well as consolidates his ability to present and discuss a scientific problem both in written and oral form.
Depending on the chosen path, while maintaining the general training objectives of the class, the Master's graduate will have acquired specialized skills that will enable him to design and study a new chemical reaction and optimize the synthesis of new compounds and materials. Students will develop the ability to design and carry out syntheses of organic, inorganic and organometallic molecules for the most varied types of applications, prioritizing processes that meet the criteria of efficiency and environmental sustainability imposed by social sensitivity and current international regulations. Students will also acquire the necessary theoretical/mechanistic basis for the rationalization of synthetic studies and will be able to apply advanced methods for structural characterization.
The Master's graduate will be able to develop new analytical methods and make decisions regarding the most suitable sampling and analysis methods for the characterization of complex systems. In this context, the student will be able to identify and apply the most suitable technologies for the analysis of quality and process control in various fields (clinical, toxicological, food and environmental). These skills will allow the new graduate to easily enter the world of work related to certification and quality analysis issues.
The Master's graduate will have the skills to develop and validate statistical and computational models that can support experimental methods in the characterization of chemical systems of interest. To this end, the student will become familiar with the use of computational techniques aimed at solving structural and mechanistic problems, and with the statistical approach for the treatment of data and for the optimization of processes. He will also be able to use mathematical and computer tools for the processing of matrices obtained through the combination of experimental data and simulated quantities in the study of structure-property relationships.
Dublin descriptors: I - Knowledge and understanding The graduate must have acquired in-depth knowledge in the various fields of inorganic chemistry, physical chemistry, organic chemistry, analytical chemistry and industrial chemistry and familiarity with the main methodologies and instrumental techniques for analysis and synthesis for structural characterization and the definition of structure-property relationships necessary for the understanding of phenomena at the molecular level. He must also know the fundamental computational approaches to the problems related to chemistry. Depending on the chosen path, the graduate will be able to consolidate his skills in a specific area of specialization. In particular, he will be able to acquire advanced knowledge in the field of organic and inorganic synthesis, emphasizing the mechanistic aspects that regulate the processes and the role of catalysis. He will be able to consolidate knowledge in the application of analytical chemistry methods for the study of systems of biological, environmental, food and quality control interest. He will be able to acquire advanced knowledge in the field of statistical treatment of data matrices in order to extract useful information and in the simulation of atomic and molecular properties.
In order to achieve the aforementioned training objectives, the course of study provides a solid multidisciplinary training through the provision of common courses, while the acquisition of specialized knowledge is left to the courses that characterize the chosen path. An intense laboratory teaching activity is planned, aimed at knowledge of the modern instrumentation for measuring the properties of chemical compounds and/or materials and the techniques for structural determination, the approaches for the preparation and purification of compounds and materials of scientific and technological interest, as well as the methods for the statistical processing of chemical data and for the simulation of experimental quantities.
The method of verifying the acquisition of knowledge and understanding skills, defined by each teacher, may consist of passing oral exams, in-progress tests, or the evaluation of short reports on the practice carried out in the design and execution of laboratory experiments. In addition, the thesis committee will evaluate the written report in which the student describes and discusses the thesis work and his oral presentation.
II - Ability to apply knowledge and understanding Regardless of the chosen training path, the graduate must be able to apply his knowledge in the various fields of chemistry, demonstrating mastery of the scientific method of investigation and skills both to devise and support arguments and to solve chemical problems even in interdisciplinary contexts. He must be able to work correctly in the laboratory, with autonomy and decision-making ability, addressing and solving problems in the various fields of chemistry, making informed decisions and drawing conclusions based on the data and information available. Depending on the area of specialization chosen in the training path, the graduate will be able to acquire the ability to carry out in the laboratory synthetic processes described in the literature but also to design and carry out new syntheses with the aim of obtaining products or materials with specific functions, he will be able to apply certified analytical methods or develop and validate new methods in the field of quality control of processes or materials, he will be able to use computational or chemometric methods with competence for the simulation or processing of chemical data in specific scientific problems. In order to develop the ability to apply the acquired knowledge, the course of study emphasizes the role of laboratory activities, planned for many courses, and provides for a mandatory practical training in the second year which can be carried out in a university laboratory or in companies or external bodies within the scope of specific agreements. An important training role in this context is represented by the preparation of the thesis, in which the student is called to carry out an individual research activity under the guidance of one or more teachers in a university or extra-university laboratory.
The verification of the achievement of the objectives in terms of ability to apply knowledge and understanding is left to the passing of profit exams, the outcome of laboratory reports, the evaluation of the mandatory practical training and the final evaluation of the thesis.
III - Autonomy of judgment Graduates must have acquired high critical thinking skills and must be able to carry out scientific research independently in the chosen field, identifying the most appropriate methods to address problems in the field of chemistry. They must be able to design and conduct experiments, interpret the results and devise the subsequent development of the experimentation in order to acquire knowledge and/or optimize methods or processes in a context of scientific and applied research. They must also be able to use appropriate bibliographic sources and electronic archives available on the web. Based on the specialized training provided by the chosen path, the graduate must be able to evaluate the most suitable choices for carrying out the synthesis of old and new materials or substances, taking into account the environmental and economic sustainability of the process, and the toxicity of reagents, solvents and catalysts. In the context of the application of analytical methods for the quality control of materials and processes, the graduate must be able to evaluate the most appropriate analytical approach to meet the requirements set out in the current legislation in terms of quality requirements of the system being analyzed and present the results in an appropriate form. The graduate must be able to identify the most suitable and effective statistical or computational approaches in order to obtain useful information from chemical systems of interest, reducing the use of human and instrumental resources in the laboratory.
IV - Communication skills The graduate in Chemical Sciences must be able to communicate, in a clear and unambiguous way, information, scientific data and conclusions to specialist and non-specialist interlocutors, also through the preparation of written reports, presenting the experimental data in the form of diagrams, tables and graphs, also using the English language and the computer tools necessary for the presentation. He must be able to work in a group, to operate with a high degree of autonomy and to quickly integrate into working environments. Within the possible specializations provided for in the course of study, the graduate will have the opportunity to acquire specific languages and methods of presentation of the results. These specificities include the description of the stages, mechanisms and conditions of the synthesis processes, the presentation of the quality parameters of the analytical methods, the representation of the results of multivariate statistical treatments and of simulations of atomic-molecular properties. These objectives are achieved through laboratory training activities and the preparation of the written and oral presentation of the final test.
V - Learning ability Graduates must have developed the learning ability that will enable them to update themselves effectively in all areas of chemistry and its applications. They must therefore be able to effectively integrate the knowledge acquired by identifying textbooks, reference scientific literature and other useful materials for in-depth study. They must also be able to read and learn in English. The development of general learning skills, integrated with specialized training, must put the graduate in a position to continuously update knowledge in the areas of specialization. In particular, he must take into account the continuous technological innovations in organic and inorganic synthesis, the evolution of instrumentation and analytical methods for quality control and the development or implementation of computer tools for statistical and computational analysis.
The ability to learn is monitored during the course of study through profit checks and examination tests that focus on the notions to be acquired through independent study.
Function in a work context:
Function in a work context:
The contents of the master's degree course provide the necessary training to be able to practice the profession of chemist independently (free profession with registration in the Register of Chemists - Section A, after passing the State Exam) or to be able to access research institutions, public administrations, professional companies and consulting firms, national or international, companies, industries and research laboratories, analysis, quality control and certification and work environments that require in-depth knowledge in the fields of synthesis and characterization of new products and materials, health, food, cosmetics.
Among the activities that master's graduates can carry out, the following are particularly noteworthy: activities to promote and develop scientific and technological innovation, as well as the management and design of technologies, and the exercise of functions of high responsibility in the sectors of industry, the environment, health, cultural heritage and public administration.
The Master's Degree in Chemical Sciences is a qualification for access to the Doctoral School in the area.
Skills associated with the function:
Skills associated with the function:
The Master's graduate can carry out highly specialized professional activities in the industrial sector, in public and private research laboratories, in the fields of synthesis and characterization of new materials, health, environment, energy, safety, food, cultural heritage. He is able to work with a high degree of autonomy, assuming responsibility for projects and structures, using the knowledge acquired in the field of chemistry and materials and applying the disciplinary investigation methods acquired independently. Graduates will be able to carry out activities to promote and develop scientific and technological innovation, management and design of technologies. The Master's Degree course allows access to third-level courses, such as Doctoral Schools and Second-level Master's degrees in the chemical field and in other related scientific fields or concerning interdisciplinary issues, as well as specialization courses for teaching in secondary schools.
Professional status conferred by the degree:
Employment opportunities:
The employment opportunities for the master's graduate are offered by:
- Universities, research institutions, agencies such as ARPA, ANPAT, Ministries, Civil Protection;
- Industrial and applied research centers, industrial production, certification companies, quality control;
- Scientific dissemination agencies.

Program, texts and objectives: Official language(s) of teaching and assessment: ENGLISH.
Degree awarded: Master's Degree in Physics.
Specific learning objectives: The educational objective of the Master's degree program is to train a physicist with a solid basic education and adequate specialist training in one of the current fields of physics through a specific curriculum, in line with the objectives of Class LM-17.
The specific learning objectives to be achieved are: a) mastery of the scientific method obtained through solid cultural training in classical and modern physics and its theoretical, experimental and applied aspects present in the Department;
b) in-depth knowledge of modern physics and the specific knowledge corresponding to the chosen educational path;
c) in-depth knowledge of modern instrumentation and experimental techniques, data collection and analysis procedures, and formulation and solution of models, also through numerical simulation;
d) ability to use the acquired knowledge for the use and design of sophisticated measuring instruments or for the modeling of complex systems in the various fields of Physics present in the Department, but also in areas other than the scientific one;
e) fluent use of the English language, in written and spoken form, with reference also to disciplinary and technical vocabulary.
To achieve these objectives, the educational path provides for the completion of basic training through a set of common mandatory courses in characterizing disciplines, mainly taught in the first year of the course, supplemented by thematic laboratory courses. Specific training in areas of specialization is mainly provided in the second year of the course through various curricula and the completion of the master's thesis. The areas of specialization are related to the thematic areas of research present in the Department.
The course of study, delivered in English and therefore accessible to Italian and international students on the basis of international agreements, reflects the nature of current cutting-edge scientific research and aims to provide students with skills useful for working in an international context.
External internships are planned at companies and research laboratories, or internal internships at research groups, as preparation for the degree thesis and subsequent entry into the world of work.
Dublin descriptors: I - Knowledge and understanding: The educational path offered makes it possible to consolidate knowledge of modern physics, including Quantum Mechanics applied to the Physics of Matter and Nuclear Physics, Quantum Electrodynamics and the Physics of Atmospheric fluids and Space plasmas, as well as knowledge of cutting-edge topics in the chosen field.
The degree course includes characterizing courses for over 45 CFU, which include advanced experimental/laboratory/computational techniques, in addition to advanced theoretical topics and their application in diversified contexts.
In particular, at the end of the educational path, the Master's Degree in Physics will obtain:
Knowledge:
- excellent knowledge and understanding of the theoretical/mathematical formalisms in the field of quantum physics, including relativistic physics, statistical physics and their implications in the various sectors of physics.
- in-depth knowledge of the physical principles of the main experimental investigation techniques and methodologies and the resulting data collection and analysis with applications relating to the most recent methodologies adopted in the various contexts.
- knowledge of cutting-edge research topics with applications to specific research sectors.
- knowledge of frontier topics in related sectors chosen by the student.
- knowledge of numerical calculation techniques for data processing and simulation of complex physical systems.
Skills:
- ability to understand complex physical-mathematical formalisms in various sectors.
- ability to understand scientific articles and specialist scientific literature.
- ability to understand mathematical models applicable to real physical problems.
- ability to understand and recognize the laws that govern the dynamics of physical phenomena in different sectors through interdisciplinarity.
- ability to understand the physical mechanisms underlying the most advanced experimental measurement techniques.
Learning methods: Dedicated courses (characterizing and related and supplementary), dedicated seminar activities, internal internship or external internships, group work (team work), final thesis work.
Verification methods: Individual exams with a final written and oral test.
Any intermediate tests for partial evaluation or feedback.
All courses in the educational path include a final exam with a final written and/or oral test. In laboratory courses, the student is guided in activities that involve the autonomous setting up of experimental apparatus, the acquisition, analysis and processing of data, both experimental and obtained from numerical simulations. In some courses, typically in laboratory and/or specialist courses in the second year, the final exam can be taken by presenting a project carried out by the student with a related discussion.
II - Ability to apply knowledge and understanding: At the end of the educational path, the Master's Degree in Physics will have acquired the following skills:
- ability to apply the acquired knowledge in different contexts and to perceive the interdisciplinary value of the learned theories and experimental methodologies.
- ability to set up an experimental apparatus to carry out measurements usable in the field of scientific research.
- ability to apply the acquired knowledge to cutting-edge research in their own field and in other fields.
- ability to apply the acquired knowledge to cutting-edge research.
- ability to apply, develop and design advanced calculation techniques.
- ability to schematize a physical system in a mathematical model.
- ability to solve complex problems by solving analytical and/or numerical equations and optimization techniques.
- ability to communicate their results and reasoning clearly and exhaustively to experts in the field and to non-experts, in written and oral form.
- ability to transfer their physical-scientific knowledge to others.
- ability and flexibility to apply the tools of reasoning and the scientific method in any other area.
Learning method: The block of common courses of about 40 CFU provides an adequate transversal and interdisciplinary perspective for the application of knowledge; in most of the courses, theoretical lessons are accompanied by exercises in the classroom or left to individual work; the projects carried out in the more advanced courses provide an opportunity to learn methodologies for carrying out and presenting scientific work; the preparation of the thesis and the final test consolidate these skills in a medium-term project; the laboratory courses provide the necessary knowledge to design and use a measuring apparatus suitable for solving the problem under consideration; external internships provide the opportunity to apply the acquired skills in contexts outside the university (research laboratories and/or high-tech industries).
Verification method: All verification tests involve the application of knowledge to problems not previously addressed and allow the stimulation of initiative and the evaluation of the student's autonomous work.
III - Autonomy of judgment: The study of the scientific method applied to the physical world develops the autonomy of judgment in the Master's Degree graduate, in particular with regard to:
- formulating a critical reasoning.
- critically analyzing a physical phenomenon in the light of the data/evidence collected.
- critically comparing their theoretical and/or numerical results and/or experimental results with those available in the relevant scientific literature, obtained from databases and bibliographic research.
- conducting a critical and motivated analysis.
Learning methods: These skills are acquired through the analysis and interpretation of experimental data, their critical comparison with theoretical results and models, under the supervision of the teachers involved in the scientific research activities relevant to the proposed areas.
In the specialist courses, students are continuously encouraged to delve into different texts and original scientific articles.
Verification methods: The evaluation of these skills is carried out with tests in progress and final tests within the proposed courses and in the final test.
IV - Communication skills: At the end of the educational path, Master's Degree graduates in Physics will have acquired the following skills:
- ability to conduct a scientific discussion by providing relevant and pertinent scientific arguments in support.
- ability to use computer tools to present a scientific topic and to conduct a scientific discussion in the presence of experts, based on valid, convincing and relevant arguments.
- ability to present the results of their research to an expert and non-expert audience, choosing the right language and presenting the most appropriate aspects in both cases.
Learning methods: Training activities that involve the presentation of physics topics (essays and seminars within the various courses), in English, culminating in the presentation relating to the final test.
Verification methods: Evaluation of the expository ability, of motivating their scientific conclusions and of conducting a scientific debate during the oral examination tests and in the presentation of the thesis, all carried out in the presence of a commission of teachers.
V - Learning ability: During the educational path, students acquire advanced skills in autonomous learning in Italian and English, being encouraged to carry out bibliographic research (texts and scientific articles in English) and to select the material of interest, comparing and critically evaluating the different sources.
The graduates are also able to build complex reasoning and modify standard demonstrations to adapt them to new situations that may also arise in non-strictly scientific areas.
The graduates finally acquire an understanding of the limits of their knowledge and the ability to identify textbooks, sources and scientific articles relevant and useful for further study.
This path provides them with the ability to independently undertake further studies (doctorate and second-level masters in physics and technical/scientific disciplines) and to make the best use of training opportunities in any technical/industrial work environment.
Learning methods: Students progressively acquire these skills in the specialist courses and in the work of preparing for the degree thesis.
Verification methods: The topics covered in the various courses are proposed for independent study and evaluated during the examination or during intermediate verification.
Function in a work context:
Function in a work context:
The Master's Degree graduate in Physics is able to operate with a high degree of autonomy, also assuming responsibility for projects and structures, in public and private research contexts, nationally and internationally, and in public and private companies operating in technologically advanced sectors.
The solid scientific training, familiarity with mathematical models, computer tools and experimental apparatus, allows physicists to access design and analysis functions in a wide spectrum of work applications, even if not directly related to physics, and to interact constructively with other professional figures such as engineers, managers and specialists in information technology.
The Master's Degree graduate in Physics can participate in and/or coordinate research and development activities in the technological field, for example by designing sophisticated measuring instruments and/or activities for modeling complex physical systems, can carry out activities for the promotion and development of scientific and technological innovation, can carry out activities for the management and design of technologies, and can exercise functions of high responsibility in the sectors of industry, environment, health, cultural heritage and public administration.
He/she can assume the role of technologist, project leader for development and research activities, laboratory technician, developer of scientific and industrial software, manager of computing centers.
The physicist can carry out managerial and/or expert functions in the Regional Agencies for Environmental Protection (ARPA) and in industrial research laboratories. The physicist can also carry out design and analysis functions in computational activities that require knowledge of mathematical models and in the area of programming and information and communication technologies.
Skills associated with the function:
Skills associated with the function:
The skills acquired by the Master's Degree graduate in Physics, both theoretical and experimental, are broad and generally develop flexibility of reasoning and the ability to adapt the scientific methodology to a wide range of work needs, including:
- skills in all aspects of classical and modern physics with a strong propensity for in-depth study.
- ability to use the scientific method.
- ability to coordinate working groups in the field of scientific research.
- ability to use complex measuring apparatus and interface them with computers for the optimization and automation of measurements.
- ability to communicate effectively on scientific topics, also in English.
In addition, the Master's Degree graduate can acquire, depending on the chosen path and the specific thesis work, interdisciplinary skills in electronics, applied mathematics, data analysis and numerical calculation that can be used in various work contexts.
Professional status conferred by the degree:
Employment opportunities:
The Master's Degree in Physics is the main training channel for a physicist to exercise a highly specialized scientific profession with ample employment opportunities in the public sector (education and research centers, national and international laboratories, institutes and agencies in the scientific field) and in the private sector (companies in the technology, microelectronics, software, nanotechnology, energy and finance sectors).
The Master's Degree physicist is able to work with a high degree of autonomy, assuming responsibility for projects and structures, using the specific skills acquired for the modeling of complex systems in the fields of basic and applied sciences; therefore, he/she can hold positions with high qualifications in the scientific/technological area.
The Master's Degree in Physics is also the basis for a career oriented towards specialized professions in education and research and is a prerequisite for access to the doctoral program in the area.

INFORMATION ON STUDY PLANS AND COURSES General information relating to the current academic year.

Website: https://www.disim.univaq.it/degree.php?section=iscritti.

Dates and deadlines: Online registration: 18/07/2024 - 20/12/2024.

Roles: Study plan approval manager: GIUSEPPE DELLA PENNA.
President: HENRY MUCCINI.
Program, texts and objectives: Official language(s) of teaching and assessment.
ENGLISH.
Degree awarded: Master's Degree in COMPUTER SCIENCE.
Specific learning objectives: The Master's Degree in Computer Science is characterized by significant independent project work by students, in order to develop their judgment and problem-solving skills.
The skills provided by the Degree Course mainly concern distributed systems and mobile applications, computer networks, advanced algorithms, artificial intelligence, and the analysis and development of complex software systems. Through a constant analysis, the Course aims to incorporate but also anticipate the prevailing needs of the market. The Degree Course intends to introduce students to the most advanced and cutting-edge themes of Computer Science, both of a scientific and applicative nature. According to the vision of the Course, the Master's Degree in Computer Science is a candidate to be a protagonist of technological innovation in the international arena.
In practical terms, the Course aims to provide in-depth theoretical, methodological and professional skills in the relevant areas of computer science: the graduate will be able to design, analyze, specify, develop, verify and maintain software systems, configure and manage network services and telematic systems, and develop and manage complex information processing systems.
The Course of Study pays particular attention to the importance of internationalization, and to this end all mandatory courses, in all the planned curricula, are taught in English. It is also planned that, for interested and deserving students, there is the possibility of attending one of the two years of the course at foreign Universities in place of the courses offered by our campus, as part of specific agreements with foreign universities. These students will be able to obtain, upon completion of the training course, the foreign degree in addition to the one issued by our University. The list of affiliated universities and the calls for applications regulating access to the mobility program and the selection methods will be published each year in the Course Offer and/or in the Study Plan, which can be consulted on the website of the Degree Course.
In particular, the planned paths are:
- Standard, to be carried out entirely at the L'Aquila campus;
- International Double Degree in consortium with the University of Nice (France), called UBIDIS;
- International Double Degree in consortium with the Universities of Malardalen (Sweden) and VU-Amsterdam (Netherlands), called GSEEM.
Excellence paths are also being designed and implemented, also in collaboration with the Gran Sasso Science Institute http://www.gssi.infn.it/index.php/it/.
In relation to the quality of the training process, it should be noted that the Degree Course has the "GRIN Seal".
The GRIN Seal, awarded every year since 2004 in collaboration between GRIN (Informatics Group - the association of university professors of informatics) and AICA (Italian Association for Informatics and Automatic Calculation), certifies the quality of the contents of three-year and master's degree courses in informatics (classes L-31 and LM-18). The results of the quality certification process are available online at http://grin.informatica.uniroma2.it/certificazione. This certification is based on a set of criteria that define how much and what kind of computer science is taught, how much mathematics of areas relevant to computer science is taught, and how many full-time computer science professors are present. The details of the certification rules are available at the URL http://www.grin-informatica.it/opencms/export/sites/default/grin/files/RegoleCertificazione2012.pdf.
Dublin descriptors: I - Knowledge and understanding Graduates must have in-depth knowledge and understanding of the essential mathematical and computer science concepts for the analysis and design of complex computer systems. This knowledge includes advanced algorithms and data structures, formal methods and verification of complex software systems, design and optimization of networks, telematic systems and applications, artificial intelligence, advanced software engineering and web engineering.
Graduates must also have in-depth knowledge of computer science and related fields and methodologies, from the fundamental to the most innovative and advanced.
Starting from this knowledge, the graduate must be able to independently understand the principles and solutions relating to complex computer applications and technologies, even if not considered during the course of study because they are characterized by recent developments or related to specific contexts.
In summary, graduates must have:
- knowledge and understanding of the advanced mathematical and computer science concepts underlying complex computer systems;
- in-depth knowledge of computer science and a systematic understanding of related aspects and key concepts;
- the ability to independently understand and influence the latest developments in the sector and innovative and specific applications.
In each of the planned curricula, these objectives are achieved through the use of dedicated courses (characterizing, related and complementary) for a total of over 80 CFU.
II - Ability to apply knowledge and understanding Graduates must be able to apply their knowledge and understanding to the analysis and development of advanced computer and telematic systems and solutions.
In particular, they must be able to analyze complex computer problems, evaluate the corresponding solutions and propose new ones suitable for their level of knowledge and understanding, and which may involve interdisciplinarity and interventions outside their field of specialization. The analysis involves the identification of the problem, a clear definition of the specifications, the examination of possible solution methods, the choice of the most appropriate methodologies and technologies and their correct application.
Graduates must be able to use a variety of methods, including mathematical analysis, computational modeling or practical experimentation, in order to design and implement complex computer solutions, both working independently and directing or collaborating with graduates and computer and non-computer professionals.
In summary, graduates must have:
- the ability to apply their knowledge and understanding to identify, formulate and solve complex computer problems using classical or advanced methods;
- the ability to apply their knowledge and understanding to analyze computer products, processes and methods, even if highly complex;
- the ability to apply their knowledge and understanding to the development and implementation of complex solutions and advanced projects that meet defined or partially specified requirements;
- an understanding of design methodologies and the ability to use them.
These objectives are achieved both through dedicated courses and through a consistent set of advanced courses, which allow to put into practice the knowledge acquired and which provide for the realization of projects both on an autonomous basis and through participation in working groups.
III - Autonomy of judgment Graduates must have acquired a high capacity for critical thinking, for identifying the most appropriate methods for analyzing and solving complex computer problems and for designing advanced systems, for understanding the limits of their knowledge and for independently undertaking investigations appropriate to their level of knowledge and understanding. These investigations may involve bibliographic, regulatory and database research. They may also involve the design and conduct of experiments, the interpretation of data and computer simulation, and, where necessary, the development of original theoretical and practical solutions, even extending the frontier of knowledge acquired in the reference areas.
With regard to the computer science profession, graduates must be able to apply their knowledge and understanding to develop theoretical-practical skills to solve problems, conduct investigations and implement complex computer solutions, even by coordinating and directing different working groups. These skills may include knowledge, the use and awareness of advanced hardware and software processes and equipment, experimentation, the use of scientific and technical literature and other sources of information.
Graduates must also be able to recognize the broader and non-technical implications of computer practice, of an ethical, commercial and industrial nature.
In summary, graduates must have:
- the ability to use appropriate methods to conduct theoretical and applied research or other articulated investigations on appropriate technical topics, using references to scientific and technical literature, regulations, databases and other sources of information;
- the ability to direct working groups for the purpose of carrying out complex computer projects;
- the ability to design and conduct appropriate experiments, interpret data and draw conclusions;
- the ability to choose and use appropriate equipment, tools and methods, combining theoretical and practical aspects;
- an understanding of the applicable techniques and methods and their limitations;
- an awareness of the non-technical implications of computer practice.
In addition to dedicated courses and project activities, these objectives are also achieved through internships and direct involvement in working contexts and through the training activities related to the final exam.
IV - Communication skills Graduates must:
- be able to operate effectively individually, as part of a group and as coordinators or managers of groups;
- be able to use methods to communicate effectively with the computer science community and in general with society;
- have the necessary skills to integrate and organize activities within collaborative projects;
- have the necessary skills to acquire the requirements of the problem through interaction with clients, to transfer the specific knowledge acquired to their collaborators and to present and communicate the results effectively;
- be able to use effectively, in addition to Italian, the English language both in the technical-scientific field and for the exchange of general information.
These objectives are achieved through training activities that involve group work, the preparation of project reports in English, and finally through the preparation of the written and oral presentation of the final exam.
V - Learning ability Graduates must have acquired the ability to study scientific subjects, even in relation to different and advanced contexts, in order to effectively integrate the knowledge received. They must also be able to understand the limits of their knowledge and have the ability to identify the reference scientific literature, textbooks, other sources and useful material for in-depth study. These skills must allow the graduate to effectively undertake higher-level training courses, such as doctoral or second-level master's degrees, and managerial careers that require a high degree of autonomy and updating skills.
They must also have the ability to read and learn in English.
The ability to learn is constantly monitored during the course of study through progress checks and exams that focus on the knowledge to be acquired, especially through independent study.
English is learned in specific courses and through the progressive use of the foreign language in learning.
Function in a work context.
Functions in a work context:
Computer specialist. Programmer: knowledge of the main algorithmic methods and programming languages also for advanced and innovative applications, including network applications, mobile applications and applications involving artificial intelligence. Web programmer: knowledge of the main languages for Internet and mobile applications. System administrator: knowledge of the main operating systems, their applications and possible developments.
Network designer: knowledge of the main systems, protocols and network applications.
Software project and coordinator: knowledge of the most advanced elements and methods of Software Engineering. Database designer and manager: knowledge of the main formalisms and languages for the definition and use of databases, knowledge of possible future developments. Database administrator: knowledge of the main DBMS. Training technician: general knowledge acquired in the master's degree. Marketing assistant: knowledge of the main computer systems and their industrial and commercial applicability.
Researcher: advanced knowledge acquired in the master's degree in the basic and applied context.
Entrepreneur (especially in relation to innovative start-ups): ability to apply their skills in an innovative way to create and market new applications.
Skills associated with the function.
Skills associated with the function:
Computer specialist. Computer science and information technologies are now pervasive and widely applied in almost all fields. In the future, the prospect is for a further expansion of the domains and modes of application. Consequently, the Master's Degree in Computer Science will be able to find a job both in companies and organizations that develop new computer applications, and in those that simply apply and manage them.
In general, the employment and professional areas of reference for graduates of the class are those of the design, organization, implementation, management and maintenance of computer systems (with specific regard to the areas of advanced application, new theoretical and technological developments with attention to the requirements of reliability, performance and security and, today, also of Ethics of Informatics).
Graduates are prepared both to work in companies that produce computer systems, networks and mobile applications, and in companies, public administrations and, more generally, in all organizations that use computer systems.
Master's graduates in Computer Science will be able to access coordination and managerial functions, and roles related to basic and applied research in both industrial and research institutions.
They may also find employment in teaching in training institutions.
Furthermore, the international GSEEM and UBIDIS paths provide specific skills in advanced fields, which can be used both in Italy and abroad.
Professional status conferred by the degree.
Job opportunities:
Computer specialist. Employee of a private computer or ICT (Information and Communication Technology) company or other sectors in which computer science finds its application (i.e. virtually all sectors of work). Employee of a public administration with the role of developing or managing computer systems. Entrepreneur in the computer or ICT field or in fields in which these disciplines play a relevant role.
ICT consultant. Teacher or researcher in training institutions or public or private research centers.

Program, texts and objectives: Official language(s) of teaching and assessment.
ITALIAN.
Degree awarded: Master's Degree in ENVIRONMENTAL BIOLOGY AND ECOSYSTEM MANAGEMENT.
Specific learning objectives:
The Master's Degree Course in Environmental Biology and Ecosystem Management aims to train environmental biologists and environmental experts with advanced training in the field of environmental analysis, management, assessment and restoration, both in undisturbed conditions and in conditions altered by specific anthropogenic activities, climate change or unusual natural events. The educational objectives of the course consist of acquiring: advanced levels of knowledge of the biotic and abiotic components of ecosystems as a tool for correct integrated analysis of the ecosystems themselves; ability to collect experimental data in the field and in the laboratory, with a critical approach and interpretative skills; ability to analyze data using statistical methods with the support of mathematical and computer tools, and ability to critically interpret the results; principles, methods and tools for assessing resources and environmental impacts, in compliance with current national and Community legislation; knowledge relating to the mitigation and compensation of anthropogenic impacts on biodiversity and the rehabilitation of habitats; autonomy in the implementation of new conceptual models and methodological protocols for field and laboratory investigations; ability to hold positions of responsibility in the management activities related to nature conservation and environmental quality control at national and international level; mastery of written and oral English, as well as Italian, with reference also to the disciplinary lexicons specific to the professional figures operating in the environmental sector; preparation of a high profile for access to Research Doctorate Schools and Second Level Master's Degrees. The course of study provides for the possibility of choosing between two training paths. The first is mainly oriented towards the analysis of the various biological components of terrestrial ecosystems, including wetlands and inland waters. It is distinguished by the presence of a higher proportion of courses that deal with ecology and biomonitoring, even in sensitive habitats, and the effects of environmental impacts at different levels of biological organization. The second path is more oriented towards the analysis of phenomena at a more global ecosystem level and the management of the territory with a view to conservation and environmental restoration. It is distinguished by the presence of courses that deal with environmental botany, environmental assessment techniques, forecasting tools, territorial planning tools, bioremediation, and solid waste treatment. The two curricula provide for common courses relating to the physics and chemistry of the environment, earth sciences, the ecology of particular biocenoses, responses to environmental stresses, methods of biological conservation, and environmental economics.
Dublin Descriptors: I - Knowledge and understanding. The Master's graduate knows and/or is able to understand: the field and laboratory tools and procedures for the detection and monitoring of the biotic and abiotic components of natural and anthropized ecosystems; the mathematical-statistical and computer tools for the analysis of environmental data; the results of these analyses, which he/she is able to interpret critically; the tools and techniques for environmental assessment and territorial planning applied in compliance with current legislation; the effects of the different modes of management of natural resources; the English language, as well as Italian, with reference also to the disciplinary lexicons specific to the different professional figures operating in the environmental sector. The results indicated will be achieved through the courses present in the table of training activities that deal with the physics and chemistry of the environment, earth sciences, the applied aspects of biological disciplines and ecology, the methods of representation, analysis and modeling of environmental data, the techniques of environmental assessment and territorial planning. The verification of knowledge and understanding is carried out through profit exams and tests in progress and during field activities, laboratory exercises and internship activities.
II - Ability to apply knowledge and understanding. The Master's graduate is able to apply knowledge and understanding in a multidisciplinary professional context relating to the study of biodiversity, its individual components, the conservation and management of natural resources, even in a broader context of territorial planning, environmental restoration and assessment of environmental sustainability of plans and processes. In this context, the graduate can carry out both managerial activities of coordination and management, and specific activities.
The ability to apply knowledge and understanding is obtained through: group activities relating to 'case studies' proposed within the various training activities; field and laboratory exercises; internships inside or outside the University. This ability is verified during the activities described above and during the activities aimed at preparing the final thesis.
III - Autonomy of judgment. The Master's graduate possesses autonomy of judgment with respect to: the choice of the most appropriate methodologies for the assessment, analysis, monitoring and conservation of biodiversity, to be applied in different ecological and biogeographic contexts and in relation to the different conditions of disturbance; the elaboration and interpretation of experimental data and the re-elaboration of literature data; the use of the most appropriate criteria for the application of sustainable development strategies in different territorial realities; the management of projects, in relation to tools, means and personnel involved; choices on ethical and deontological issues related to the conservation and management of nature; the application of current legislation in the field of management and conservation of biodiversity while interacting with the authorities responsible for the control and management of natural heritage and territorial planning. The expected results are achieved and verified during the training activities that propose 'case studies', field exercises, internships, and activities related to the preparation of the final thesis.
IV - Communication skills. The graduate acquires transversal communication skills with respect to the different professional figures operating in the environmental sector, which allow him/her to clearly express concepts to specialist and non-specialist interlocutors, both in verbal and written form, at least in Italian and English. These skills are acquired and verified through: direct interaction between teacher and student during frontal teaching activities, field and laboratory exercises; the preparation of reports relating to the various teaching activities; the preparation of oral and written exam tests; internship activities inside and outside the University; activities for the preparation of the final test and the discussion of the thesis.
V - Learning ability. The course of study develops learning skills that allow graduates to continue their studies independently and begin a professional career in the field of biodiversity conservation and management, territorial planning, restoration and environmental sustainability. These skills are acquired during the training activities through the research and reading of the most recent specialist articles, the brainstorming on the objectives of 'case studies' to be developed, and the teacher's encouragement to participate in national and international seminars and conferences. Learning skills are verified during exercises, tests in progress and profit exams.
Function in working context:
Function in working context:
- implementation and coordination of activities for planning, design, recovery and management of the natural and semi-natural environment;
- management and coordination in company policies relating to the achievement and maintenance of environmental sustainability of works, plans, projects;
- census of the natural, plant and microbial heritage;
- analysis and control of pollutants;
- design and application of integrated biomonitoring procedures for terrestrial, aquatic and atmospheric environments;
- preparation and evaluation of environmental impact studies, strategic assessments and environmental risk assessments;
- preparation of thematic maps and forecasting tools aimed at territorial planning with a view to protecting biodiversity as a whole or specific components thereof;
- basic or applied research activities.
The functions listed above, managerial and coordinating or specific, are typically carried out in an interdisciplinary or transdisciplinary context, in collaboration with other professional figures operating in the environmental sector.
Competencies associated with the function:
Competencies associated with the function:
The skills usually exercised in the working context concern:
- ability to implement conceptual models and scientific investigation protocols for specific biotic and abiotic components of the environmental compartment and for the territory as a whole;
- knowledge and ability to apply field and laboratory tools and procedures for the detection and monitoring of the biotic and abiotic components of natural and anthropized ecosystems, and for the assessment of biological responses to environmental stresses;
- ability to analyze data using appropriate mathematical and computer tools, and to critically interpret the results;
- knowledge and ability to apply what is required by national and Community legislation relating to the professional activities connected with environmental management (e.g. environmental assessment techniques, territorial planning, waste treatment, wastewater treatment plants, etc.);
- ability to assess resources and knowledge of the economic implications of the different modes of management of natural resources, with a view to implementing interventions aimed at sustainable development;
- ability to work independently in positions of responsibility and coordination, and in synergy with other professional figures operating in the environmental sector;
- adequate knowledge, in written and oral form, of the English language, as well as Italian, with reference also to the disciplinary lexicons specific to the different professional figures operating in the environmental sector.
The CLM offers two training paths that provide partially differentiated skills. One is mainly oriented towards the analysis and management of the biological component and basic and applied research, the other is more focused on the technical-evaluative and management aspects of the territory as a whole.
Professional status conferred by the degree:
The Master's graduate can carry out his/her functions as a freelancer or within public and private bodies that deal with territorial planning, environmental quality control (analysis of pollutants, terrestrial, aquatic and atmospheric biomonitoring), conservation of biodiversity, waste disposal, bioremediation. These include: bodies specifically responsible for the protection of the natural environment (Regional and National Parks and Reserves, WWF Oases, ARTA); Environment departments of public bodies (Ministries, Regions, Provinces and Municipalities) and private or state-owned companies (Municipal Environmental Services, Reclamation Consortia, Water and Wastewater Treatment Consortia, Optimal Territorial Areas). The scientific research sector also offers employment opportunities at Universities or research bodies/institutes (CNR, ENEA, etc.). Holding a Master's degree allows registration in the registers of the following professions, after passing the relevant State Exam and/or internship, where required: biologist, agronomist and forester, geologist, landscape architect. Graduates who have a sufficient number of credits in appropriate subject groups may, as provided for by current legislation, participate in the entrance tests for teacher training courses.

Program, texts and objectives:
Official language(s) of teaching and assessment: ENGLISH
Specific learning objectives:
The Master's Degree program in Applied Data Science trains professionals, the Applied Data Scientist, who can contribute within medium/large organizations as a key role in working groups that deal with framing analysis problems, planning and managing the acquisition of large data streams (i.e., "big data"), such as, for example, those related to market research or genome sequencing. The Applied Data Scientist will be able to identify, represent, acquire, manage and analyze this data, coming from specific application areas, using quantitative methodologies, mathematical-statistical-computer techniques and computer tools, and effectively communicate the results of the analyses, contributing to the formulation of tactical and strategic choices, as well as producing knowledge and value.
The Course provides:
- in the field of Information Technologies, foundational methodological knowledge for data processing and analysis, IT skills focused on Data Science and Big Data, programming and databases, machine learning and data mining, and Data Security skills;
- in the statistical-mathematical field, mathematical skills for Networks and for decision-making, skills in probability, statistics and statistical learning, skills in decision-making and optimization models, applied to the management, processing and analysis of data of various kinds;
- in the Legal and Business field, knowledge of the economic and legal aspects of data processing and use, business skills in organizational processes in the presence of big data;
- in the Linguistic and Social field, it provides skills for social analysis and the identification of ethical problems arising from the acquisition, management, processing and use of data, as well as provides useful skills to deal with logical-epistemological problems posed by data and their representation useful for managing, processing and analyzing textual data.
The Course will provide related, complementary and transversal skills that allow the graduate to interact and operate effectively in multi- and interdisciplinary groups in order to understand the needs of the sector in which they operate and to suggest effective solutions, to communicate the results of the analyses conducted in an effective way, even through advanced techniques of visualization and representation of information. Furthermore, the Course will provide skills to evaluate the legal, ethical and social implications of the methodologies and processes adopted and to keep up to date with the developments of information technology and data science.
The Course offers teaching in English and is characterized by a strong presence of laboratory activities, which constitute a fundamental, characterizing and indispensable element. Furthermore, the Course provides practical activities, in which the theories and methods acquired are applied. These activities are carried out in specific laboratories.
The Course in Applied Data Science also provides the possibility of carrying out internships and theses in companies and public and private administrations, including research and technological institutes, characterized by the advanced processing and use of data. These activities are an integral and qualifying part of the training program and facilitate the transfer of skills from the University to companies and public and private administrations.
DESCRIPTION OF THE TRAINING PROGRAM The Course is designed to train experts in data processing, analysis and use in specific application domains. Among the application domains of interest, the life sciences, digital services for citizens, process and product innovation for companies and public and private administrations, including research and technological institutes, can be considered. For each domain, a specific curriculum is planned.
The curricula share a common initial training path and then differ as they provide suitable tools for the generation, processing and analysis of data relating to the application area to which the curriculum refers. The common path consists mainly of compulsory courses, aimed at providing and/or standardizing the foundational methodological knowledge for data processing and analysis, the knowledge relating to data security issues, as well as the business, legal and linguistic knowledge relating to the notions of data and data representation. Particular importance is given to technological knowledge for the processing of Big Data and to knowledge of a legal and philosophical nature necessary to understand and address the ethical and legal problems related to the processing and use of data in their respective application areas and to evaluate the legal, ethical and social implications of the methodologies and processes used.
Dublin Descriptors: I - Knowledge and understanding
The Master's degree graduate in Applied Data Science knows the techniques of Computer Science, Engineering, Statistics and Mathematics relevant to the processing, analysis and visualization of data.
He knows the methods of data generation and collection and has the ability to understand the possible sources of uncertainty that compromise its quality.
He knows the techniques of data analysis and has the ability to understand how to apply them to data from different areas and application sectors.
He knows the computer tools and software platforms for data processing and has the ability to understand the problems related to the reliability and security of data and software systems.
He knows the mathematical-modeling tools necessary to understand how to use data to optimize the processes of companies, institutions and public administrations and improve the products and services offered.
He knows the techniques and tools for data representation and visualization of the results of the analyses to communicate data and the results of the analyses conducted effectively.
He knows the legal regulations relating to the collection, processing and use of data as well as the ethical aspects relating to the use of data in the different application areas considered by the Course.
The methods and teaching tools with which the expected results are achieved are frontal teaching lessons, project and laboratory activities in groups or individually, or the final test.
The verification of knowledge and understanding is entrusted to written and oral exams and to the evaluation of the elaborations produced for the project activities, laboratory and the final test.
II - Ability to apply knowledge and understanding
The graduate in Applied Data Science is able to collect, classify and analyze data in various application domains. He is able to evaluate the quality of the data and to identify the most suitable computer tools for their processing, also with reference to the management of security.
The graduate is able to apply the mathematical-modeling skills acquired and to use the data to improve the products and services offered by companies, institutions and public administrations.
The knowledge of the regulations on data allows the graduate to design and conduct experiments, interpret the results and, if necessary, develop original solutions and methodologies in compliance with the reference ethical and legal principles. He is able to understand and evaluate the ethical and legal impacts connected to the processing and use of data.
He is able to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed solutions, to dialogue, also in English, and to operate effectively with experts from the various application sectors in order to understand the needs of the sector and to suggest effective technical solutions.
The Applied Data Scientist, thanks to the interdisciplinarity of his training, is able to coordinate multidisciplinary projects based on the massive use of data.
The teaching tools with which the ability to apply knowledge and understanding is achieved are exercises and project activities in which students must apply the methods and techniques learned, as well as internships and the final test.
The teaching tools with which the ability to apply knowledge and understanding is verified are:
- the profit exams, with written and oral tests, also relating to project activities in which students must apply the methods and techniques learned;
- the evaluation of the reports and elaborations produced following group work, internships or final test.
III - Autonomy of judgment
Graduates in Applied Data Science acquire a high capacity for reasoning and critical judgment that will allow them to identify the most appropriate models and techniques to manage and analyze data relating to the processes and activities of an organization in order to extract new knowledge and value.
Applied Data Scientists have the ability to evaluate the impact of the proposed solutions in the application context, both with regard to the technical aspects and the organizational aspects. They are also able to identify and evaluate the broader and non-technical implications of Applied Data Science, such as those in the ethical, legal, economic and industrial fields.
They acquire the ability to understand the limits of their own knowledge and are able to identify any methodological tools to supplement their skills.
To promote the autonomy of judgment of the graduates, an active learning method will be adopted based on the student's participation, such as i) laboratory activities and in-depth study of specific and exemplary case studies, ii) internships and direct involvement in working contexts, iii) practical training activities connected to the final test.
The evaluation of the student's ability to express judgments autonomously is carried out through oral exams and analysis of personal elaborations produced both within the individual modules and in the final test.
IV - Communication skills
The Applied Data Scientist
- is able to communicate clearly the results and the most appropriate strategic lines resulting from the analysis of the data, also through adequate visualizations of the results;
- is able to present the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed solutions in technological, economic and legal terms;
- uses fluently, in written and oral form, English with reference also to the disciplinary lexicons;
- is able to communicate information, ideas, problems and solutions to interlocutors with different levels and areas of specialization, using appropriate linguistic tools;
- is able to communicate effectively with the members of a group, especially when he holds the role of coordinator or group leader;
- has the communication skills necessary for the acquisition of the requirements of the problem through interaction with the clients and the experts of the area of interest.
These objectives are achieved through training activities that involve group work, the drafting of reports in English in written and oral form of projects, and finally through the preparation of the written and oral presentation of the final test.
The verification of these objectives takes place through the profit exams and the evaluation of the reports and elaborations produced following group work, internships or final test.
V - Learning ability
The graduate in Applied Data Science
- has the learning skills necessary to allow him to continue studying in an autonomous way, as well as to proceed independently in updating knowledge, as required by the continuous evolution of technology, the social, legal, economic and productive system;
- is able to read and understand scientific texts of university and post-university level, to use technical manuals for the use of software of different types and applications;
- is able to undertake post-university studies, such as second-level masters, research doctorates and/or careers in the field of research;
- has the ability to read and learn in English.
The learning ability is acquired and verified during the course of study through the carrying out and evaluation of individual and group application projects, or the final test, elaborated in an original way by the student. In the preparation of the final test, the student is free to choose the methodologies and technologies to use.
Function in a work context.
Function in a work context:
The Master's degree graduate in Applied Data Science holds high-level technical and/or managerial roles, as an Applied Data Scientist, Data Analyst and Data Manager and Data-Driven Decision Maker, as well as a support figure for specialists in data management, processing and analysis and modeling or technical figures in specific application fields. He can operate in contexts that require the use of computer, mathematical, statistical and data processing techniques in the tertiary sector and in public administrations, in the industrial and business sector, and in the scientific, technological and application sectors such as the biological and health sectors and the business sector.
He is a professional figure to which are entrusted activities of collection, analysis, processing, interpretation, dissemination and visualization of quantitative or quantifiable data of the organization, for analytical, predictive or strategic purposes. In his work, this professional figure identifies, collects, prepares, validates, analyzes and interprets data relating to the various activities of the organization, in order to extract information (synthesis or derived from the analysis), also through the development of predictive models to generate organized knowledge systems, in order to create new knowledge and value, improve processes and/or products and possibly define new ones.
Skills associated with the function.
Skills associated with the function.
The Applied Data Scientist is able to:
- identify, classify and process the data in the possession of an organization in a specific application domain, with attention to the quality of the data and the rules that govern its processing;
- identify which data should be acquired outside the organization and the related acquisition methods, also in economic and legal terms;
- apply the techniques of Computer Science, Statistics and Mathematics relevant to the processing of large amounts of data and to formulate innovative, qualitative and quantitative answers to complex problems that require a multi- and interdisciplinary approach;
- explore, validate, model and analyze data to add value to the organization, both in terms of process and in terms of product;
- identify and use the most effective software, hardware and network infrastructures for the processing of (big) data, and manage the problems related to their reliability and security;
- communicate effectively the data and the results of the analyses carried out, both in written and oral form, also through advanced techniques of visualization and representation of information;
- understand the problems and evaluate the ethical and legal impacts connected to the processing and use of data;
- demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed solutions;
- dialogue, also in English, and operate effectively with experts from the various application sectors in order to understand the needs of the sector and to suggest effective technical solutions;
- continuously update and connect with the most advanced international realities in the field.
Professional status conferred by the degree.
Employment opportunities:
Given the variety of the types of data that can be processed, the employment opportunities are related to many sectors. The Applied Data Scientist holds high-level technical and/or managerial roles in contexts that require knowledge of the disciplines of computer science, mathematics, statistics, economics and social sciences and in-depth knowledge, including legal, of data processing and English. Thanks to its interdisciplinarity, it can coordinate Data Science projects in various application areas.
Being its training multidisciplinary, its employment opportunities can be in more areas, and include small and medium-sized enterprises, large companies, consulting and research centers, Public Administration:
- Public and private bodies
- Public and private research bodies
- Automated manufacturing industries
- Banks and insurance institutions
- Public Administration
- Public and private health institutions
- Smart City service providers
- Tourism service providers
- Art and culture service providers
- Transport service providers
- Companies operating in the IT sector
- Companies operating in the telecommunications sector
- Media
- Large-scale retail
- E-commerce service providers
- Energy distributors (gas and electricity)
- Water distributors

INFORMATION ON STUDY PLANS AND COURSES General information relating to the current academic year.
Duration: 2 years.

Language: Italian, English.
Type: MASTER'S DEGREES.
Regulations: D.M. 270/2004.
