Location: L'Aquila - University of L'Aquila.
Department: DEPARTMENT OF CIVIL, BUILDING, ARCHITECTURAL AND ENVIRONMENTAL ENGINEERING.
Admission requirements: Mandatory qualifications: [TSS].
Upper Secondary School Diploma.
Optional qualifications (choose from the following): [TSS + L2].
Bachelor's Degree: [TS + TSS].
Foreign qualification.
Dates and deadlines: Online registration: 18/07/2024 - 20/12/2024.
Deadline for submitting self-certification: 17/07/2024 - 20/12/2024.
Deadline for choosing the course online: 18/07/2024 - 19/07/2024.
Roles: Study plan approval manager: FRANCESCO D'ANNIBALE, President: FRANCESCO D'ANNIBALE.
Program, texts and objectives: Official language(s) of teaching and assessment: ITALIAN, ENGLISH.
Specific learning objectives: Graduates of the Master's Degree Course in Infrastructure Engineering have a thorough understanding of the theoretical and scientific aspects of mathematics and other basic sciences and are able to use this knowledge to interpret and describe complex engineering problems. In this context, the professionals that this Degree Course aims to train apply existing knowledge in the field of design, construction and maintenance of complex transport systems, roads, railways, airports and ports, bridges, canals, dams and intake works, irrigation systems; they design solutions to prevent, control or remediate the negative impacts of human activity on the environment; they deal with the prevention and remediation of hydrogeological hazards and slope instability, and with the management of watersheds; they conduct research on the technological characteristics of specific materials and processes; they define and design standards and procedures to ensure the functionality and safety of infrastructure; they oversee and direct these activities.
In particular, the choice of specific courses allows students to acquire skills related to:
- the planning, design, construction, management and monitoring of infrastructure systems;
- the technical assessment of the aspects related to the complex effects connected to the construction and/or refurbishment of infrastructure works;
- the resolution of complex problems related to the design and construction of infrastructure works;
- the analysis and evaluation of urban and territorial systems and the acquisition of planning techniques and tools at all scales;
- the assessment of risks associated with natural events, such as earthquakes, floods, landslides, in relation to the complex aspects concerning the design, planning, construction, refurbishment, management and monitoring of infrastructure.
The achievement of these objectives is pursued through a training activity structured in teaching modules, which include classroom lectures, laboratory exercises and individual study or practice, and which lead to credits that the student obtains by passing exams.
The training path for obtaining the Master's Degree in Infrastructure Engineering therefore includes training activities, also delivered in English, divided in a balanced way into the subjects relating to the completion of specific training in the disciplines characterizing Civil Engineering and the integration with related cultural areas.
Two areas of learning are therefore planned:
- Area for in-depth basic training: aimed at corroborating and implementing knowledge and methodological tools in the disciplines characterizing Civil Engineering and integrating with related cultural areas.
- Area for in-depth engineering training: aimed at providing knowledge and methodological tools in the field of design, construction, management and monitoring of infrastructure and infrastructure systems.
The disciplines included in the training path are also organized chronologically in such a way as to allow first the completion of basic training in the field of Infrastructure Engineering, monitoring and the risks associated with it, and then to develop concepts and methods specific to the design, construction, management and monitoring of infrastructure and infrastructure systems. The disciplines cover the typical sectors of civil engineering, such as hydraulic and port structures, concrete technology, structural theory, construction and monitoring of bridges, transport technology and economics, monitoring of infrastructure and territory, etc.; depending on the individual student's choices, these activities are accompanied by the study or in-depth analysis of other disciplines such as construction in seismic areas, seismic risk assessment and statistical tools for the design of infrastructure, timber construction, finite element structural analysis, steel construction, foundations, construction site organization, applied geology, geomatics, urban planning, BIM, etc.
Dublin Descriptors: I - Knowledge and understanding: Master's graduates in Infrastructure Engineering will have knowledge and understanding that, on the one hand, extend and strengthen those of the basic sciences acquired in the first-level training, and on the other hand, allow them to develop original ideas and to develop and solve complex engineering problems even in an innovative context and in applied research for civil infrastructure. These results will be achieved through lectures, exercises and participation in seminars held by university professors, visiting professors and professionals from the world of work, as well as guided tours of construction sites and places of interest. The use of the numerous departmental laboratories completes the training strategy of the Degree Course.
The training path includes activities characterizing the disciplinary area of Civil Engineering, in particular in the scientific-disciplinary sectors of Science and Technology of Structures (ICAR/08 and ICAR/09), Hydraulic Constructions (ICAR/02), Transport (ICAR/05), Topography and Cartography (ICAR/06), Geotechnics (ICAR/07) and their mutual integration and with related cultural areas.
The verification of knowledge and understanding is carried out in an organic way within the framework of all the assessments provided for in the course of study (exams, written and oral, in which both theoretical preparation and design skills will be assessed).
II - Ability to apply knowledge and understanding: Master's graduates in Infrastructure Engineering, following the didactic approach of the course, which aims to stimulate active participation and the ability to develop autonomous skills of the students, will be able to apply the knowledge acquired for the planning, design, analysis, construction, monitoring and refurbishment of civil infrastructure works, as well as the assessment of risks associated with natural events and the development of any mitigation strategies. These skills are acquired through exercises, usually monographic and design-oriented, in which the ability to interact in a group with other students is also stimulated, and through laboratory activities.
The verification of the ability to apply knowledge and understanding is carried out through the written and/or oral and/or practical tests provided for the profit exams, in particular through the exam tests of the disciplines that provide for a design activity and, for the other training activities, through the final exam.
III - Autonomy of judgment: Master's graduates must possess, at the end of the course of studies, a personal autonomy of judgment regarding the decisions to be taken in the phases of realization of civil infrastructure.
They will therefore be able to take autonomous decision-making responsibilities and actively participate in the design process in interdisciplinary contexts.
Advanced critical thinking skills will also be developed through the progressive involvement in research activities, through the analysis and interpretation of experimental data, theoretical results and models.
During the training process, the student will acquire the ability to solve advanced engineering problems, through the development of design applications, mainly in the courses placed in the second year.
The evaluation of the ability and autonomy of judgment achieved will be carried out progressively in the profit exams of the courses, in the development of design applications and in the preparation and discussion of the final degree thesis.
IV - Communication skills: The ability to communicate the objectives and methods of implementation of designs, even complex ones, is essential for effective insertion into the professional world.
It is therefore important for the Master's graduate to possess adequate tools for communication and to have verified their mastery through targeted simulations.
The Master's degree course will therefore provide all the tools to consolidate and further develop the communication skills of students, both written and oral, and communication through graphic representation, as well as through the use of IT and telematic tools.
At the end of the training process, the student will have developed:
- the ability to communicate clearly and convincingly the process and design choices, as well as the scientific orientations underlying them, to specialist and non-specialist interlocutors;
- the ability to manage relationships with the plurality of specialist and non-specialist subjects involved in the development of civil infrastructure (public bodies, companies, design firms, etc.);
- communication skills, also in English, both towards the scientific community and towards the different social components, even if not competent;
- both the ability to operate independently and the ability to operate as a member of a group in which there will be different skills, depending on the needs of development and the complexity and interdisciplinarity inherent in the design and realization of the infrastructure work;
- the ability to coordinate a group, even with an interdisciplinary character.
These objectives will be pursued through lectures and exercises, also held in English, requiring in particular the students, in the various courses, in the seminars and in the final thesis exam, presentations both oral and written and/or computerized of their work, also through the use of audio-visual means. The evaluative verifications of the communication skills will take place in the profit exams, in intermediate tests and seminars, and in the final degree exam.
V - Learning ability: The Master's degree course will provide students, in addition to specific knowledge, a methodological approach to study that will allow them to successfully undertake further studies (Master's and Doctoral degrees) and will enable future professionals to independently embark on a continuous process of professional growth, updating and learning.
An objective of the Degree Course is, among others, the offer of a method of work, as well as specific knowledge. This objective will be pursued through the alternation of traditional training moments (lectures) with other moments more dedicated to the development of skills of self-organization, critical synthesis and personal research (internships, degree thesis).
The verifications will take place through the profit exams and the discussion of the final degree exam.
Function in a work context:
Function in a work context:
The professional profile of the graduates is, in particular, characterized by the following functions, without claiming to be exhaustive, in a work context:
- design of complex infrastructure systems and works;
- assessment of the physical effects on the environment related to the construction of infrastructure works;
- direction of works aimed at the construction of infrastructure works;
- design of the refurbishment of infrastructure works;
- coordination of activities aimed at the management and monitoring of infrastructure works in relation to the systems associated with them.
The usual activities of the graduate may be carried out in collaboration with other professional figures involved in the infrastructure chain (Civil Engineers with different specializations, Environmental and Territorial Engineers, planners, etc.), also in a coordinating role.
Skills associated with the function:
Skills associated with the function:
In order to carry out the functions and activities associated with the professional profile, the student in Infrastructure Engineering will acquire specific knowledge, skills and competencies. In particular, by way of example, these concern:
- the ability to coordinate design groups of complex infrastructure works;
- the knowledge and understanding from a technical point of view of the aspects related to the effects resulting from the construction of infrastructure works;
- the ability to solve complex problems related to the design and refurbishment of infrastructure works;
- the ability to interact with the other professional figures involved in the infrastructure chain;
- the ability to adapt one's action to the evolution of methods, techniques, tools and technologies;
- the ability and competence in the assessment of risks associated with natural events in relation to the aspects concerning the design, planning, construction, refurbishment, management and monitoring of infrastructure (such as floods, earthquakes, landslides, etc.).
Professional status conferred by the degree:
Employment opportunities:
The professional profile and the employment and professional opportunities expected for graduates in Infrastructure Engineering are a direct result of consultation with stakeholders and the analysis of sector studies.
The objective of the Degree Course is to train Infrastructure Engineers who can practice the profession in the fields of Civil Engineering with reference to the design, planning, construction, refurbishment, management and monitoring of infrastructure. It is consistent with the University's Strategic Plan 2020-2025, which, among its objectives, aims to promote the quality of the training offer with paths consistent with the needs of the individual and society. The profession can be classified, as indicated by ISTAT, in the category "Civil engineers and related professions".
It should be noted that access to the profession, as indicated by current legislation, is subject to passing the state exam for the qualification to practice the profession of Engineer, Civil and Environmental Sector.
The professional opportunities concern the typical sectors of Civil Engineering in the infrastructure field. The professional fields for graduates range from the classic figure of the freelance engineer employed in medium/large companies, to employment in managerial positions in design companies, construction companies, central and local government bodies, and regions and municipalities. In particular, the possible professional opportunities for graduates can be listed, without claiming to be exhaustive, as follows:
- public offices for planning and management of civil infrastructure;
- companies, bodies, consortia and agencies for the management and control of infrastructure works;
- design firms operating in the field of design, refurbishment and monitoring of civil infrastructure;
- construction and maintenance companies of infrastructure works.
The continuation of studies in specific research doctorates represents a further, albeit particular, employment opportunity for graduates.

Program, texts and objectives:
Official language(s) of teaching and assessment: ENGLISH
Specific learning objectives:
The objective of the Master's Degree Course in Telecommunications Engineering: Advanced Technologies and Services is to train professionals with solid skills in Information Engineering and with specific preparation in one of the areas into which the vast disciplinary sector of telecommunications is divided. Starting from a solid background in mathematical-physical and engineering disciplines, which is a prerequisite for admission to the course, the course goes on to explore the theoretical-scientific aspects related to the characterizing disciplinary sectors and aims to provide the knowledge and skills necessary to develop advanced design skills with reference to systems characterized by a high degree of complexity and requiring innovative solutions at the product and/or service level.
In line with the evolution of recent years and taking into account the relevant professional fields, the course of study proposes a privileged educational path for the characterization, design and management of ICT infrastructures ("pervasive ICT infrastructures") that provide support for the most modern network applications (broadband services for users, industrial automation, automotive, advanced building systems such as smart buildings, power grid, etc.). In essence, the focus is on the network infrastructure, which is increasingly pervasive, articulated and heterogeneous, and which underlies the IoT (Internet-of-Things) paradigm and the world of networked systems and cyber-physical systems.
Assuming that students already have a good understanding of the basic topics of signals, systems and telecommunications networks, the curriculum provides for:
- courses in the disciplines that characterize Telecommunications Engineering, listed below: digital transmission systems, propagation models and modeling of communication channels, wireless communication systems, architectures and protocols for broadband and software-defined networks, photonic networks, signal processing and multimedia applications, systems for remote sensing, antenna systems and electromagnetic design techniques, design of metropolitan and access networks;
- courses in related or complementary engineering fields, such as: digital electronic systems, software engineering, embedded software architectures, stochastic models for networks and methods for controlling and optimizing network resources, models and methods for the environmental impact of radio systems, cyber security in the ICT field;
- specific in-depth study of basic disciplines, such as combinatorial mathematics, coding theory, algorithms for cryptography, operations research and optimization;
- further opportunities for students to choose training activities, which include strengthening knowledge of foreign languages, acquiring professional content, for which the degree program offers a structured offer, especially in the field of cyber security, and exploring aspects of business organization (individually or jointly combined with practical experience through internships in companies in Italy or abroad and in foreign universities).
The course of study is characterized by the combination of theoretical and methodological aspects relating to telecommunication systems with advanced skills in modern HW and SW technologies for the development and implementation of solutions. In this regard, it should be noted that the present course of study has already anticipated today's trends by introducing a module on embedded systems some time ago. The course of study includes project work and the explicit presence of an advanced laboratory teaching module with an adequate number of credits during the second year.
Curricula have been defined with the general objective of intercepting a trend in the field of Telecommunications to differentiate in function of a greater focus on technological aspects and in general of a greater proximity of the topics to the physical level on the one hand and of a certain propensity to address the sector of networks and services enabled by these on the other.
The Master's Degree Course in Telecommunications Engineering: Advanced Technologies and Services concludes with a final project, concerning a design and/or research activity of relevance, which demonstrates mastery of the topics covered, the ability to operate independently and an adequate level of communication skills.
Both for the carrying out of the final internship and for the carrying out of project work in the ordinary activities of the various teaching modules, the course of study offers a wide range of opportunities in the telecommunications laboratories (also the seat of the Local CISCO Academy for the release of CISCO certifications), laboratories of the DEWS Center of Excellence, laboratories of electromagnetism and EM compatibility, laboratories of HW/SW platforms and photonic systems, laboratories of optics and photonics. In this regard, it is important to emphasize the possibility of involving students in a large number of research projects at the DISIM, which guarantee the possibility of carrying out experimental activities in advanced contexts. In addition, internships are available at a large number of partner companies in Italy (e.g. Leonardo, Thales Italia, Thales Alenia Space, Telespazio, TIM, Wind Tre, etc.) and abroad (ABB in Sweden, Nokia-Siemens Networks in Denmark, etc., also through the ERASMUS Traineeship). Finally, it is possible to carry out the internship at foreign universities in the ERASMUS agreement (e.g. KTH Stockholm, University of Aalborg, Technical University of Berlin, Instituto Superior Técnico of Lisbon, ENST of Rennes, AGH Krakow, Polytechnic University of Catalonia), with which there are ongoing collaborations also for the achievement of the double degree.
In general, student mobility experiences are encouraged within the framework of ERASMUS and ERASMUS Placement agreements.
Finally, initiatives have been launched aimed at i) increasing the degree of internationalization, ii) organizing training focused on research, iii) formalizing initiatives for entering the world of work through apprenticeships for higher education. With reference to the first point, the Degree Course has made itself available to host foreign students within the framework of ERASMUS, ERASMUS Mundus (e.g. Euroweb) and TEMPUS programs and delivers all teaching activities in English since the academic year 2015-2016, with full openness to the recruitment of students on an international basis. With reference to point iii), an apprenticeship program with companies has been activated and made operational.
Dublin Descriptors: I - Knowledge and understanding
The training course offered by the Master's Degree in Telecommunications Engineering: Advanced Technologies and Services aims to provide students with the knowledge and tools to understand and address the problems related to telecommunications engineering, from both the technological and service perspectives.
At the end of the training course, the Master's graduate will have acquired:
- the knowledge underlying telecommunications engineering and the design methodologies, through the fundamental courses in the characterizing sectors ING-INF/03 and ING-INF/02;
- more advanced topics in the ICT field to be able to understand the most relevant scientific developments through advanced courses in the characterizing sectors;
- tools and methodologies more oriented to the themes of transmission chains and signal processing; or, skills necessary for the design and management of modern telecommunications networks and for the development of services enabled by new generation networks; or skills for the design and management of new generation networks through an international training course, depending on the chosen curriculum;
- interdisciplinary knowledge and transversal skills through courses in related or complementary fields.
The teaching path includes lectures and classroom exercises, laboratory activities and seminars by experts, and individual study activities. The verification of the achievement of the learning outcomes takes place mainly through the carrying out of written and/or oral exams, possible laboratory tests, and the carrying out and presentation of group assignments and across multiple training modules. Finally, the course concludes with the evaluation of the final project by a degree commission. Through these verifications, the students' ability to understand, the ability to solve problems and the ability to communicate effectively are evaluated.
II - Ability to apply knowledge and understanding
The Master's graduate will be able to apply their knowledge and understanding skills to the definition and resolution of complex design problems, and to the development and configuration of complex telecommunications networks, also evaluating their economic and organizational implications. The achievement of the ability to apply knowledge is achieved through critical reflection on the texts proposed for individual study and the carrying out of numerical exercises and practical laboratory exercises and individual or group work involving bibliographic research and the use of simulation and/or professional development environments for design.
III - Autonomy of judgment
The Master's graduate will be able to analyze, interpret and describe complex problems in telecommunications engineering, even on the basis of limited or incomplete information. He/she will also be able to assess the implications on social and ethical responsibilities related to the application of his/her knowledge and judgments. He/she will be able to integrate and use the knowledge necessary for the formulation of his/her own judgment on topics related to his/her specialization and will be able to develop a sufficient degree of creativity to define innovative solutions and approaches.
The training objective is pursued, in particular, through the teaching courses and project work and by encouraging meetings and discussions with representatives of the world of work through the organization of seminars and conferences and through the carrying out of the final degree thesis. The latter represents the moment in which the student confronts typical contexts of telecommunications engineering, elaborating original and innovative ideas, taking on the task of illustrating them and supporting their validity during the discussion.
IV - Communication skills
The Master's graduate will have developed the ability to communicate and express without ambiguity in English the development and conclusions of his/her analysis or design work, as well as the context of the knowledge related to it.
He/she will be able to interact with interlocutors, specialists and non-specialists, on topics related to the different disciplines covered by the course of study, to highlight problems and to communicate solutions using arguments and language appropriate to the different circumstances.
He/she will have developed relational skills that favor work within a group, as well as the ability to carry out coordination actions.
These objectives will be pursued in the ordinary carrying out of the teaching activity (encouraging the active participation of students), at the time of the profit checks (carried out mainly in written and/or oral form with 'open' answers), and through the carrying out of group work that involves the need to present also in a seminar form. Finally, the final project involves the discussion, in a contradictory manner with a commission, of a thesis developed independently, under the guidance of a teacher supervisor. The content of the thesis is not only evaluated in this case, but also the candidate's ability to synthesize, communicate and present.
V - Learning ability
At the end of the training process, the graduate will have developed learning skills that will allow him/her to independently set up the study of engineering and basic disciplines, even those not included in his/her curriculum. This ability, which will be well motivated by encouraging an awareness of the need for continuous training as an integral part of future professional activity, will allow the graduate to undertake with autonomy and profit any further studies (Master's and Doctoral degrees) and paths of updating and improving his/her knowledge in a self-directed manner.
The development of learning ability is pursued, within the scope of the individual teaching modules, by giving importance to the methodological aspects and stimulating individual in-depth study on specialist texts, standardization documents and scientific literature: the care of these aspects is intrinsically included in the project work and, finally, in the preparation of the final degree thesis, in which the ability to acquire new skills through autonomous research and studies is stimulated.
The verification of learning skills is an integral part of the individual exams and the final exam.
Function in a working context.
Function in a working context:
The graduate in Telecommunications Engineering: Advanced Technologies and Services of the University of L'Aquila is characterized by the combination of i) knowledge of the most modern communication technologies and architectures and ii) skills in terms of ability to model, simulate, emulate and implement in the various operating environments, with particular reference to emerging technologies and new generation networks and services.
Based on the acquired training, the professional profile for Master's graduates in Telecommunications Engineering: Advanced Technologies and Services allows them to carry out tasks related to advanced design, planning and management of complex systems and offers the basis for operating in the field of innovation and development of new solutions, basic and applied research for the development of technologies for Telecommunications, new generation networks and innovative services. A natural employment perspective is therefore represented, within the various companies, by the research and development laboratories and the design, planning and management areas of telecommunications systems, and provides access to the highest levels of the technical career. In addition, the Master's Degree provides stimuli and motivations for access to second-level Master's courses, as well as to Doctoral courses and, therefore, to a more marked orientation for carrying out research and innovation activities.
Skills associated with the function.
1) Sizing, planning and management of telecommunications networks, in relation to the architectural aspects and the programmability of modern networks; in this respect, the skills acquired in the modules of TLC Networks and partly related to certifications (e.g. CISCO and Juniper) are particularly useful;
2) Design and management of security and information protection aspects, with reference to the modules relating to cryptography and security in ICT and partly related to certifications (e.g. SPLUNK);
3) Design and modeling of digital transmission systems on physical carrier (copper and fiber optics) and radio;
4) Design and deployment of radio networks in various technologies;
5) Design, simulation and development of microwave systems, with particular reference to radio frequency chains and antennas, MIMO systems and beamforming techniques;
6) Methods and techniques for signal processing for telecommunications and for the processing of sounds and images;
7) Design and modeling of Software Defined Networks and Software Defined Radio solutions;
8) Analysis of the main vulnerabilities related to security in the ICT field and related countermeasures;
9) Assessment of the compatibility of radio communication systems with regulations on the environmental impact of electromagnetic fields.
Professional status conferred by the degree.
Employment opportunities:
The relevant company field is made up of companies that design and/or produce systems and equipment for telecommunications, operators of networks that manage complex telecommunications systems, companies and organizations that provide services through the use of telecommunications systems. In this respect, it is important to emphasize that the organization of the training path and the contents of the specialist teaching modules have been designed to provide the graduate with in-depth knowledge and appropriate design methods in sectors of great relevance in the field of modern telecommunications: radio technologies for access (e.g. mobile radio communications) and for broadband interconnection, optical technologies, remote sensing systems and applied electromagnetism, networking and internetworking technologies, programmable radio and network equipment. Particular interest is given to the integration between telecommunications technologies and the Internet world, which is closely linked to the Information and Communication Technology (ICT) scenario and the pervasive use of these technologies in all production sectors and social life. This approach corresponds to the intention of providing the graduate with ample employment prospects throughout the national and Community territory. On the other hand, it also aims to meet the relevant recruitment needs of important companies in the Abruzzo region, in a context that is being strengthened. In this context, company internships also aim to facilitate the future graduate's entry into the world of work and may evolve, in some cases regulated by specific agreements with companies, into further specialization and training activities.

Program, texts and objectives: Official language(s) of teaching and assessment: ITALIAN.
Degree awarded: Master's Degree in ELECTRONIC ENGINEERING.
Specific learning objectives: The objective of the Master's Degree Course in Electronic Engineering is to train an Engineer capable of designing and developing advanced electronic technologies and systems, to be applied in various contexts. The characteristic that specifically distinguishes the learning objectives of this master's degree is to consider electronic systems in their complexity and entirety, also taking into account the issues related to the design and implementation of its components (both hardware and software).
The Master's Degree in Electronic Engineering provides the necessary skills for this professional profile, deepening the themes of information and communication technologies. This results in a course of study that, based on the foundations of mathematics, physics, computer science and electronics, already possessed by students thanks to the training acquired in the first level of university, deepens and develops their application potential, directing teaching towards the design and management of electronic systems.
Dublin descriptors: I - Knowledge and understanding: The study course of the Master's Degree in Electronic Engineering is based on the methodological rigor of the scientific subjects. The graduate dedicates a lot of time to personal study, knows the fundamental aspects of the theories, even the most recent ones, which are the basis of electronic engineering, integrating the knowledge acquired during the first-level course with methodological and theoretical insights.
The graduate must be able to define suitable models suitable for the interpretation and description of problems related to the field of electronics, electromagnetism and electronic measurements. He must also have a mastery of the theoretical-scientific aspects of information engineering, in order to be able to identify, formulate and solve in an innovative way the problems related to the collection, processing, storage and use of information in complex and distributed systems that can use the most varied technologies.
The graduate in Electronic Engineering must be able to develop original and innovative technical solutions, starting from those already known through the scientific literature. In this way, he will be able to effectively contribute to the activities of research or project groups, even international ones, operating on reference themes of the curriculum and develop his thesis independently.
The teaching methods and tools are those described in the learning objectives. The verification of the achievement of the learning outcomes takes place mainly through the carrying out of written and/or oral exams which conclude with the assignment of a grade and which may eventually include laboratory tests.
II - Ability to apply knowledge and understanding: The didactic approach of the Master's Degree Course in Electronic Engineering aims to stimulate the active participation and the ability of autonomous elaboration of the students. Therefore, the graduate is able to apply the acquired knowledge for the analysis and design of systems for the acquisition and processing of information, which are determining elements in today's communication society.
In particular, the autonomous re-elaboration of knowledge is delegated to personal deepening, in order to evaluate the degree of mastery of the knowledge acquired by the student, enabling him to find the appropriate technical solutions for the design, sizing and maintenance of information systems.
The tests (written and oral exams, reports and seminar presentations of design works) involve the carrying out of specific tasks in which the student demonstrates the mastery of subjects, tools, methodologies and critical autonomy.
The final test represents the culmination for the refinement and verification of the acquired skills, with the addition of any elements relating to innovation and research.
III - Autonomy of judgment: The graduate in Electronic Engineering must have the ability to analyze and design complex systems, evaluating the impact of electronic solutions in the application context, both with respect to the technical aspects and the organizational ones.
The characterizing teachings provided, in particular those with a more practical and professionalizing character, allow, through the carrying out of individual and group exercises, to develop the ability to select, elaborate and interpret data for the analysis of the different systems that can contribute to the processing of information.
The study plan includes activities in which students can apply the theories presented to them, also possibly through comparison with professionals external to the University, operating in companies, agencies or bodies in the electronics sector. Consequently, relational and teamwork skills, the ability to select relevant information and to be aware of the social and ethical implications of study activities will be developed.
The training objective will be pursued, in particular, through the teaching courses and design works and by encouraging meetings and interviews with representatives of the world of work promoted with the organization of seminars, conferences and through the master's thesis. The latter represents the moment in which the student confronts contexts typical of electronic engineering, elaborating original and innovative ideas independently, taking on the task of illustrating them and supporting their validity during the discussion.
IV - Communication skills: The graduate in Electronic Engineering must be able to interact with specialists from different application sectors in order to understand effectively the terms of intervention of electronic systems in the different areas.
The graduate must be able to describe clearly and comprehensibly electronic and electromagnetic technical solutions and aspects. In particular, he must be able to train collaborators, coordinate and participate in project groups in the electronics and information industry, plan and conduct training.
These objectives will be pursued in the ordinary carrying out of teaching activities (encouraging the active participation of students), at the time of the profit checks (carried out mainly in both written and oral form with "open" answers), and through the carrying out of group works that involve the need to report also in seminar form.
Finally, the final test involves the discussion, in a contradictory manner with a commission, of a thesis developed independently, under the guidance of a teacher supervisor. The subject of evaluation in this case is not only the content of the thesis, but also the candidate's synthesis, communication and presentation skills.
V - Learning ability: The graduate in Electronic Engineering, as a result of the didactic approach and the methodological rigor of the entire study course, is able to independently acquire new technical-scientific knowledge relating to the topics of the course itself, starting from the technical-scientific literature in the specific sector of the entire Information Engineering.
The verification of learning skills will be an integral part of the individual exams and the final test.
Function in a working context:
Function in a working context:
The main functions carried out by the graduate in Electronic Engineering are those related to innovation and development of production, advanced design, planning, programming and management of complex systems.
Freelance activities are also planned, both in manufacturing or service companies and in public administrations.
Competencies associated with the function:
Competencies associated with the function:
In addition to the specific skills of the professional profile, the Electronic Engineer is characterized by:
- aptitude for the development and continuous updating of technical knowledge;
- high organizational capacity;
- creativity, initiative and autonomy in carrying out one's activity;
- propensity for teamwork;
- relational skills to collaborate and interact with experts from different disciplinary areas;
- ability to work towards objectives;
- attention to detail and rigor, even in compliance with safety and environmental requirements;
- flexibility and adaptability to various situations;
- aptitude to work in an international context and to interact with people of different cultural backgrounds.
Professional status conferred by the degree:
Employment opportunities:
The employment opportunities for graduates in Electronic Engineering are to be expected: in manufacturing or service companies, in public administrations and in research institutions, in freelance activities.
The typical professional areas for graduates in Electronic Engineering include:
- advanced design;
- applied and industrial research;
- product and process innovation.
The following can be cited as application areas:
- microelectronic technologies, which allow the integration of an increasing number of functions in circuits with reduced surface area and decreasing consumption; the evolution of these technologies is of considerable importance, so much so as to decisively influence the processing capacity of information, and therefore the power of applications;
- nanoelectronic technologies, which aim to make a brilliant leap in quality, taking inspiration from the achievement of the physical limits of microelectronics, in order to introduce new generations of devices and therefore functions;
- optical technologies, now indispensable for the "mass" transmission of information, but rich in applications in many fields;
- measurement and monitoring instrumentation, crucially linked to the "hardware" quality of its circuit components, with applications in almost all technological fields;
- remote sensing, significantly based on the ability to process electromagnetic data and on the knowledge of the physical structure of the transmission medium and the objects to be detected;
- high frequency (RF and microwave) techniques, used not only in all radio communication systems, both fixed and mobile, but also in industrial, medical and scientific applications;
- the study of electromagnetic interference, crucial both in the design of compact circuits and high-speed information transmission systems, and in the integration of different systems, all based on the electrical nature of operation, and coexisting in the same environment;
- sensor technology, a rapidly growing sector, which essentially integrates the sensor itself with the electronics necessary for the correct interpretation and transmission of the data detected.
Among the employment opportunities in the information sector, the following can be identified: electronic industries; aerospace industries; component industries; public and private bodies; but also more typical industries in the industrial sector, in which modern analog and digital electronics constitute a significant part of the production activity; research bodies operating in the field of advanced electronics.

Program, texts and objectives: Official language(s) of teaching and assessment: ENGLISH.
Specific learning objectives: The Master's Degree in Computer Engineering aims to create highly qualified professionals for the analysis, design, implementation and management of computer systems, applications and services based on the use of highly complex technologies, through the use of the most modern tools. Consequently, this course allows students to acquire a solid background capable of fully responding to the continuous demands for innovation that require a high degree of specialization and possibly an interdisciplinary approach.
To appropriately pursue the specific learning objectives, the Course of Studies is structured into curricula that provide specific skills for the training of different professional figures, and which represent distinct declinations of a unitary project.
Specifically, the unitary project provides for the provision of the following skills and abilities common to all curricula: analysis, design, implementation and management of computer systems, applications and services based on the use of highly complex technologies, based on the Internet and the Web, on robotics, and on artificial intelligence, through the use of the most modern tools. In addition:
- as a designer in the field of information technology, the Computer Engineering graduate will have in-depth knowledge and understanding of topics such as: design and implementation of corporate information systems, automation of services in public and private bodies, design of architectures and computer systems in networks;
- as a designer in the field of computer engineering, the Computer Engineering graduate will have in-depth knowledge and understanding of topics such as: design of architectures and dedicated (embedded) HW/SW systems and with close interaction with the external environment (cyber-physical), advanced architectures of information processing systems, design and analysis of high-performance and/or low-power processing systems.
The Master's graduate in Computer Engineering is therefore able to understand, use and innovate the most advanced computer technologies (HW/SW) and is therefore able to both master the increasingly rapid developments in the ICT sector and to apply their knowledge to the numerous application fields in which computer technologies can be used. In fact, these graduates have a thorough preparation in the sciences of engineering and in the basic sciences, which, enriched by specific computer knowledge and adequate design skills, allow them to interact with specialists in various sectors.
DESCRIPTION OF THE EDUCATIONAL PATH: The Course of Studies offers teaching in English and is structured into curricula. It provides a core of characterizing teachings common to all curricula that represent the basic characteristics of the Computer Engineer professional profile. Specifically, each curriculum provides for additional characterizing teachings specific to that curriculum, a set of related and supplementary courses, typically methodological and foundational and with a broad scope, to allow for a broad engineering vision of the problems and, finally, a set of elective courses to be able to carry out in a flexible and interdisciplinary manner the in-depth studies of greatest interest.
In particular:
- the core of characterizing teachings common provides skills on aspects such as: design methodologies, also specifically aimed at innovation, fundamentals of algorithms and data structures, software engineering, development infrastructures, databases;
- the in-depth studies aimed at the profile in the field of information technology provide additional skills on aspects such as: engineering of algorithms, processing of big data, distributed systems, methods and measures for Information Technology, technologies for software development;
- the in-depth studies aimed at the profile in the field of computer engineering provide additional skills on aspects such as: embedded systems and topics of automation, such as system identification and data analysis and modeling of hybrid systems;
- the in-depth studies of mathematics, appropriate for each curriculum, allow to acquire the necessary skills on aspects such as: mathematical modeling of real problems, coding methodologies for transmission and protection of information, discrete optimization, evaluation of algorithms for solving problems;
- the in-depth studies of engineering, appropriate for each curriculum, are mainly aimed at electronics and telecommunications, and provide skills on aspects such as: analysis and design of digital circuits, telecommunications networks, wireless communication, cybersecurity, cloud computing, Internet of things;
- the in-depth studies in computer science cover more formal aspects such as those related to: artificial intelligence, machine learning, software architecture and software quality.
It should be noted that the Course of Studies in Computer Engineering is characterized by a strong presence of practical, design and laboratory activities, which constitute a fundamental, characterizing and indispensable element, favoring an interdisciplinary approach. The Course of Studies also provides for the possibility of carrying out internships and theses at companies and public and private administrations, including research and technology institutions. These activities are an integral and qualifying part of the educational path and facilitate the transfer of skills from the University to companies and public and private administrations.
Dublin descriptors: I - Knowledge and understanding: The Master's graduate of this Course of Studies must have knowledge and understanding of the main methodologies, including advanced ones, necessary to be able to correctly describe and model engineering problems that require solutions typical of the Computer Engineering expert. This knowledge is initially provided by an adequate number of courses in the characterizing sectors. The knowledge is completed by further courses to be selected in the related engineering subjects. In particular, the importance given to the ability to formulate problems in a rigorous manner by means of the most appropriate mathematical models has led to the inclusion in the Course of Studies of mathematical contents of an applied type. Furthermore, in order to allow students to fully understand the typical problems in the entire ICT field, various contents offered by the related courses in the ING-INF and INF sectors are included in the study plan. Further credits in the free-choice subjects allow the student to deepen the topics of engineering that he/she considers most interesting and consistent with the desired professional profile.
The student also has the possibility of choosing various types of professional seminars, held by company professionals or external lecturers, in which the ability of understanding acquired during the course of studies is tested on specific professional topics.
The verification of knowledge and understanding is carried out in an organic manner within the framework of all the assessments provided for by the individual courses of the study program.
II - Ability to apply knowledge and understanding: The Master's graduate of this Course of Studies, based on the chosen curriculum, will be able to apply the knowledge acquired to achieve the following objectives:
- be able to formulate real problems by means of mathematical models, and be able to identify the most appropriate model for the problem in question;
- be able to apply knowledge relating to modern methodologies for the design, development and implementation of software systems, including consolidated and emerging technologies, for the management of the entire development cycle, the monitoring of quality and performance, and maintainability;
- be able to design, develop and validate dedicated ("embedded") systems and computer systems based on joint Hw/Sw design techniques;
- be able to create environments for interaction between users and systems, having full knowledge of human-computer interaction issues;
- be able to create information systems that include interconnected components, computer networks and intelligent, robotic and/or autonomous entities;
- be able to design and implement web/mobile/cloud-based applications;
- be able to design, implement and experimentally validate efficient, centralized and distributed algorithms for computational problems of various kinds;
- be able to engineer algorithms and computing systems in relation to performance, scalability, and the processing of heterogeneous and massive data, also taking into account techniques for the analysis and processing of big data, and machine learning and artificial intelligence methodologies;
- be able to design and maintain complex databases, knowing the main technologies for supporting fault tolerance and distribution;
- be able to manage the issues related to the cybersecurity of heterogeneous information systems.
These objectives are achieved both by providing solid methodological foundations through courses of a more theoretical nature, and by having students work on design activities, thanks to a certain number of courses that provide for practical-type exams. In these courses, the students, divided into working groups, carry out design activities that involve the implementation, or computer simulation, of algorithms, complex software systems based on different technologies and types of architectures, interactive systems, complex databases, and dedicated hardware/software systems. Furthermore, in the context of these activities, the students experience the dynamics of teamwork and are trained in the preparation of technical reports and the presentation of the results obtained. This allows students to enrich the hard skills typical of engineering with soft skills that are highly useful in the working context.
III - Autonomy of judgment: Thanks to the solid methodological preparation and the laboratory activities, the graduates will acquire the ability to analyze the design results of the experiments and simulations and to evaluate both the adequacy of models and/or procedures in the application context and the impact of the computer solutions designed, with respect to technical aspects, organizational aspects, deontological implications and any socio-economic repercussions. These skills will allow them to interact with other professional figures, even in interdisciplinary contexts, and to make decisions to solve the problems that may arise in the field of computer engineering in a manner consistent with the chosen path.
The achievement of this objective is achieved through individual and group study, participation in design activities in the laboratory, the preparation of reports on project activities, and the preparation and writing of the final degree thesis, which must be the result of a personal re-elaboration of the curricular contents learned.
The verification of autonomy of judgment is carried out through the individual or group reports (in particular in the context of the disciplines that provide for a design activity) and the written and/or oral tests provided for the profit exams and, for the other training activities, through the final test.
IV - Communication skills: The Master's graduate in Computer Engineering must acquire the appropriate language to express themselves on disciplinary issues, both at a general and specialist level, and, more generally, communication skills that allow them to:
- coordinate and participate in project and/or research and/or development groups in the field of computer engineering
- interact effectively with specialists from different application sectors in order to understand their specific needs in the implementation of computer tools to support their activities
- plan and conduct training in the field of computer engineering
- organize the results of their work in an effective form from a communicative point of view
- be able to describe in a clear and understandable way solutions and technical-scientific aspects of a computer nature, even in forms suitable for dissemination, with particular attention to business and social communication.
These objectives require the development of technical-scientific writing and oral presentation skills, also through the use of modern multimedia presentation technologies, which are developed throughout the study path within the regular training activities provided, through moments of discussion and comparison in group work, and refined in seminar activities and in the presentation of projects and theses, as well as in the preparation of the final test.
The teaching offered in English allows the student to have a continuous linguistic experience preparatory to interaction in international professional contexts. The Master's graduate in Computer Engineering will therefore acquire the ability to understand and express themselves in the English language, in written and oral form, at least in their technical-scientific context.
V - Learning ability: The Master's graduate in Computer Engineering must possess learning skills that allow them to update and assimilate technological innovations in the field of computer engineering. In particular, they must be able to independently acquire new technical knowledge from the scientific and technical literature in the sector, both in the areas deepened in the study path and in other areas of Computer Engineering, in function of the multiple application needs.
These learning skills are developed during the individual study of the topics covered in the lectures and exercises, as well as through laboratory activities, carried out individually and/or in groups.
The verification of learning skills is carried out through the written and/or oral tests provided for the profit exams and for the other training activities, through the design activities and the related technical reports required in some courses, and through the final test. In particular, the development of the degree thesis involves an autonomous elaboration of the technical and scientific literature in the sector.
Function in a working context:
Function in a working context:
The Computer Engineer trained by this course of studies has a high level of professional qualification and a thorough basic culture and has an aptitude for innovation, multidisciplinary work and creativity. These skills allow them to play an active and critical role in the evolution of information processing systems, information technology and its applications, meeting the needs and challenges of a rapidly evolving society, supporting and promoting change with awareness of the impact of technology on the socio-economic context.
This professional figure will therefore be able to both understand the technological evolution in the sector and contribute to it, and will be able to carry out analysis, design, development and validation functions of complex/innovative software applications and systems, both in a centralized and distributed environment, both for fixed and mobile devices.
The computer engineer is, in the first place, a designer of equipment and systems, and has an aptitude to create hardware and software systems that find applications in industry and in the public and private services sector. He/she can design and implement integrated hardware and software systems for a wide range of dedicated applications (e.g., embedded applications). He/she is able to adopt modern methodologies and technologies for the design of information processing systems and related data models; for the design of interactive applications that optimize usability and user experience; for intelligent systems and decision support systems; for web-services and the necessary architectures. He/she can design, implement, analyze and engineer efficient algorithms, even for problems of high complexity. He/she is able to develop: applications that exploit modern cloud architectures for the processing and storage of big data; mobile and pervasive applications. He/she has knowledge to evaluate and appropriately integrate the technologies available for the implementation of systems and services. He/she is able to apply the principles of information security in the design of devices and systems. He/she can carry out research activities in the fields of information and communication technologies (ICT).
Skills associated with the function:
The Master's Degree in Computer Engineering provides advanced skills in the design and implementation of information processing systems in its broadest sense, with specific skills in the use of innovative technologies, in the evaluation of the adequacy from the point of view of computational performance, maintainability, usability, scalability and security of the systems themselves.
In particular, the course provides specific skills in the following areas:
- software design: knowledge of design methodologies, development and implementation of software systems, including consolidated and emerging technologies, for the management of the entire development cycle, the monitoring of quality, and maintainability;
- design, development and validation of dedicated ("embedded") systems and computer systems based on joint Hw/Sw design techniques;
- creation of environments for interaction between users and systems, knowledge of human-computer interaction issues;
- creation of information systems, which include interconnected components, computer networks and intelligent, robotic and/or autonomous entities;
- design, development and testing of web/mobile/cloud-based applications;
- analysis and understanding of the design structure, quality and performance of complex information systems;
- design, implementation and experimental validation of efficient, centralized and distributed algorithms for computational problems of various kinds;
- engineering of algorithms and computing systems, evaluation of the issues related to performance, scalability, and the processing and storage of heterogeneous and massive data;
- analysis and processing of big data, application of methodologies of machine learning and artificial intelligence;
- design of cloud-based information systems that are able to exploit modern parallel computing and cluster-based infrastructures;
- design and maintenance of complex databases, knowledge of the main technologies for supporting fault tolerance and distribution.
- management of the issues related to the cybersecurity of heterogeneous information systems.
Professional status conferred by the degree:
Job opportunities:
The Master's graduate in Computer Engineering can carry out the various tasks indicated above, also with a coordinating role. These functions can be carried out in manufacturing or service companies, in public administrations, in self-employment or in entrepreneurial activities started independently, in research and technology institutions.
The professional figures in the field of computer engineering appear in numerous statistics as being in high demand and well paid in the industrial field, both at national and international level. In fact, the recent ISTAT employment rates three years after graduation (AlmaLaurea data, 2020) reveal that 100% are employed (94% work, 4% attend doctoral/master's courses). This shows an excellent employment situation.
