Program, texts and objectives: Official language(s) of teaching and assessment: ITALIAN.
Degree awarded: Master's Degree in MANAGEMENT ENGINEERING.
Specific learning objectives: The Master's Degree in Management Engineering offered at the University of L'Aquila, in compliance with the learning objectives that characterize the relevant Degree Class, is characterized by specific learning objectives through a common section (including the majority of the credits provided for the characterizing and related/integrative educational activities) and 2 distinct educational curricula that allow for a specialized focus in terms of design of production and logistics systems in the first, and in the management of production, organizational and logistics systems in the second.
The specific learning objectives and the description of the areas of in-depth study relating to the common section and the two identified curricula are described below.
With regard to the common section, it aims to achieve the following learning objectives:
a) to enable the analysis, interpretation and description of complex company problems based on an interdisciplinary perspective that provides for the sharing of approaches, tools and techniques from both the characterizing scientific-disciplinary sectors (Production and processing technologies, Mechanical industrial plants and Business and management engineering) and the related/integrative ones (Mechanical and thermal measurements, Information processing systems);
b) to identify and implement innovative technical, organizational and management solutions based on an interdisciplinary approach to the complex problems typical of Management Engineering, with particular focus on manufacturing companies;
c) to take into account - in the analysis, definition of alternatives, choice of the best option and its implementation - the contextual factors of a technological, sector, organizational and management nature;
d) to possess advanced knowledge in the field of analysis and evaluation of company costs as support for the decision-making process based on technical, technological, organizational and management variables;
e) to have adequate knowledge of production and logistics systems and production, organizational and logistics processes in order to allow further specialization in one of the proposed curricula.
The learning objectives of the common section are achieved through the combination of courses relating to the characterizing sectors and those relating to the related-integrative sectors. Specifically, with reference to the former (characterizing sectors), the topics relating to operations management and supply chain management are distributed between the first and second year of the master's degree course, while those relating to the evaluation of decision-making alternatives, based on advanced cost accounting systems, are concentrated in the second year. In the first year, an in-depth study of industrial quality management is also planned, in order to promote a more complete interdisciplinary vision. Finally, with regard to the related-integrative sectors, the focus is on the topics relating to the creation and management of databases and the management of industrial equipment.
As for the first of the two curricula, it is specifically focused on the design of production and logistics systems, therefore, starting from the learning objectives of the common section previously described, it allows the achievement of the following specific learning objectives:
a) development of design skills for complex systems through innovative solutions resulting from interdisciplinary approaches based on the integration of some of the characterizing scientific-disciplinary sectors (Production and processing technologies and Mechanical industrial plants) with the related/integrative ones (in particular, Mechanical and thermal measurements);
b) develop advanced theoretical-experimental skills in the simulation and validation of projects relating to production and logistics systems.
In order to achieve the aforementioned specific objectives, courses relating to the learning areas of production system technologies (including the most innovative ones, such as additive manufacturing) and industrial plant safety are planned in the two years of the course. The integration of the skills provided in the learning areas of the common section with those just described allows the development of a design capacity for production and logistics systems and their subsequent validation, also through their simulation.
The curriculum focused on the management of production, organizational and logistics systems of manufacturing and service companies adds to the learning objectives of the common section the following elements:
a) development of skills in analysis, evaluation and selection of alternatives and implementation of innovative management solutions based on an interdisciplinary approach based on some of the characterizing scientific-disciplinary sectors (Mechanical industrial plants and Business and management engineering) and on the related/integrative ones (in particular, Information processing systems);
b) develop skills in the design and implementation of simulations of integrated management solutions that specifically take into account the dimension of human resources and the management of environmental sustainability.
The further learning objectives pursued within this second curriculum are achieved through the inclusion, in the first and second year of the course, of further courses relating to economic-management topics, with particular focus on financial management, human resources and environmental sustainability. The integration between the contents of these courses and those provided in the common section allows the development of skills capable of identifying innovative management solutions and implementing them through possible simulation of their effects.
Regardless of the curriculum chosen for their specialization, the Master's Degree in Management Engineering offered by the University of L'Aquila promotes the fluent use of the English language, with particular attention to the disciplinary lexicon typical of industrial and service companies.
Dublin Descriptors: I - Knowledge and understanding: At the end of the Course of Studies, the student will have acquired mainly:
- knowledge of decision-making systems with particular attention to the phases of data collection and analysis;
- knowledge of decision-making systems with particular attention to the evaluation of possible alternatives and the definition of the optimal solution;
- knowledge of methods and techniques for managing production, organizational and logistics systems;
- knowledge of techniques for processing and validating indicators for evaluating the performance of management processes;
- knowledge of systems for evaluating the impact of company systems in terms of economic, environmental and social sustainability.
II - Ability to apply knowledge and understanding: At the end of the Course of Studies, the student will have acquired mainly:
- ability to undertake and implement decisions, even in non-deterministic contexts;
- ability to measure, detect, classify and analyze the data necessary to support business decisions;
- ability to develop, implement and manage processes of organizational, management, production and technological innovation;
- ability to evaluate opportunities for improving the degree of economic, environmental and social sustainability of production and management systems.
III - Autonomy of judgment: It is assumed that the development of autonomy of judgment, communication skills and learning ability is encouraged by the interaction with the teacher and with other students during the teaching activities. In particular:
- during the lectures, the ability to acquire knowledge and understanding is stimulated;
- in the interaction with the students, decision-making situations are proposed, in order to develop the ability to understand and identify appropriate solutions;
- in the participation in guided exercises and group work, communication and argumentation skills are developed;
- in the preparation of written reports (also in groups), skills in synthesis and application are promoted.
At the end of the training process, the student will be able to formulate autonomous and critical judgments, even on the basis of limited/incomplete information. In this sense, he will know how to take into account the priorities that from time to time - autonomously or in cooperation - he will consider most appropriate. In particular, the Master's degree graduate in Management Engineering:
- is able to retrieve and select the information necessary for the resolution of a problem that involves simultaneously aspects of a technological, plant, organizational and management nature;
- is able to interpret and evaluate the results of an improvement process (product/process innovation, logistics, management control) to be implemented/implemented in a company, taking into due account the specificities of the same (e.g. size, sector of activity, ...);
- has the ability to analyze and decide on company problems of high strategic impact such as the sizing of production capacity and the technical, economic and financial evaluation of investments;
- is aware of the responsibilities that the engineering solutions adopted may have in terms of economic, environmental and social sustainability.
These skills will also be developed through the analysis of case studies dealt with during the studies, as well as in the retrieval and processing of the information necessary for the preparation of the thesis. The verification of the achievement of these skills will be evaluated in the profit exams and in the discussion of the final paper.
IV - Communication skills: At the end of the training process, the student will have acquired:
- ability to relate and communicate in a clear and well-argued manner with specialists and non-specialists, of different cultural background (technological, organizational, economic) and different levels of company responsibility;
- ability to integrate into working groups, even with a coordinating function;
- ability to present and describe in a clear and effective way the problems and the related engineering solutions;
- ability to communicate effectively with representatives of the industrial world at both national and international level.
These skills are developed both during the training activities and through cooperation and discussion in group activities. The verification of these skills is ascertained in group activities, in the exams and in the final test.
V - Learning ability: At the end of the training process, the student will have acquired:
- awareness of the need for continuous learning, to be undertaken independently throughout his working life;
- the ability to independently acquire new knowledge, both of a technical and scientific nature, necessary for the improvement and management of processes and economic aspects.
This ability derives from the consolidated learning methodology acquired during the course of study. The verification of this ability is carried out in the exams, in the retrieval and consultation of scientific and technical literature and in the preparation of the final paper.
Function in a work context:
Function in a work context:
The Master's Degree in Management Engineering has been active for twenty years and has trained about 500 master's graduates.
The Management Engineer trained at the University of L'Aquila has a strong industrial vocation which allows him to operate also in service companies, thanks to the general vision of the processes and the interdisciplinary and multifunctional approach.
The management engineer trained at the University of L'Aquila is able to exploit economic, managerial and engineering skills to define and implement organizational, operational and technical company procedures with an integrated vision, making the necessary changes to optimize the processes (organizational, production, logistics) in order to combine efficiency, effectiveness and profitability with an orientation towards innovation.
Starting from a solid common base of knowledge and skills typical of industrial systems engineering, through the 2 specific training paths previously described, the Master's degree graduate in Management Engineering of the University of L'Aquila will be able to specialize in the design of production and logistics systems or in the management of management processes, with particular attention to organizational, production and logistics processes.
As regards the design of production and logistics systems, the Master's degree graduate in Management Engineering of the University of L'Aquila will be able to carry out the following tasks:
- design of production systems with particular reference to industrial companies;
- design/redesign of logistics systems both in the field of manufacturing companies and in that of engineering consulting;
- design/redesign of technological cycles in manufacturing companies, also using innovative production technologies.
As regards the management of organizational, production and logistics processes, the Master's degree graduate in Management Engineering of the University of L'Aquila will be able to carry out the following tasks:
- organization and management of production and support activities (e.g. maintenance, production management);
- organization and management of supply chain management activities (e.g. procurement, industrial and distribution logistics);
- design and management of systems for analyzing operational, economic and financial performance (e.g. management control, financial management);
- design and management of organizational and information systems.
Skills associated with the function:
Skills associated with the function:
The course of study is designed to train professionals capable of operating with a high level of specialized skills, even within multidisciplinary groups, in the areas typical of management engineering with reference to the design and/or management of company systems, both in the case of production of goods and in the provision of services.
More specifically, the master's graduates who will have successfully followed the curriculum relating to the design of production and logistics systems will have acquired the following knowledge and skills that will enable them to carry out the professional roles previously indicated:
- Knowledge of the principles of design of production plants
- Knowledge of the technologies of production processes
- Knowledge of quality management systems in manufacturing and service companies
- Ability to measure, detect, classify and analyze the data necessary to support business decisions
- Ability to analyze and interpret the operating modes of complex production systems
- Ability to plan, manage, analyze and implement new production methodologies aimed at optimizing the operations cycle
- Ability to contribute to the introduction of innovative methodologies in the field of production
As regards, however, the master's graduates who will have successfully followed the curriculum relating to the management of organizational, production and logistics systems, the latter will have acquired the following knowledge and skills that will enable them to carry out the professional roles previously indicated:
- Knowledge of decision-making systems with particular attention to the phases of data collection and analysis in support of the identification of possible alternatives
- Knowledge of decision-making systems with particular attention to the phases of evaluation of possible alternatives and identification of the optimal solution for the management of organizational processes
- Knowledge of systems for managing and controlling operations
- Knowledge of quality management systems in manufacturing and service companies
- Knowledge of systems for detecting, analyzing and evaluating the performance of organizational processes
- Ability to measure, detect, classify and analyze the data necessary to support business decisions
- Ability to analyze and interpret the operating modes of complex management systems
- Ability to deal with and solve new or low-deterministic problems, typical of the organizational systems in which he is called to operate
- Ability to plan, manage, analyze and implement new organizational and management methods aimed at optimizing company processes
- Ability to contribute to the introduction of new techniques and tools for the management of company processes
Professional status conferred by the degree:
Job opportunities:
The peculiarity of the management engineer, his flexibility and transversality allow to identify a plurality of sectors and professional roles in which to carry out his duties. Graduates find natural employment in any manufacturing and service company, regardless of the specific sector of activity and size. Graduates also find employment in consulting firms, public utility service companies (e.g. transport, healthcare, telecommunications) and public administration. After passing the State Exam and registration in a specific register, they can carry out freelance activities. The solid knowledge and skills developed and the interdisciplinary vision acquired in the study path, finally allow the Master's degree graduate in Management Engineering of the University of L'Aquila to undertake entrepreneurial paths even in sectors with a high level of technological innovation.

Program, texts and objectives: Official language(s) of teaching and assessment: ITALIAN. Degree awarded: Master's Degree in CHEMICAL ENGINEERING. Specific learning objectives: The Master's Degree in Chemical Engineering trains highly skilled technicians capable of tackling the design and development of process and scientific-technical innovation. The training builds on the basic engineering knowledge required for admission to the course and, in line with the relevant ministerial guidelines LM22 and the guidelines of the European Federation of Chemical Engineers (EFCE), is strongly characterized by the specific features of the location. The student is thus effectively involved in the process of transferring knowledge developed by research on key issues in modern chemical engineering. The training course is structured in teaching modules, with classroom lectures, laboratory exercises and individual and group study, with the assistance of the teaching staff. The student obtains the credits associated with the modules by passing the exams. The chronological structure of the training course, detailed in the table of training activities, assists the student in their cultural growth and gradually leads them to develop professional autonomy. To this end, even the subjects taught in the first year of the course, aimed at consolidating knowledge of the issues that characterize chemical engineering, use the "homeworking" tool. The subjects in the second year structure the students' maturity, guiding them more decisively towards the design aspects of the profession. The degree course may include several training paths that also offer teaching on transversal themes in line with the internationally recognized figure of the modern chemical engineer. There are courses that orient the student towards industrial biotechnological processes, renewable energy chains, new materials, resource reuse, the design of environmentally sustainable plants and the environmental control of industrial waste.
Dublin Descriptors: I - Knowledge and understanding: During the training process, master's degree graduates will acquire all the knowledge necessary for understanding the fundamental principles of Chemical Engineering, which constitute the unitary structure of the course of study. They will be able to identify and master the knowledge relating to the design and sizing of equipment and process plants; industrial instrumentation and process control; process analysis and simulation. This knowledge will be developed harmoniously through strong integration with transversal disciplinary skills aimed at stimulating an interdisciplinary approach and the extrapolation of one's knowledge to complex systems/situations and innovative sectors. The knowledge and understanding skills of the student are acquired through core subjects, active participation in exercises, seminars, internships as well as personal and group study. II - Ability to apply knowledge and understanding: At the end of the training process, master's degree graduates will be able to apply their knowledge to formulate, develop, synthesize and solve complex problems of Chemical Engineering and related interdisciplinary industrial sectors, and will therefore be able to plan the material and energy balances that govern the operation of units, processes and chemical plants; develop the calculations for the sizing and verification of the operation of individual equipment and systems of equipment; develop the modeling, design and management of chemical and energy processes; choose and use, among the available operations and processes, those most suitable for sustainability and environmental protection in relation to industrial activities in general and those of the chemical industry in particular. The verification of the achievement of learning outcomes mainly takes place through the written and/or oral tests provided for the exams. Further significant moments of verification include self-assessment tests carried out also on digital platforms and spaces, online applications and digital devices, laboratory experiences, internship activity reports, reports of individual and/or group projects with their related presentations and during the final examination. III - Autonomy of judgment: The Master's Degree graduate in Chemical Engineering develops the ability to analyze and design complex production systems and processes, evaluating their characteristics and benefits and any potential damage that may arise from their development. The applied subjects he has received during his studies develop his autonomy of judgment and the ability to make strategic decisions, supplementing any lack of information through experimentation and simulation in conditions close to real ones. To achieve this goal, the master's degree in chemical engineering is structured on a didactic approach that combines theoretical training with examples, applications, individual and group work and tests that stimulate active participation, a proactive attitude and the ability to autonomous elaboration. In order to promote the achievement of full professional autonomy of judgment, the course of study offers its students many opportunities to compare with professionals external to the University operating in companies, agencies or bodies in the field of Chemical Engineering or related sectors. IV - Communication skills: The master's degree graduate in chemical engineering acquires the ability to lead working groups and projects involving people with expertise in different disciplines and at different levels. The progressive development of this ability is monitored by the course of study, which encourages students to present and synthesize the results of their study and their thesis work, and to understand the state of the art of the topics addressed. The Master's Degree graduate in Chemical Engineering is able to describe in a clear and understandable way solutions and technical aspects of applications specific to the sector, to argue and defend their technical choices, to communicate the results to the scientific community and to non-specifically competent social groups, to train collaborators and participate in project groups by coordinating their activities. V - Learning ability: The Master's Degree graduate in chemical engineering has a learning ability that allows him to effectively and flexibly address the work problems related to technological innovation and the changes in the economic and production system. The Master's Degree graduate in Chemical Engineering has developed, as a result of the didactic approach and the methodological rigor of the entire course of study, the ability to autonomously acquire new technical-scientific knowledge relating to the topics of the course itself, starting from the literature of the specific sector or in related sectors. This is because he is fully aware of the need for autonomous learning throughout his life, in order to increase his skills and knowledge. The subjects studied during the master's degree course in Chemical Engineering are taught using approaches that induce the ability to identify, define, analyze and solve different and complex problems through in-depth studies, personal but guided by the teaching staff. Particularly useful for this purpose are the degree thesis and any internships carried out in the laboratory, in industrial production contexts and at design companies, the initial self-assessment tests and intermediate verification tests carried out also through tests on digital platforms and spaces, online applications and digital devices, the reports of individual and/or group projects with their related presentations.
Function in a work context:
Function in a work context:
The Master's Degree graduate in Chemical Engineering at the University of L'Aquila has a solid foundation in transversal and specialized scientific disciplines, which enables him to interpret, describe, formulate and solve complex problems. Typical tasks that he will carry out in the work context are the design, operation and control of equipment and plants in the chemical, environmental, biotechnological and new materials industries, paying continuous attention to the issues of environmental, economic and social sustainability and safety. He will collaborate with all the technical-scientific and organizational-managerial professionals involved in modern production contexts, also managing international relations at interpersonal and corporate level. He will be able to immediately hold coordination roles at a medium level of responsibility. He has the fundamental basis to undertake further paths of professional growth and training, which may lead him to hold roles of greater responsibility.
Skills associated with the function:
Skills associated with the function:
The training received during the course of study by the Master's Degree Engineer in Chemical Engineering develops balanced skills and abilities between specialized and transversal knowledge. These will be habitually used to work effectively in groups including professionals also from different cultural backgrounds. The Master's Degree Engineer in Chemical Engineering, thanks to his ability to define, model and solve complex problems, will be able to carry out activities of coordination in the fields of applied research and industry, innovation, sustainable development and production.
Professional status conferred by the degree:
Employment opportunities:
Master's degree graduates in Chemical Engineering will work in the professional fields of applied research and innovation, development and production, advanced design, and planning. Both in the private sector and in public administrations as well as in freelance work. In particular, for the exercise of freelance work, it is necessary to pass the state exam for the qualification to the profession of Engineer and to register with the relevant professional register.
Master's degree graduates in Chemical Engineering will find employment in the chemical and process industry, in the food, pharmaceutical and biotechnological industries, in companies for the development and transformation of polymeric, ceramic, glass and composite materials, in engineering, plant engineering and environmental services companies, in civil and industrial companies and bodies as heads of the environment, water and energy sector, in applied research centers, in industrial laboratories, in structures of the public administration responsible for the management of energy, the environment and safety. These skills can also be expressed in freelance or subordinate consulting activities within manufacturing or service companies, or in the public administration.

Program, Texts and Objectives: Official language(s) of teaching and assessment: ITALIAN.
Degree awarded: Master's Degree in ELECTRICAL ENGINEERING.
Specific learning objectives: The Master's Degree in Electrical Engineering aims to train technicians with a high-level university education and skills to develop and manage complex activities related to scientific and technological design and innovation and to promote research in a broad technical-scientific field. It aims to build, on the basic and engineering training required for admission to the course, a training focused on the in-depth study of the scientific disciplines specific to Electrical Engineering, without neglecting content from related or complementary cultural areas.
The objectives of the training are the development of professional skills regarding:
- the design of systems and the management of processes related to the production, transformation, distribution and use of electrical energy;
- the design and control of electric machines and power converters, equipment and systems for electric mobility, industrial automation and home automation;
- the measurement and monitoring of electrical systems;
- the modeling and analysis of electromagnetic emission phenomena in electrical systems.
The achievement of these objectives is pursued through a training activity structured in teaching modules, which include classroom lectures, laboratory exercises and individual study or practice. These modules lead to credits that the student obtains by passing profit exams.
The Master's degree course in Electrical Engineering may provide for multiple training paths in order to organize the skills offered in specific or emerging areas of electrical engineering, such as renewable energy and distributed generation, electric mobility, industrial automation and home automation.
The disciplines included in the training path focus on the typical sectors of electrical engineering: electrical systems for energy, converters, electric machines and drives, electrical engineering, electrical and electronic measurements; these activities can be supplemented by transversal disciplines such as automation and computer science, or integrative with respect to specific training paths, such as electronics, telecommunications, energy and mechanical systems, transport.
The training path is organized in such a way as to distribute the methodological training and the knowledge provided in a coordinated and progressive manner within the scope of the courses and other training activities provided for in the study course.
Dublin Descriptors: I - Knowledge and understanding: During the training process, Master's degree graduates in Electrical Engineering acquire in-depth skills in the disciplinary area characterizing electrical energy:
- knowledge and understanding of the methodological and design bases of electrical engineering;
- knowledge and understanding of the different components of the production, conversion, transmission, distribution and use of electrical energy chain;
- knowledge and understanding of the technologies and electrical components for civil and industrial automation systems;
- knowledge and understanding of the technologies and components for electric mobility;
- knowledge and understanding of the methodologies for measuring and analyzing electrical quantities;
- knowledge and understanding of the problems related to electromagnetic emissions in electrical systems.
This knowledge is integrated, also in relation to the teaching plan and the learning areas identified annually by the Area Teaching Council, with disciplinary skills of a transversal nature, such as automation and computer science, or integrative with respect to the strictly electrical field, such as electronics, telecommunications, energy and mechanical systems, transport.
The training aims to offer a broad spectrum of multidisciplinary knowledge that allows the development of the strategic vision necessary to successfully face the technological and socio-economic challenges of the future of electrical energy, both in traditional contexts and in the more emerging contexts of smart cities and technologies for sustainable and eco-compatible development, from the use of renewable energy sources to electric mobility, to distributed generation systems.
The characterizing training activities are based on the disciplines specific to the field of electrical energy, specifically ING-IND/31 - Electrical Engineering, ING-IND/32 - Converters, electric machines and drives, ING-IND/33 - Electrical systems for energy, ING-INF/07 - Electrical and electronic measurements.
The integrative or related training activities are identified within the scope of the disciplines ING-INF/01 - Electronics, ING-INF/03 - Telecommunications, ING-IND/13 - Mechanics applied to machines, ING-IND/09 - Systems for energy and the environment, ING-IND/17 - Industrial mechanical plants, ICAR/05 - Transport, ING-INF/04 - Automation, ING-INF/05 - Information processing systems.
Other knowledge and skills include mastery of technical and conversational foreign languages.
The tools used to achieve the training objectives include theoretical lessons and exercises in the classroom, practical laboratory activities, individual and/or group projects, training for the use of instruments and software for calculation, seminars and educational visits, training and orientation internships, individual study and self-learning activities, thesis activities.
II - Ability to apply knowledge and understanding: At the end of the training process, Master's degree graduates in Electrical Engineering will be able to:
- develop mathematical models and simulate the behavior of electrical systems for the production, transmission, distribution and use of electrical energy;
- develop procedures and guidelines for energy efficiency and monitoring of civil and industrial plants;
- apply optimized design methods for plants and electric machines, aimed at energy saving and sustainable development;
- solve problems of management and control of automation systems;
- model and design components and systems for electric mobility.
The acquired skills will allow them to face problems, even of a complex nature, in contexts that are not well defined or with specific contradictions, or with constraints external to the strictly scientific/technological problems typical of a purely theoretical context.
Master's degree graduates in Electrical Engineering will be able to manage all the stages of evolution of an electrical process and/or system, starting from research and development, passing through detailed design and the implementation phase, to arrive at the management/supervision of the system; they will be able to use laboratory equipment and define test and measurement protocols; they will be able to use computer tools both for the collection of textual and numerical information and for the processing of calculations and simulations as well as for the preparation of the final technical documentation of an activity; they will be able to work in a team and interact with subjects and structures in the workplace; they will be able to express themselves in a foreign language, both technical and conversational.
The verification of the ability to apply knowledge and understanding is carried out through the written and/or oral tests provided for the profit exams, the results of exercises in the classroom or in the laboratory, the reports of internship activities, the reports of individual and/or group projects, the tests of use of instruments, computer tools and calculation software, the discussion of the degree thesis.
The level of mastery of the knowledge achieved is assessed in particular in design-type activities and in the preparation of the final thesis, in which the application and critical analysis of the information and knowledge acquired, personal initiative and the ability to face and solve problems are punctually put to the test, also in an extra-university context, promoting activities with companies, professional studios and external bodies, national or foreign.
III - Judgment skills: Master's degree graduates must have the ability to design and conduct analytical investigations, through the use of models and complex experiments, knowing how to critically evaluate the data obtained and draw conclusions. Master's degree graduates must also have the ability to investigate the application of new technologies in the field of electrical engineering.
The didactic approach provides that theoretical training is accompanied by examples, applications, individual and group work and tests that stimulate active participation, a proactive attitude and the ability to autonomous elaboration.
IV - Communication skills: Master's degree graduates must be able to operate effectively as a leader of a project and/or a group, which may be composed of people with expertise in different disciplines and at different levels. The Master's degree graduate must be able to work and communicate effectively in broader contexts, both national and international.
The didactic approach provides in (some) characterizing courses involving project activities and in the thesis work, applications and tests that stimulate active participation, a proactive attitude and the ability to communicate the results of the work carried out.
V - Learning ability: The Master's degree graduate must possess a learning ability that allows him to effectively face the changing work problems related to technological innovation and the changes in the economic and production system.
He must also be aware of issues such as risk and change management. Finally, he must be able to recognize the need for autonomous learning throughout his life.
The courses of the Master's degree use didactic methodologies such as the analysis and resolution of different and complex problems, the integration of the various disciplines and group discussion; these methodologies promote the acquisition of skills related to learning and adaptation. Other tools useful for achieving these skills are the degree thesis, which provides that the student measures and understands new information, and the possible internship carried out in a laboratory or in an industrial production context.
Function in a work context:
Function in a work context:
The Master's degree in Electrical Engineering trains technicians with a high-level university education and skills to design and manage complex activities related to scientific and technological design and innovation and to promote research in a broad technical-scientific field.
The training received allows the electrical engineer to interact with professionals from different cultural backgrounds, to lead the work of the group and to operate in the workplace with autonomy and flexibility and in compliance with professional ethics, even at an international level.
Skills associated with the function:
Skills associated with the function:
Master's degree graduates in Electrical Engineering have:
- technical, economic and management skills in the field of electrical systems for energy: plants for production from conventional and renewable sources, transmission, distribution and use of electrical energy, monitoring and diagnostics of networks and users, energy saving;
- skills regarding the technologies and electrical components for civil and industrial plants, in automation and home automation systems, in electrical systems for mobility, in plants for distributed electricity generation;
- skills regarding the methodologies for measuring and analyzing electrical quantities: monitoring of plants and machines for industrial production, transmission, processing and management of measurement information;
- skills in the design, sizing and control of electric motors, electromechanical actuators and electronic power systems;
- skills regarding the problems related to electromagnetic emissions in electrical systems: generation of disturbances, electromagnetic compatibility, rejection and immunity.
Professional status conferred by the degree:
Job opportunities:
The job opportunities for Master's degree graduates in Electrical Engineering include both manufacturing or service companies, public administrations, research institutions and self-employment. With regard to the latter, the course of studies prepares for the profession of engineer, section A, industrial sector, electrical specialization.
The typical professional activities for Master's degree graduates in Electrical Engineering are:
- the design of electrical and electronic power components, equipment and systems;
- the management and conduct of industrial production and transformation processes;
- the management of the technical office of manufacturing companies, the tertiary sector, services and the public administration;
- technical and management activities in companies operating in the energy and transport sectors.
In addition, the specialized knowledge acquired on the different themes of the electrical energy chain offers the Master's degree graduate a wide range of job opportunities in the emerging sectors of smart cities and technologies for sustainable and eco-compatible development, from the use of renewable energy sources to electric mobility, to distributed generation systems.
Graduates who have obtained a sufficient number of credits in appropriate disciplinary areas may, as provided by current legislation, participate in the entrance exams for training courses for secondary school teaching.

Program, texts and objectives: Official language(s) of teaching and assessment: ITALIAN, ENGLISH.
Degree awarded: Master's Degree in MECHANICAL ENGINEERING.
Specific learning objectives: The Master's Degree in Mechanical Engineering aims to train technicians with a high-level university education, with skills to carry out and manage complex activities related to the design and development of scientific and technological innovation and the promotion of research for industrial purposes. It therefore aims to build, on the basic and engineering training required for admission to the course, a broad and high-level engineering training, with particular reference to mechanical engineering, and a professional competence aimed at: solving complex engineering problems, the advanced design of components, machines, energy systems, technologies, structures and mechanical systems, the design and management of complex industrial production activities and related processes. The knowledge acquired must also be adaptable to scenarios of evolving methods, techniques, tools and technologies.
The Master's Degree course in Mechanical Engineering provides for five curricula (biomedical, energy, mechatronics, design and vehicles) within which disciplinary content related to the characterizing sectors of Mechanical Engineering is addressed, with different weights.
- The Biomedical Curriculum provides a consolidated basic training in Mechanical Engineering, oriented to the analysis, modeling, design and development of devices, equipment, systems and procedures for support in diagnostic imaging; robotic systems for medical and industrial applications; prostheses, artificial organs and devices for supporting vital functions. In addition, in-depth knowledge of thermo-fluid dynamics applied to the analysis and modeling of complex biological systems is provided.
- The Energy Curriculum provides a consolidated basic training in Mechanical Engineering aimed at providing knowledge on heat transfer, thermodynamics and fluid dynamics applied to machines and energy conversion systems. Knowledge is also provided on energy issues related to power transmission. The training objective is also aimed at understanding the problems of combustion, dynamic models, regulation, environmental impact and modern energy technologies with a view to sustainability.
- The Mechatronics Curriculum provides a consolidated basic training in Mechanical Engineering aimed at providing knowledge relating to the analysis and development of complex mechanical systems such as robotic devices, automatic and mechatronic systems in general. Knowledge is also provided on systems for automation, electronics and the control of mechanical devices.
- The Design Curriculum provides a consolidated basic training in Mechanical Engineering aimed at providing knowledge on the processes relating to the development of products, process technologies, machines and complex mechanical systems. Knowledge is also provided on the analysis, conceptual development, functional and concrete design of groups and complex mechanical systems, including robotic devices and automatic systems. In-depth knowledge is also provided on the methodologies and processes of concurrent design, with reference to known or to be identified use requirements.
- The Vehicles Curriculum provides a consolidated basic training in Mechanical Engineering aimed at providing knowledge on the design and development of vehicles with specific reference to dynamic and fluid dynamic modeling, the management of technological processes and modern technologies. Knowledge is also provided on propulsion systems with specific reference to the sector of sustainable mobility.
The transversal training objective for all curricula is aimed at understanding the methodologies and non-routine processes of the design and development of innovative products, which take place in conditions of uncertainty, in order to face the complex current and future challenges of mechanical engineering.
At the end of the training process, regardless of the curriculum followed, the student will have acquired:
- an in-depth knowledge and a clear understanding of the methodological and design bases of mechanical engineering;
- knowledge and understanding of the most rigorous methodologies for the advanced design of components, machines, energy systems, technologies, structures and mechanical systems, as well as for the design and management of complex industrial production activities and related processes and plants;
- a critical knowledge of the latest developments in modern technologies.
The final examination, of an experimental, modeling or design nature, is an integral part of the training and is often accompanied by apprenticeship internships at national and international bodies, companies and universities.
The shared training objective between the different curricula is guaranteed by courses common to all training courses and by dedicated courses, but referable to the same SSDs characterizing the class. In this way, the disciplinary content is combined with the specific industrial area to which the curriculum refers.
The training course for obtaining the Master's Degree in Mechanical Engineering provides for training activities divided in a balanced way in the subjects relating to the completion of specific training in the disciplines characterizing mechanical engineering and the integration with related cultural areas. The disciplines included cover the typical sectors of mechanical engineering: machine construction, applied mechanics, machines, methods for industrial design, mechanical technologies, thermal measurements and tests. These activities are accompanied by the study of other disciplines of a transversal nature, such as fluid dynamics, control systems, electronics and electrical drives and systems.
Dublin Descriptors: I - Knowledge and understanding: At the end of the training process, the student will have acquired:
- an in-depth knowledge and a clear understanding of the methodological and design bases of mechanical engineering;
- knowledge and understanding of the most rigorous methodologies for the advanced design of components, machines, energy systems, technologies, structures and mechanical systems, as well as for the design and management of complex industrial production activities and related processes and plants;
- a critical knowledge of the latest developments in modern technologies in the sectors of mechanical design, energy, automation, biomedicine, vehicles, the integration of mechanical systems with electronic and IT systems and industrial production.
The methodological training and the information necessary to enable the student to acquire the knowledge indicated above are distributed in a coordinated and progressive manner within the courses and other training activities proposed by the course of study. The verification of knowledge and understanding skills is carried out in an organic manner within the framework of all the assessments provided for in the course of study.
II - Ability to apply knowledge and understanding: At the end of the training process, the student will have acquired:
- an in-depth knowledge and a clear understanding of the methodological and design bases of mechanical engineering;
- knowledge and understanding of the most rigorous methodologies for the advanced design of components, machines, energy systems, technologies, structures and mechanical systems, as well as for the design and management of complex industrial production activities and related processes and plants;
- a critical knowledge of the latest developments in modern technologies in the sectors of mechanical design, energy, automation, biomedicine, vehicles, the integration of mechanical systems with electronic and IT systems and industrial production.
The methodological training and the information necessary to enable the student to acquire the knowledge indicated above are distributed in a coordinated and progressive manner within the courses and other training activities proposed by the course of study. The verification of knowledge and understanding skills is carried out in an organic manner within the framework of all the assessments provided for in the course of study.
III - Autonomy of judgment: At the end of the training process, the student will have acquired the ability to manage the complexity typical of the problems of Mechanical Engineering from the ideation and development phase to the integration of all design and concrete realization activities of the product and processes. He will also have acquired the ability to independently manage complex systems and processes, also assuming responsibility for them. He must therefore be able to formulate critical judgments and assessments also on the basis of limited or incomplete information, taking into account the increasingly stringent problems of reliability, safety, environmental protection and ethics in general, connected with the responsibility of using technologies and plants.
Specific skills must be developed in the field of design: the ability to use one's knowledge to design solutions to complex problems, even if not well known or interdisciplinary; creative ability for the development of innovative and original approaches; the ability to interact with social and cultural processes; the ability to operate in conditions of uncertainty. In the event of a lack of specific information on the system under study, graduates must also have the ability to experiment and simulate, in conditions as close as possible to those of real operation of the machines, technological processes and plants under analysis.
The preparation and writing of the final degree thesis, which must be the result of a personal re-elaboration of the curricular content learned, is delegated in particular to achieving this objective.
The verification of autonomy of judgment is carried out through the written and/or oral tests provided for the profit exams, in particular through the exam tests of the disciplines that provide for a design activity and, for the other training activities, through the final test.
IV - Communication skills: At the end of the training process, the student will have developed:
- the ability to communicate in a clear and well-argued manner the process and design choices, as well as the scientific orientations underlying them, to specialist and non-specialist interlocutors;
- the ability to manage relationships with the plurality of subjects, specialists and non-specialists, involved in the development of the systems of interest to Mechanical Engineering;
- communication skills both towards the scientific community (national and international) and towards the different social components, even if not competent;
- both the ability to operate independently and the ability to operate as a component of a group in which there will be different skills, depending on the needs of the project development;
- the ability to coordinate a group, even an interdisciplinary one;
- linguistic and IT skills that allow for international openness;
- knowledge of the non-technical implications of professional practice.
These skills are developed during the regular training activities and through various moments of discussion and comparison in group work and in the various occasions of meeting with representatives of the world of work (conferences, guided tours, etc.).
The verification of communication skills is carried out through the written and/or oral tests provided for the profit exams and for the other training activities, in particular through the final test.
V - Learning ability: At the end of the training process, the student will have acquired the awareness of the need for continuous learning, to be undertaken independently throughout his working life.
He will also have acquired the ability to:
- keep his knowledge of the technical regulatory framework of reference for the professional sector in which he operates up to date;
- independently acquire new technical and scientific knowledge relating to the subjects of the course itself, starting from the scientific and technical literature in the specific sector.
These skills are mainly developed during the individual study of the topics covered in the lessons and exercises. The development of the final degree thesis also provides, in most cases, for the autonomous consultation of the technical and scientific literature in the sector.
The verification of learning skills is carried out through the written and/or oral tests provided for the profit exams and for the other training activities, in particular through the final test.
Function in a work context:
Function in a work context:
The professional figure of the mechanical engineer requires the technical-scientific knowledge, skills and competences necessary to interpret, describe, formulate and solve the complex problems that typically arise in an industrial context.
Master's graduates in Mechanical Engineering acquire in the training course knowledge of the main characteristics of the methods, techniques, systems and most advanced tools used in the processes of the industry in general. These skills can also be expressed in freelance or employed activities within manufacturing or service companies, or in public administration. The degree prepares for the profession of engineer, section A, industrial sector, mechanical specialization.
Considering the employment commitments that have affected Master's graduates in Mechanical Engineering in recent years, the following employment opportunities can be identified in an industrial context: mechanical and electromechanical industries; aerospace and automotive industries; public and private bodies operating in the sector of supply and management of traditional and alternative energy resources; companies and businesses producing industrial products and complex and innovative systems, also in the biomedical and mechatronic fields; companies that deal with the production and conversion of energy; plant engineering companies; companies that develop and produce systems for automation, robotics and special machines; manufacturing companies and service companies for the design and development of capital and consumer goods; manufacturing companies in which the graduate is also employed in managerial roles for the maintenance and management of complex machinery in production lines and departments; industries and research bodies operating in the automotive sector and related components; companies operating in the thermotechnology sector. More generally, the professional figure in question finds employment in the numerous industrial sectors in which the skills typical of the mechanical engineer find application.
Competencies associated with the function:
Competencies associated with the function:
The Master Mechanical Engineer is able to solve, often in an innovative way, complex and interdisciplinary problems in which technical-functional and economic needs interact. Sufficient cultural knowledge is required to address and solve problems related to the design and development of products, mechanical systems, machines and energy systems, and technological processes. The skills necessary for the conduct and management of complex production activities and related processes and plants are also required.
The skills associated with the function of the Master Mechanical Engineer require the skills necessary to interact with professional figures of different cultural backgrounds, to lead group work and to operate within a company organization with autonomy and flexibility, in compliance with professional ethics.
The ability to manage professional relationships and those related to business activities, even at an international level, is also required.
Graduates in the Master's Degree course in Mechanical Engineering must therefore:
- have in-depth knowledge of the theoretical-scientific aspects of mathematics and other basic sciences and be able to use this knowledge to interpret and describe complex engineering problems or those requiring an interdisciplinary approach;
- have in-depth knowledge of the theoretical-scientific aspects of engineering, both in general and in depth with respect to those of mechanical engineering;
- be able to design, plan, design and manage complex and/or innovative systems, processes and services;
- be able to design and manage experiments of high complexity;
- have contextual knowledge and transversal skills;
- have knowledge in the field of company organization (corporate culture) and professional ethics;
- be able to use fluently, in writing and orally, at least one language of the European Union in addition to Italian, with reference also to disciplinary lexicons.
Professional status conferred by the degree:
Employment opportunities:
The employment opportunities for Master's graduates in Mechanical Engineering are to be expected both in manufacturing or service companies, in public administrations and in research bodies, depending on the areas of training chosen, and in freelance work. The course in fact prepares for the profession of engineer, section A, industrial sector, mechanical specialization.
