INFORMATION ON STUDY PLANS AND COURSES General information relating to the current academic year. Duration: 2 years. Degree program: 2022. Status: Open. Credits: 120 CFU. Language: English. Type: MASTER'S DEGREES. Regulations: D.M. 270/2004. Degree class: LM-25 - Master's Degree in Automation Engineering. Admission: Open Admission. Location: L'Aquila - University of L'Aquila. Department: DEPARTMENT OF ENGINEERING AND INFORMATION AND MATHEMATICS. Website: https://www.disim.univaq.it/degree.php?section=iscritti. Admission requirements. Mandatory qualifications: [TSS]. Upper Secondary School Diploma. Optional qualifications (choose from the following): [TSS + L2]. Bachelor's Degree: [TS + TSS]. Foreign qualification. Dates and deadlines. Online registration: 18/07/2024 - 20/12/2024. Deadline for submitting self-certification: 17/07/2024 - 20/12/2024. Deadline for choosing the course online: 18/07/2024 - 19/07/2024. Roles. Study plan approval manager: STEFANO DI GENNARO. President: STEFANO DI GENNARO. Program, texts and objectives. Official language(s) of teaching and assessment: ENGLISH. Specific learning objectives. The Master's Degree in Engineering of Control and Automation Systems aims to train professionals with extensive and solid skills in Information Engineering, through which they can understand, manage and contribute to the innovation of systems for automation, operating safely in national and international contexts. The Degree Course pursues the objectives characterizing the Class, training designers of automatic control systems and systems for industrial automation, for the energy transition and for electric mobility. To appropriately pursue the specific learning objectives, the Course of Studies will be structured in curricula that provide specific skills for the training of these designers and that represent distinct declinations of the unitary project. As a designer of automatic control systems, the graduate in Engineering of Control and Automation Systems will have in-depth knowledge and understanding of topics such as: modeling, identification, analysis, control and optimization of systems, in complex contexts, such as robotics or dedicated electronic devices ('embedded'), and will have excellent skills in applying this knowledge and skills in order to design, manage and supervise automated control systems. As a designer in the field of industrial automation and energy transition, the graduate in Engineering of Control and Automation Systems will acquire advanced design skills in Information Engineering, including automatic control, artificial intelligence and machine learning, in the technologies of Electrical Energy Systems, in Computer Science and Industrial Communications, and will have knowledge and skills in the field of power electronic converters, machines and electrical drives for industrial applications, for electric propulsion and for the generation of electrical energy from renewable sources; models and methods for the analysis, simulation and control of electrical, electromechanical and electrochemical systems that control energy, both in deterministic and stochastic contexts; techniques of artificial intelligence and machine learning for Industry 4.0 and for the advanced control of energy systems; techniques for the design and programming of distributed and embedded information systems for industrial applications; systems and techniques for communications in industrial, smart grid and automotive environments. Finally, as a designer in the field of electric mobility, the training of the graduate in Engineering of Control and Automation Systems will be aimed at acquiring advanced knowledge and skills in Information Engineering, and in particular the graduate will have knowledge and operational skills relating to topics of modeling, identification, analysis and synthesis of controllers, optimization, implementation of controllers on dedicated digital devices (embedded), and electrical technologies for mobility in the 'automotive' field, such as control of electric motors, power actuators, batteries, energy optimization of the vehicle system. By favoring an interdisciplinary approach, and pursuing a method in which future designers are placed at the center of the training process, in which teaching and assessment are not two distinct entities, but are closely and continuously connected, with a measurement of the learning process throughout the training phase through formal and informal assessment methods, the Course of Studies will allow future designers to acquire knowledge and skills with: - appropriate mathematical insights; - extensive knowledge of the automation sector for all curricula, with appropriate declination of knowledge in other sectors characterizing the class, appropriate for each curriculum; - solid knowledge of the theoretical-scientific and application aspects of the sciences of engineering, electrical and electronic systems used in the generation, distribution and use of electrical energy for the control of energy and energy efficiency. The programs of the characterizing teachings developed by the Course of Studies and aimed at achieving the aforementioned skills, abilities and competencies concern: - models and methods for the analysis and simulation of systems in both deterministic and stochastic contexts; - techniques for data analysis and filtering; - models and techniques for static and dynamic optimization; - computer modeling and simulation of dynamic systems; - analysis and control of robotic systems; - modeling and control algorithms for hybrid systems; - methods for implementing control algorithms on dedicated systems (embedded); - analysis and design of power electronic converters for automation and for the control of energy produced from renewable sources, distribution networks and electrical systems for mobility. Dublin descriptors: I - Knowledge and understanding. The graduate of this Course of Studies (CdS) must have knowledge and understanding of the main methodologies and technologies, including advanced ones, necessary to be able to correctly describe and model engineering problems that require typical solutions of the expert in Control and Automation Systems Engineering. To this end, the necessary knowledge to understand, analyze and design solutions to the typical problems of Control and Automation Systems Engineering is provided by a significant number of credits provided in the characterizing sectors. Furthermore, in order to rigorously formulate, through appropriate mathematical models, the problems that such a graduate will be called upon to solve, and to be able to understand problems of various kinds in the field of Information Engineering, the acquisition of appropriate mathematical knowledge and the various related engineering branches is foreseen. Furthermore, thanks to the elective courses provided, the student can deepen the engineering topics that he/she considers most interesting. Finally, the student can complete his/her training through the knowledge to be acquired with further training activities provided for internships and traineeships at companies, public or private bodies, professional orders, as well as appropriate professional courses held by company professionals, in which the knowledge and skills acquired during the course of study are tested on specific company topics. The verification of knowledge and understanding skills is carried out in an organic manner within the framework of all the assessment methods provided for by the individual courses of the study program. II - Ability to apply knowledge and understanding. The graduate of this CdS will be able to apply the knowledge and understanding acquired to achieve the following objectives: - be able to formulate real problems through mathematical models, and be able to identify the most appropriate model for the problem at hand (static or dynamic model, stochastic or deterministic, continuous or discrete); - be able to analyze the requirements for control and automation systems, and evaluate compliance with the requirements and specifications; - be able to design and implement estimation and control systems; - be able to build mathematical models of physical systems for the simulation and verification of control algorithms, with particular reference to industrial problems; - be able to implement the hardware and software of control systems for energy production and systems for industrial automation; - be able to identify and use problem-solving algorithms, define and evaluate innovative algorithms. These objectives are achieved both by providing solid methodological foundations by means of teachings of a more theoretical nature, and by proposing project activities to students, thanks to a certain number of teachings that provide for practical examination methods in which the students, gathered in working groups, must carry out a project activity that involves the realization, or the computer simulation, of control algorithms for the various problems that arise in the interdisciplinary contexts where automation solutions are required, such as those that arise in an industrial environment (electrical machines and drives for industrial applications, for electric propulsion and for the generation of electrical energy from renewable sources, power electronic converters, electrical systems, energy systems, electromechanical and electrochemical systems that control energy, etc.). III - Autonomy of judgment. Thanks to the solid methodological and disciplinary preparation, as well as the laboratory activities, the graduates will acquire the ability to analyze the results of projects, experiments or simulations, and will be able to evaluate the adequacy of a certain model or a certain procedure or a certain system. This will allow them to interact with other professional figures and to make decisions to solve the problems in the context of Control and Automation Systems Engineering. The achievement of this objective is delegated, in particular, to the preparation and writing of the final degree thesis, which must be the result of a personal re-elaboration of the curricular contents learned. The verification of learning and autonomy of judgment is carried out through written and/or oral tests, provided for the passing of the exams of the individual courses of the study program, through the examination tests of the disciplines that provide for a project activity and, for the other training activities, through the final test. IV - Communication skills. During the course of study, through the examination tests and the preparation of the final test, the graduates acquire the appropriate language to express themselves verbally, in writing and in multimedia form, on the disciplinary issues, both at a general and specialist level. This communication skill will be continuously verified in the examination tests, and in particular in the final test. The ability to understand and express oneself, at least in one's own technical-scientific context, will also be required. These skills are developed during the regular training activities and through various moments of discussion and comparison (seminars, conferences, guided tours, etc.). The verification of communication skills is carried out through the written and/or oral tests provided for the exams and for the other training activities, in particular through the final test. V - Learning ability. The graduates must update and assimilate the technological innovations in the field of information and automation engineering, train collaborators, participate in research and development groups in the information and automation industry, and contribute to basic training in the information and automation sector. These learning skills are developed mainly during the individual study of the topics covered in the lectures and exercises. The development of the degree thesis involves an autonomous elaboration of technical and scientific literature in the field. The verification of learning skills is carried out through the written and/or oral tests provided for the exams and for the other training activities, through the project activities in some courses, and through the final test. Function in a working context. Function in a working context: This Course of Studies aims to train the professional figure of an engineer of control and automation systems. The main functions that this professional figure will perform, depending on the specific skills acquired in the different curricula in which the Course of Studies will be structured, are those of a control systems engineer, an engineer in the field of industrial automation and energy transition, an engineer in the field of electric mobility. These functions are appropriately declined depending on the different working contexts. Competencies associated with the function. Competencies associated with the function: The graduate in Control and Automation Systems Engineering trained in this Course of Study is an expert capable of analyzing problems and situations in interdisciplinary contexts where automation solutions are required. Furthermore, he/she will have high and diversified skills in the field of Information Engineering, through which he/she can successfully face the main present and future challenges of the industrial automation, energy transition and electric mobility sectors, crucial in the ecological transition in the sustainable mobility sector. More specifically, the graduate in Control and Automation Systems Engineering is an expert capable of analyzing problems and situations in interdisciplinary contexts where automation solutions are required. He/she can define the requirements and specifications of design for automation devices (dedicated microprocessor systems, robotic systems, control or monitoring systems, etc.). He/she can design and evaluate automation solutions also through computer simulations. The strong methodological preparation that characterizes him/her allows him/her to explore innovative automation solutions. This engineer can also perform functions of management of automation systems, fully understanding the mechanisms of operation. He/she will have the ability to analyze the quality and performance of the systems, to identify any problems and critical issues and to propose solutions. In his/her function as an engineer of control systems, the graduate in Control and Automation Systems Engineering will be able to use modern techniques and tools for the efficient design of components, systems and processes typical of automation, also making use of skills in the definition of mathematical models for the analysis and simulation of processes and control systems. He/she may also have functions of verification and validation of the performance of automatic systems, conduct experiments and analyze and interpret the data. The knowledge provided by the courses offered allows the graduate thus trained to analyze and understand automation and control systems designed and implemented by others, and to critically evaluate their adequacy in relation to the application, quality and performance. The acquired knowledge will allow him/her to analyze and understand problems of industrial interest and to propose automatic solutions, defining the models to be used in the phase of: - design and programming of automated or robotic systems; - design of continuous or event-driven automatic control systems; - design and development of embedded systems; - sales and assistance of automation systems. In the field of energy transition and industrial transformation, according to the "Industry 4.0" paradigm in which the knowledge required for automation engineers is changing rapidly and significantly, with more specialized skills in the enabling technologies related to the domain of information technologies, the graduate in Control and Automation Systems Engineering is trained as a new high-level professional, with high and diversified skills in the field of Information Engineering, through which he/she can successfully face the main present and future challenges of the industrial automation and energy transition sectors. In his/her function as an engineer of intelligent systems for the automation and control of energy systems, the graduate in Control and Automation Systems Engineering acquires, with rigorous methodology and also from an application point of view, the most advanced skills of Information Engineering, necessary to successfully perform the profession of automation engineer specialized in the control of energy systems. To achieve these objectives and in order to favor an interdisciplinary approach, the training path develops: - appropriate mathematical insights; - solid knowledge of the theoretical-scientific aspects of the sciences of engineering, with particular attention to that of information; - solid knowledge of Automation, the technologies of Electrical Energy Systems, Computer Science and the Technologies for Communication. In his/her function as an engineer of control systems in the field of electric mobility, crucial in the ecological transition in the sustainable mobility sector, the graduate in Control and Automation Systems Engineering is an expert in electric propulsion systems, with advanced knowledge in the sector that makes him/her ready for the imminent challenges of electric mobility. Such a graduate acquires not only a solid training in the main areas of control and electric vehicles, but also solid knowledge in the components of electric vehicles and an advanced specialization in energy storage systems, control of the electric propulsion system, control in electric mobility, that is, in the integrated systems of control systems for electric mobility. To this end, the student is trained to be an expert capable of analyzing the problems related to mobility and the components of electric vehicles and to analyze them in interdisciplinary contexts where the skills of automation are needed in relation to electric mobility. He/she can therefore define the requirements and specifications of design for automatic devices for electric mobility, and knows how to evaluate and compare the different methodological and technological solutions available for this purpose. Such a graduate combines methodological aspects with the technological aspects to be implemented in innovative solutions in the field of electric mobility. The graduate in Control and Automation Systems Engineering trained in this Course of Study will be able to: - analyze the needs of customers and the related problems, define the requirements and specifications of design for applications and automatic systems (such as dedicated embedded systems, robotic systems, control or monitoring systems, etc.); - be able to use modern techniques and tools for the efficient design of components, systems and processes typical of automation, also making use of skills in the definition of mathematical models for the analysis and simulation of processes and control systems; - may have functions of verification and validation of the performance of automatic systems, conduct experiments and analyze and interpret the data; - be able to understand and manage complex automatic systems, analyzing their quality, possibly identifying critical issues and proposing solutions. Finally, as skills and abilities common to all the functions described above, the graduate in Control and Automation Systems Engineering has skills that can be applied to a much wider range of other engineering and economic contexts. Such a graduate can in fact be employed in various industrial and economic sectors, given the relevance of the training for today's high-tech companies, in which the ICT component is becoming increasingly important. Such a graduate acquires in fact skills relating to: - in-depth scientific and technical knowledge of control engineering and the ability to effectively use this knowledge; - the ability to work both independently and in multidisciplinary groups, interacting effectively with specialists from various fields; - the ability to communicate effectively in an international context; - the ability to adopt the most appropriate methodologies for the problems at hand and to select the technological components necessary to implement the proposed solution; - the ability to transfer high-tech methodologies from the university to the industry. Professional status conferred by the degree. Career opportunities: There are numerous career opportunities for the graduate in Control and Automation Systems Engineering. The main career opportunities for the graduate in Control and Automation Systems Engineering are represented both by industries, in particular in technologically advanced sectors that produce products that include dedicated control subsystems or automation components (such as logic and control units, electronic control units, dedicated systems, data acquisition and processing units), and by industries, companies or bodies in different sectors that operate or provide services through the use of systems for information processing and automation (for example, in the field of production and distribution of goods and services, energy, public administration, finance, communications, transport, maintenance, quality control). Among the main sectors of companies interested in graduates in Control and Automation Systems, there are: electronics, electromechanical, automotive, aerospace, energy, chemical, machinery and equipment for automation, computer components, measuring instruments, bioengineering. In his/her function as a designer of intelligent systems for the automation and control of energy systems, the main career opportunities for the graduate in Control and Automation Systems Engineering are in companies operating in technologically advanced sectors that design, produce and/or manage systems for automation and/or for the control of energy, electronic industries, companies and bodies operating in many sectors that operate and/or provide services with a high technological content, using advanced and complex energy systems, companies operating in the production and distribution of electricity, including from renewable sources, in public administration, in finance, in transport, in maintenance, in quality control. In his/her function as a designer of control systems in the field of electric mobility, the main career opportunities for the graduate in Control and Automation Systems Engineering are represented by industries, in particular those in technologically advanced sectors that produce products that include control subsystems in the electric and hybrid automotive field (logic and control units, electronic control units, dedicated systems, data acquisition and processing units), with national and international industrial prospects.

Program, texts and objectives: Official language(s) of teaching and assessment: ENGLISH
Degree awarded: Master's Degree in MATHEMATICAL ENGINEERING
Specific learning objectives:
The evolution of the scientific, technological and economic context requires professionals capable of tackling increasingly complex problems with an integrated approach between mathematical modeling and the use of computational resources.
The Master's Degree course in Mathematical Engineering meets this challenge and aims to train graduates with a broad multidisciplinary profile and characterized by solid theoretical-methodological preparation in mathematical modeling and scientific computing.
The solid theoretical training will be accompanied and made concrete by knowledge and experience in at least one application domain, in the field of engineering or science, and integrated with the ability to communicate and interact with experts in areas of engineering, physics and natural sciences, economics and social sciences. Internships and thesis work in research laboratories and companies will constitute a further element of training, allowing students to put into practice the problem-solving skills and knowledge acquired.
The learning objectives of the study program are as follows:
- to be able to address complex problems in a multidisciplinary context in a flexible but rigorous manner, through the construction of mathematical models, and their numerical solution using computational resources for scientific computing;
- to be able to evaluate which solution techniques and computational and technological tools to use, developing an engineering approach aimed at solving a problem in the most efficient way possible;
- to be able to communicate and interact with experts in at least one application domain, understanding the main issues and the specific language.
Graduates of the study program will have the training that will allow them to successfully enter the world of business, or to continue their studies in a doctoral program in modeling and computational fields.
The courses offered during the program are organized into various areas:
- Theoretical training: completion of basic mathematical and engineering training;
- Mathematical modeling, aimed at deriving, starting from the application problem, the mathematical model suitable for describing the phenomenon and analyzing the solutions from a qualitative and quantitative point of view;
- Numerical simulation, aimed at describing the methods of numerical approximation and integration and the methodologies for representing the numerical solution;
- Scientific computing: courses in this area will provide knowledge on the hardware and software technology of scientific computing, on advanced and parallel programming, on the management of large amounts of data, as well as knowledge of the design of efficient algorithms.
- Applications: courses will be provided in various application areas, both introductory to the issues of the area, and on the application to this area of the methodological knowledge acquired.
The study paths will give different emphasis to the methodological aspects, creating professional figures more focused on scientific computing or more oriented to modeling in engineering and science. In the second year, the student will acquire knowledge in a specific application area among those proposed by the course and the ability to apply the methodological tools in that area, both through specific courses and in the internship and thesis work.
Dublin Descriptors: I - Knowledge and understanding: At the end of the training process, the student will acquire:
- an in-depth knowledge and a clear understanding of the methodological foundations of mathematical engineering;
- the desire to study and the ability to generally use the principles and methods of Mathematics and Physics;
- the sensitivity to adapt their use to the specific difficulties of the problem to be solved, the desired accuracy of the solution, also from a technological point of view, and the sustainable investment of time and money.
The methodological training and the information necessary to enable the student to acquire the knowledge indicated above are distributed in a coordinated and progressive manner within the courses and other training activities offered by the study program. In particular, the methodological foundations and the principles of mathematics and physics are acquired within the mathematics, physics and computer science courses (Mathematical Analysis, Numerical Analysis, Mathematical Physics), while the aspects relating to their use in concrete problems are mainly dealt with in the engineering disciplines (Automatic Control, Information Processing Systems, Fluid Dynamics) and in mathematical disciplines with a more applied character, in particular in the field of Numerical Analysis. The verification of knowledge and understanding skills is carried out in an organic manner within the framework of all the assessments provided for in the study program.
II - Ability to apply knowledge and understanding: At the end of the training process, the student will have acquired the ability to:
- design/realization of models, both through courses relating to mathematical disciplines (Mathematical Analysis, Mathematical Physics), and through engineering courses, in particular in the field of Fluid Dynamics;
- management of complex systems, in particular through the courses in the fields of Automatic Control and Information Processing Systems;
- formulate and solve problems in new and emerging areas of their specialization, in particular in the aspects related to scientific computing and "big data", through courses in the fields of Numerical Analysis and Information Processing Systems;
- perform a linking function between engineers with traditional training and experts from other disciplines, thanks in particular to the coexistence in the path of basic training activities in mathematical disciplines, with an eye to the possible applications of the latter, and engineering training activities with a strong modeling character.
The verification of the ability to apply knowledge and understanding is carried out through the written and/or oral tests provided for the profit exams, in particular through the exam tests of the disciplines that provide for a design activity and, for the other training activities, through the final test.
III - Autonomy of judgment: At the end of the training process, the student will have acquired the ability to manage the complexity typical of the problems of Mathematics and Engineering in the development phase of all design, implementation and management activities of complex systems. They must therefore be able to formulate judgments and critical evaluations even on the basis of limited or incomplete information.
Specific skills must be developed in the field of design: the ability to use their knowledge to design solutions to complex, even unknown or interdisciplinary problems; creative ability for the development of innovative and original approaches; ability to interact with social and cultural processes; ability to operate in conditions of uncertainty.
The preparation and writing of the final degree thesis, which must be configured as the result of a personal re-elaboration of the curricular contents learned, is delegated to this objective in particular.
The verification of autonomy of judgment is carried out through the written and/or oral tests provided for the profit exams, in particular through the exam tests of the disciplines that provide for a design activity and, for the other training activities, through the final test.
IV - Communication skills: At the end of the training process, the student will have developed:
- the ability to communicate in a clear and well-reasoned manner the process and design choices, as well as the scientific orientations underlying them, to mathematical and/or engineering interlocutors;
- the ability to manage relationships with the plurality of subjects, mathematical and/or engineering, involved in the development of the systems of interest;
- communication skills both towards the international scientific community and towards the different social components, even if not competent;
- the ability to coordinate an interdisciplinary group;
- linguistic skills that allow for international openness.
These skills are developed during the regular training activities provided for, for some of which a presentation in front of an interdisciplinary commission is required.
The verification of communication skills is carried out through the written and/or oral tests provided for the profit exams and for the other training activities, in particular through the final test.
V - Learning ability: At the end of the training process, the student will have acquired:
- awareness of the need for continuous learning, to be undertaken independently throughout their working life;
- the ability to independently acquire new technical and scientific knowledge relating to the topics of the course itself, starting from the scientific and technical literature in the specific sector.
These skills are mainly developed during the individual study of the topics covered in the lectures and exercises. The development of the master's thesis also involves consulting the technical and scientific literature in the sector.
The verification of learning skills is carried out through the profit tests and for the other training activities, in particular through the final test.
Function in a work context:
Function in a work context:
Graduates in the Master's Degree courses in the class combine in-depth knowledge of the theoretical-scientific aspects of mathematics and other basic sciences, with particular reference to physics, with advanced knowledge of the theoretical-scientific aspects of engineering in general.
They have the advanced skills to deal with the experimental, computational, technological, economic, epistemological problems connected with the construction, verification of validity and use of models; they are therefore able to use this knowledge and skills to identify, interpret, describe, formulate and solve engineering problems, even complex ones. They also have knowledge in the field of business organization (corporate culture) and professional ethics.
Skills associated with the function:
Innovation and advanced design, in particular with regard to the definition and validation of models and calculation procedures, with particular reference to one or more technological sectors. Graduates in Mathematical Engineering may carry out functions of high responsibility in development and design centers, public and private, in the advanced technological sectors of industry, computing laboratories and companies that provide data processing and development of numerical calculation codes for industry.
Professional status conferred by the degree:
Job opportunities:
The main job opportunities concern:
- engineering companies dedicated to both consulting and research and development activities;
- public companies or bodies for the management of services;
- manufacturing companies that produce and integrate complex systems;
- companies that produce software dedicated to modeling and simulation;
- research institutes and laboratories in the field of engineering and applied mathematics.

Program, texts and objectives: Official language(s) of teaching and assessment: ENGLISH
Degree awarded: Master's Degree in MATHEMATICAL MODELLING
Specific learning objectives:
The proposed "Mathematical Modelling" degree program (LM44 class) is international and inter-university in nature. It stems from the ten-year experience of the Erasmus Mundus program "MathMods - Mathematical Modelling in Engineering: Theory, Numerics, Applications". This experience continues in the new Erasmus Mundus program "InterMaths - Interdisciplinary Mathematics" for the four-year period 2021-2024. In the version proposed starting from the academic year 2021-2022, the Master's degree is offered by the Consortium composed of:
- University of L'Aquila
- Vienna University of Technology (Austria)
- University of Hamburg (Germany)
- University of the Côte d'Azur (Nice, France)
- Autonomous University of Barcelona (Spain)
- Hamburg University of Technology (Germany)
The proposed degree program awards a joint degree. The duration of the program is the standard 120 credits over two years. The degree program is entirely taught in English.
The specific objective of the "Mathematical Modelling" Master's degree program is to train a type of engineer who is particularly skilled in the design, development and management of complex models and systems, understood both in the proper sense of Engineering (complex control systems) and in the sense of mathematical modeling (modeling, numerical simulation and optimization of complex systems). To this end, students are first provided with in-depth mathematical skills in areas such as mathematical analysis, numerical analysis, scientific computing, optimization and control theory. These skills are predominantly methodological and cover both the areas characterizing Mathematical, Physical and Computer Sciences and Engineering Sciences, the latter mainly in the disciplinary sectors ING-INF/04 Automatic Control and ING-INF/05 Information Processing Systems. Subsequently, the student will specialize in the use of various methodological approaches aimed at modeling, simulation and control of complex systems, also covering other characterizing sectors in both areas. These methodological approaches include:
- modeling and simulation of continuous media (fluid dynamics, also computational),
- "agent-based" modeling (e.g. aimed at studying emergent behaviors in complex systems or robotics),
- modeling and control on networks,
- advanced optimization (understood both as optimization of control systems and in the proper sense of operations research),
in order to be able to formulate, analyze and simulate complex models and systems in various engineering application contexts.
During their training, students in the degree program will develop not only a taste for studying and the ability to generally apply the principles and methods of Mathematics, but also the sensitivity to adapt their use to the specific difficulties of the problem to be solved, to the desired accuracy of the solution, also from a technological point of view, and to the sustainable investment of time and money.
DESCRIPTION OF THE EDUCATIONAL PATH The didactic organization is conceived according to the following scheme.
1) The first semester takes place for all students at the University of L'Aquila. It is a semester that provides common skills for the various paths that the student can undertake, essentially dedicated to advanced aspects of mathematical theory and, to a lesser extent, to skills in engineering disciplines related to automatic control.
2) The second semester takes place for all students in Vienna (Austria) or Hamburg (Germany). It is a semester that aims to unify the knowledge of the computer science, computational and numerical aspects. It mainly includes content related to numerical analysis and information processing systems.
3) The second year is focused on extremely advanced sectors in the international scientific and technological research world. Each of the partner locations offers courses that reflect its own skills and potential. The specializations offered are consistent with the background acquired during the first year and deepen some of the various methodological approaches listed above. The aim is to activate various specializations, mainly with applications to engineering. These include advanced control and optimization methods with industrial applications, modeling and simulation of complex systems, simulation of deterministic and stochastic models, both discrete and continuous.
At the end of the educational path, the student must write a thesis project, with the help of his/her supervisor, which must then be approved by the degree commission. The local coordinator of the host institution during the thesis period is responsible for assigning a supervisor to the student; however, student proposals in this regard will also be accepted. The topic of the thesis may also concern a problem proposed by a private company. In this case, the company must designate a person in charge who will follow the student's work at the company itself, especially if the thesis activity takes place at their facilities; however, the local coordinator must also assign an academic supervisor to the student, who will be responsible for the progress, adequacy and scientific quality of the thesis.
As this is an international and inter-university excellence degree program, requests for individual study plans will be examined jointly by the three members of the Consortium to ensure that such study plans comply with the regulations in force in the countries of the institutions that will award its degree, which must be assessed by the Consortium itself.
Dublin descriptors: I - Knowledge and understanding Regarding mathematical theory and modeling, the student will acquire knowledge in the following areas:
- advanced ordinary differential equations, with particular regard to nonlinear dynamic systems and bifurcation theory;
- control theory, with particular attention to digital controls and more generally to applications in engineering automatic control;
- functional analysis and partial differential equations, in order to prepare for the study of complex models and systems.
In addition, the student will acquire knowledge of the main numerical schemes used in the field of ordinary and partial differential equations.
Finally, the student will deepen the knowledge base indicated above in methodological and application contexts consistent with the specific specialization chosen.
The verification of knowledge and understanding is carried out in an organic manner within the framework of all the assessments provided for in the study program. In particular, knowledge of mathematical theory and modeling in the three areas mentioned above is acquired through theoretical lessons and exercises, also including in-progress written tests and tutoring activities. The verification of these skills involves written and oral tests. Knowledge of numerical schemes is acquired through lessons and laboratory activities, both in groups and individually. The verification of learning involves written tests and evaluation of projects.
II - Ability to apply knowledge and understanding The mathematical theory acquired is a fundamental prerequisite for tackling the specific specialization chosen and opens the student to the infinite-dimensional point of view, providing him/her with a new concept of "approximation" that potentially opens him/her to the study of advanced numerical calculation, and the basic ingredients of the calculus of variations. In addition, control theory is applied and integrated in the context of more complex models, which may include stochastic phenomena or be distributed on networks.
In the field of numerical methods, the student acquires the sensitivity to adapt the use of the methods learned to the specific difficulties of the problem to be solved, to the desired accuracy of the solution, also from a technological point of view, and to the sustainable investment of time and money.
The student will develop the ability to apply the methods learned in various contexts, including fluid dynamics, also computational, complex control systems, agent-based modeling, stochastic optimization. The methods learned include in particular the derivation, solution and simulation of partial differential equations, stochastic models, combinatorial optimization models, automatic control systems (also on networks), agent-based systems and their emergent behaviors.
At the end of the training period, the student acquires the ability to formulate and manage complex systems and models, with many variables involved, refining the methods of solution and their accuracy depending on the application context and the needs of the moment in the aforementioned fields.
The student will also be able to plan a computational strategy for solving the problem, solve it from a numerical point of view, interpret the results and use them according to the needs dictated by the problem itself.
The verification of the ability to apply knowledge and understanding is carried out through the tests provided for the profit exams. In particular, written and oral tests make it possible to verify that the student has understood the modeling techniques applied to the contexts considered depending on the chosen study path. Project activities allow, in these cases, to verify that the student is able to apply the mathematical modeling skills acquired in the solution of problems not considered during the frontal teaching hours. A fundamental role in verifying the student's ability to apply modeling and numerical simulation skills in a concrete context is played by the final test, which may also be conducted in collaboration with an industrial partner.
III - Autonomy of judgment At the end of the training course, graduates will have acquired a high level of advanced technical knowledge that can be applied to a wide range of professional contexts. This knowledge base is intrinsically interdisciplinary and versatile. It therefore allows to approach the solution of concrete problems by bringing a "new vision" to the problem itself. This aspect commonly manifests itself in the applications of mathematics to contexts of recent development, even not directly related to engineering applications, such as the modeling of "multi-agent" systems, which uses techniques originating from the study of gas kinetics. This example is paradigmatic of the potential impact of a mathematical modeler in an interdisciplinary research team, given his/her ability to "see" problems in an abstract way, decontextualized from their field of application. Another important aspect that characterizes the mathematical modeler is his/her ability to simplify and "break down" a complex problem in order to understand its deepest nature, even at the cost of temporarily making the model "less realistic".
In conclusion, the graduate in "Mathematical Modelling" is characterized by a strong independence of thought. At the same time, he/she contributes with his/her "mathematical" creativity to the understanding of the phenomena that "lie behind a problem", and to their solution through highly innovative and original techniques.
The verification of autonomy of judgment is carried out through all the tests provided for the profit exams. In particular, the final test tests the student's ability to contextualize, in the most efficient and effective way possible, the various modeling approaches and numerical techniques learned to a problem never considered during the course of study, even coming from an application context different from the one considered in the courses attended. In this sense, the student's ability to organize himself/herself in the design and implementation of the three fundamental steps of mathematical modeling in a concrete problem is tested: formulation of the model, numerical simulation, interpretation of the results. His/her ability to simplify the model autonomously is also tested, by separating it from any components deemed not essential for the interpretation of the results.
IV - Communication skills The graduate will have the ability to communicate clearly and convincingly the process and design choices, as well as the scientific orientations underlying them, both to mathematical and more specialized audiences. Therefore, the graduate will have the ability to manage relationships with the plurality of subjects (mathematicians and/or graduates in applied sciences) involved in the formulation, development and application of the models of interest.
Given the strongly international nature of the degree program, the graduate will also have communication skills both towards the international scientific community and towards the different social components, even if not competent, and will be able to coordinate an interdisciplinary group, also thanks to the varied linguistic/cultural/social knowledge that he/she will acquire during the training course in the different locations attended.
The verification of communication skills is carried out through all the exam tests that include an oral test, in particular for those courses that provide for individual projects that are discussed through seminars. In these cases, the student's ability to organize a presentation in a linear, simple but at the same time effective and exhaustive way is tested. These aspects emerge particularly in the discussion of the thesis drawn up for the award of the degree in the final test. In the tests that provide for public presentations, and in the final test, the student's linguistic skills relating to the English language are tested, in particular the fluency of speech and the ability to master the technical English relating to the subject studied.
V - Learning ability The proposed training course is strongly oriented towards research (also applied) and advanced training, so at the end of it the graduate will have acquired the awareness of the need for continuous learning, to be undertaken independently throughout his/her working life.
Especially during the thesis activity, students develop the ability to independently acquire new technical and scientific knowledge relating to the topics of interest from the scientific and technical literature in the specific sector.
In particular, the student learns the ability to research a specific topic by consulting specialized literature.
The verification of learning skills is carried out through all the exam tests (written and/or oral) provided for in the training course, with particular reference to the tests that provide for a project activity. The final test makes it possible to test the student's ability to approach the research of advanced scientific material, case studies in the literature, innovative methods and models that can help him/her in the implementation of his/her thesis project.
Function in a working context:
Function in a working context:
Formulation and study (analytical and numerical) of mathematical models in the applied sciences, with particular regard to the areas of optimization (also stochastic), fluid dynamics (also computational) and mechanics of continua.
The professional figure deals with:
- formalizing mathematical problems of the applied sciences (in particular in the aforementioned areas) in collaboration with experts in research and development and production optimization;
- developing and analyzing, also through numerical simulations, the related mathematical models.
Graduates usually acquire greater skills through post-graduate/doctoral research courses in mathematics and/or the applied sciences.
Skills associated with the function:
Skills associated with the function:
- In-depth knowledge of mathematics and other basic sciences, as well as the theoretical-scientific-modeling aspects of the applied sciences
- Advanced skills to deal with experimental, computational, technological problems, related to the formulation, validation and use of mathematical models, in particular in the areas mentioned.
Professional status conferred by the degree:
Employment opportunities:
- companies dedicated to both consulting and research and development activities;
- companies or public bodies for the management of services;
- manufacturing companies that produce and integrate complex systems;
- research institutes and laboratories in the field of mathematics and the applied sciences.

Program, texts and objectives: Official language(s) of teaching and assessment: ITALIAN, ENGLISH. Specific learning objectives: Graduates of the Master's Degree Course in Structural and Construction Engineering have a thorough understanding of the theoretical and scientific aspects of mathematics and other basic sciences and are able to use this knowledge to interpret and describe complex engineering problems, adopting a systemic and integrated, multidisciplinary approach. In this context, the professionals that this Degree Course aims to train apply existing knowledge in the field of design, construction, refurbishment and restoration of structures, buildings and civil works on a building scale, also considering aspects of economic, energy and environmental sustainability; they deal with assessing the risks associated with natural events in relation to the aspects concerning the design, planning, construction, refurbishment, restoration, management and monitoring of structures and buildings; they adopt advanced technological solutions, also for the purpose of a progressive transformation in a physical-digital sense of existing systems; they design and manage experiments of high complexity, as well as physical, mathematical and numerical models for the simulation and design of complex civil works; they oversee and direct these activities.
In particular, the choice of specific courses allows the acquisition of skills related to:
- the programming and management of complex systems;
- the planning, design, construction, management and monitoring of civil and industrial structures, with particular reference to the protection of the seismic risk of the building and monumental heritage;
- the assessment of the safety and functionality requirements of civil works, also taking into account the degradation and aging processes of the components and exposure to extreme events of natural and anthropogenic origin;
- the maintenance, restoration and redevelopment of the building heritage, with particular reference to the ability to adapt works and systems of civil engineering to the evolution of the surrounding conditions and service requirements, taking into account short, medium and long-term dynamics;
- the enhancement and redevelopment of the building heritage;
- the modeling and management of structures and buildings and their life cycle through modern representation techniques;
- the advanced design in the field of support and foundation structures.
The achievement of these objectives is pursued through a training activity structured in teaching modules, which include classroom lessons, laboratory exercises and individual study or practice, and which give rise to credits that the student obtains by passing exams. The activities are carried out in such a way as to stimulate the aptitude for teamwork and communication.
The training path for obtaining the Master's Degree in Structural and Construction Engineering therefore provides for training activities, also delivered in English, distributed in a balanced way in the subjects relating to the completion of specific training in the disciplines characterizing Civil Engineering and the integration with related cultural areas.
In particular, two areas of in-depth study are planned:
- Area for in-depth study of basic training: aimed at corroborating and implementing the knowledge and methodological tools in the disciplines characterizing Civil Engineering and the integration with related cultural areas.
- Area for in-depth study of engineering training: aimed at providing the knowledge and methodological tools in the field of design, construction, management and monitoring of both ordinary and special structures.
The disciplines included in the training path focus on the typical sectors of Civil Engineering, such as Seismic Zone Construction, Structural Design and Prefabrication, Foundations, Concrete Technology, Theory of Structures, Risk Assessment, etc.; depending on the choices made, these activities are accompanied by the study of other disciplines such as Structural Dynamics, Stability and Bifurcation of Structures, Bridge Construction, Masonry Construction, Timber Construction, Finite Element Structural Analysis, Steel Structures, Viscoelastic Structural Analysis, Technical Architecture, Site Organization, Existing Heritage Restoration, Building Information Modeling, etc.
Dublin descriptors: I - Knowledge and understanding: Master's graduates in Structural and Construction Engineering will develop skills and understanding that, on the one hand, will extend and consolidate those acquired in the basic disciplines during the first-level degree course. On the other hand, they will be able to generate original ideas and successfully address complex engineering problems, especially in innovative contexts and in applied research to structures and civil constructions, with a particular focus on the works that are carried out on the scale of civil buildings. These training objectives will be achieved through classroom lectures, practical exercises and participation in seminars conducted by university professors, guest professors and professionals in the sector. In addition, guided tours of construction sites and places of interest, together with the use of the various departmental laboratories, will complete the training strategy of the Degree Course.
The training path provides for distinctive activities in the disciplinary area of Civil Engineering, with particular reference to the scientific-disciplinary sectors of Science and Technology of Constructions (ICAR/08 and ICAR/09), Technical Architecture (ICAR/10) and Geotechnics (ICAR/07), integrated in a synergistic way and in relation to related cultural areas.
The assessment of knowledge and skills is carried out in an organic way, within the context of all the tests provided for in the study path, which include written and oral exams. During these assessments, both the theoretical preparation and the ability to elaborate, also in a design context, will be analyzed.
II - Ability to apply knowledge and understanding: Master's graduates in Structural and Construction Engineering, thanks to the didactic approach of the course which promotes active participation and the ability of students to elaborate autonomously, will be able to use the knowledge acquired for the design, planning, construction, refurbishment, management and monitoring of materials, structures and buildings. These skills are developed in linear and non-linear contexts, with particular attention to innovative structural and technological components and systems. These skills are acquired through exercises, usually of a monographic and design nature, which also encourage the ability of students to interact in groups, as well as laboratory activities.
The assessment of the ability to apply knowledge and understanding takes place through written and/or oral and/or practical technical tests planned for the exams. This assessment process focuses, in particular, on the tests of the exams of the disciplines that include design activities. For the other training activities, the verification takes place through the final exam.
III - Autonomy of judgment: Master's graduates must possess, at the end of the course of studies, a personal autonomy of judgment regarding the decisions to be taken in the design, planning, construction, refurbishment, management and monitoring of materials, structures and buildings, both in linear and non-linear fields, with particular attention to innovative structural and technological components and systems. They will therefore be able to take autonomous decision-making responsibilities and actively participate in the design process in interdisciplinary contexts.
Advanced critical thinking skills will also be developed through the progressive involvement in research activities, through the analysis and interpretation of experimental data, theoretical results and models.
During the training process, the student will acquire the ability to solve advanced engineering problems, through the development of design applications, mainly in the courses placed in the second year.
The assessment of the ability and autonomy of judgment achieved will be carried out progressively in the exams of the courses, in the development of design applications and in the preparation and discussion of the final degree thesis.
IV - Communication skills: The ability to communicate the objectives and methods of implementation of designs, even complex ones, is essential for effective insertion into the professional world.
It is therefore important for the Master's graduate to possess adequate tools for communication and to have verified their mastery through targeted simulations.
The Master's degree course will therefore provide all the tools to consolidate and further develop the communication skills of students, both written and oral, and communication through graphic representation, as well as through the use of IT and telematic tools.
At the end of the training process, the student will have developed:
- the ability to communicate clearly and convincingly the process and design choices, as well as the scientific orientations underlying them, to specialist and non-specialist interlocutors;
- the ability to manage relationships with the plurality of subjects, specialists and non-specialists, involved in the development of the systems of interest to Civil Engineering, in the sector of structures and constructions (public bodies, companies, design firms, etc.);
- communication skills, also in English, both towards the scientific community and towards the different social components, even if not competent;
- both the ability to operate independently and the ability to operate as a member of a group in which there will be different skills, depending on the needs of the project development;
- the ability to coordinate a group, even with an interdisciplinary character.
These objectives will be pursued through lectures and exercises, also held in English, requiring in particular the students, in the various courses, in the seminars and in the final thesis exam, presentations both oral and written and/or computerized of their work, also through the use of audio-visual means.
The evaluative verifications of the communication skills will take place in the exams, in intermediate tests and seminars, and in the final degree exam.
V - Learning ability: The Master's degree course will provide students, in addition to specific knowledge, a methodological approach to study that will allow them to successfully undertake further studies (Master's and Doctoral degrees) and will enable future professionals to start independently towards a continuous learning process.
The objective of the Degree Course is in fact to offer a method of work, as well as specific knowledge. This objective will be pursued through the alternation of traditional training moments (lectures) with other moments more dedicated to the development of skills in self-organization, critical synthesis and personal research (internships, degree thesis).
The verifications will take place through the exams and the discussion of the final degree exam.
Function in a work context.
Function in a work context:
The professional profile of the graduates is, in particular, characterized by the following functions, without claiming to be exhaustive, in a work context:
- design, construction, management and control of complex building systems;
- planning, design, construction, management and monitoring of civil and industrial structures, with particular reference to the protection of the seismic risk of the building and monumental heritage;
- advanced design and construction of support and foundation works;
- direction of works aimed at the construction of complex civil and industrial structures;
- refurbishment and restoration of building systems;
- coordination of activities aimed at the management and monitoring of structures and buildings in relation to the systems associated with them;
- risk assessment and the effects of natural events such as earthquakes, etc.;
- enhancement and redevelopment of the building heritage;
- analysis and development of innovative structural and technological components and systems;
- modeling of the static and dynamic behavior of materials and structures, in linear and non-linear fields.
The usual activities of the graduate may be carried out in collaboration with other professional figures involved in the civil construction chain (Civil Engineers with different specializations, Environmental and Territory Engineers, Building Engineers, Architects, Planners, etc.), also in a coordinating role.
Skills associated with the function.
Skills associated with the function:
In order to carry out the functions and activities associated with the professional profile, the student in Structural and Construction Engineering will acquire specific knowledge, skills and competencies. In particular, the graduate, by way of example:
- is able to coordinate design, construction, management and monitoring groups of structures, buildings and complex civil works;
- knows and understands from a technical point of view the aspects relating to the effects resulting from the construction of structures and civil works;
- is able to solve complex problems relating to the design, refurbishment and restoration of structures and civil works, also considering the aspects of economic, energy and environmental sustainability;
- is able to assess the risks associated with natural events in relation to the aspects concerning the design, planning, construction, refurbishment, restoration, management and monitoring of structures and buildings;
- is able to adopt advanced technological solutions, also for the purpose of a progressive transformation in a physical-digital sense of existing systems;
- is able to design and manage experiments of high complexity, as well as to use physical, mathematical and numerical models for the simulation and design of constructions and structures;
- is able to adapt his/her action to the evolution of methods, techniques, tools and technologies;
- is able to interact with the other professional figures involved in the civil works and construction chain and to operate in multidisciplinary contexts.
Professional status conferred by the degree.
Employment opportunities:
The professional profile and the employment opportunities expected for graduates in Structural and Construction Engineering are a direct result of consultation with stakeholders and the analysis of sector studies.
The objective of the Degree Course is to train Structural and Construction Engineers who can practice the profession in the fields of Civil Engineering with reference to the design, planning, construction, refurbishment, management and monitoring of materials, structures and buildings, both in linear and non-linear fields, with particular attention to innovative structural and technological components and systems. It is consistent with the University's Strategic Plan 2020-2025, which, among its objectives, aims to promote the quality of the training offer with courses consistent with the needs of the individual and society.
The profession can be classified, as indicated by ISTAT, in the category "Civil engineers and related professions".
It should be noted that access to the profession, as indicated by current legislation, is subject to passing the state exam for the qualification to practice the profession of Engineer, Civil and Environmental Sector.
The employment opportunities concern the typical sectors of Civil Engineering, with particular reference to structures and constructions. The professional fields for graduates range from the classic figure of the freelance engineer employed in medium/large companies, to employment in managerial positions in design companies, construction companies, central and local government bodies, regions and municipalities. In particular, the possible employment opportunities for graduates can be listed, without claiming to be exhaustive, as follows:
- public offices for planning, management and restoration of civil structures;
- companies, bodies, consortia and agencies for the management and control of civil works;
- professional firms operating in the field of design, refurbishment, restoration and monitoring of civil works;
- construction and maintenance companies of civil works.
The continuation of studies in specific research doctoral programs represents a further, albeit particular, employment opportunity for graduates.
