Program, texts and objectives: Official language(s) of teaching and assessment.
ITALIAN, ENGLISH
Degree awarded: Master's Degree in Administration, Economics and Finance
Specific learning objectives:
The Master's Degree in Administration, Economics and Finance aims to provide a solid and in-depth knowledge of business and economic sciences in order to enable the graduate to fully understand the business phenomenon (also in the public sector) in its many aspects (economic, business, financial) and the fundamental economic dynamics.
The Master's Degree provides a systematic ability to analyze the company, both in its structural dimension and in its functional dynamics, as well as the knowledge and methodologies necessary to carry out consulting activities in business administration and management, as well as the free professions in the economic and business area.
The educational path of the Master's Degree in Administration, Economics and Finance is divided into five curricula in order to partially distinguish the aforementioned educational project (always characterized by a solid business and economic preparation, with courses also in the legal and mathematical-quantitative area) in order to allow the student to have, on the one hand, an adequate possibility of choice (always within the indicated educational project) and, on the other hand, a solid and in-depth preparation in a specific area among those of interest to the educational project. This option also allows the student to present himself in the world of work with a robust preparation with regard to the areas chosen by him.
One curriculum is dedicated to the areas of knowledge of accounting, financial statements and the economic and financial management of the company, and to the focus on the themes of planning and control. Consequently, the relative structure of the study path is based in particular on the courses in the business area and in particular of the sector of business economics, as it aims to provide a solid preparation with regard to the disciplines of the sector, albeit integrated with basic notions of the economic, mathematical and legal area. Another curriculum is dedicated to the preparation of a graduate who intends to dedicate himself to the free profession. To this end, a solid and in-depth knowledge of the themes of accounting and financial statements is provided with regard to the carrying out of free professional activities. This curriculum provides for a structure of the study path based in particular on the courses in the business area and in particular of the sector of business economics, as it aims to provide a solid preparation with regard to the disciplines of the sector, albeit integrated with basic notions of the economic, mathematical and legal area.
Another curriculum is dedicated to preparing a graduate who intends to be an expert in management. To this end, a solid and in-depth preparation is offered on the themes of business management, marketing, business organization and human resource management; the study path aims to provide a solid and in-depth knowledge of the themes of management and to focus attention on the themes of business organization and human resource management. This curriculum provides for a structure of the study path based in particular on the courses in the management area and in particular of the sector of business organization and economics and management of companies as it aims to provide a solid preparation with regard to the disciplines of the sector, albeit integrated with basic notions of the economic, mathematical and legal area.
Another curriculum aims to provide a solid and in-depth knowledge of the issues related to economic markets with particular attention to financial markets. To this end, the themes of financial intermediation, in particular banking, and corporate finance, in particular of the company, are particularly deepened with a view to professional insertion in these areas of operation. In addition, the student acquires the necessary ability to analyze economic processes at the level of the economic system, of a single production sector or of a company, in order to enable him to work professionally with public and private bodies that use economic analysis, information and forecasting in their decision-making processes. This curriculum provides for a structure of the study path based in particular on the courses in the economic area and in particular of the sectors of political economy, economic policy, public finance and econometrics, as it aims to provide a solid preparation with regard to the disciplines of the sector, albeit integrated with important courses in the business area, and basic notions of mathematics and the legal area.
Another curriculum aims to develop the skills of the educational project with particular regard to the economics and management of public administrations. To this end, a solid and in-depth knowledge of the issues related to the direction and management of public administrations is provided. The student acquires the necessary ability to analyze the dynamics of operation of public administrations, also in connection with the economic processes in progress, in order to enable him to work professionally with public and private bodies. This curriculum provides for a structure of the study path based in particular on the courses in the legal area (and in particular in the public law area), as it aims to provide a solid preparation with regard to the disciplines of the sector, albeit integrated with important courses in the business and economic area, as well as basic notions of mathematics.
Dublin Descriptors: I - Knowledge and understanding: The Master's Degree graduate in "Administration, Economics and Finance" acquires knowledge and understanding in the business and economic-business area, with important legal and mathematical-quantitative notions, which allow him to know and understand the business and economic dynamics in progress and to face practical and theoretical problems in the aforementioned areas. The methods by which the expected results are achieved are those traditional of university teaching provided through courses ad hoc annually organized according to current regulations and through the dissemination of teaching programs and the texts recommended for the preparation of exams. The methods of verifying the achievement of the expected results consist of an exam for each individual course. The decision on the methods of the exam (written or oral) is left to the teacher in charge of the course who annually, in the exam program, also indicates the methods of carrying out the final test which has the purpose of verifying the achievement of the objectives set with the assignment of the number of credits provided for the individual course and with the awarding of a grade in thirty, attesting to the qualitative level reached by the individual student.
II - Ability to apply knowledge and understanding: The Master's Degree graduate in Administration, Economics and Finance is able to apply, within the professional and work fields, the knowledge acquired and the ability to understand developed during the studies as well as to apply the skills acquired to the theoretical and practical problems that arise in the work activity that he is called upon to carry out.
The methods and teaching tools by which the student acquires the ability to apply knowledge and understanding are those traditional of university teaching provided through courses ad hoc annually organized according to current regulations and through the dissemination of teaching programs and the texts recommended for the preparation of exams, but also the provision of an internship experience. The methods of verifying the achievement of the expected results, also from the point of view of the ability to apply knowledge and understanding, consist of an exam for each individual course, in the drafting of a final report at the end of the internship experience, in an aptitude test with regard to the knowledge of the foreign language. The decision on the methods of the exam (written or oral) is left to the teacher in charge of the course who annually, in the exam program, also indicates the methods of carrying out the final test which has the purpose of verifying the achievement of the objectives set, including the ability to apply knowledge and understanding. The successful completion of the relative test involves the acquisition, by the student, of the number of credits provided for the individual course and with the awarding of a grade in thirty, attesting to the qualitative level reached by the individual student.
III - Autonomy of judgment: The Master's Degree graduate in Administration, Economics and Finance has the ability to integrate the knowledge acquired and to formulate autonomous judgments in the business and economic area with respect to the issues concerning the direction and management of public and private bodies and in the carrying out of free professions.
The Master's Degree graduate has a high degree of autonomy of judgment with regard to the problems that arise for those who hold positions of direction and responsibility in private and public bodies and in the carrying out of free professions.
The possession of the ability of autonomy of judgment is achieved through the preparation and passing of the various exams that make up the Master's Degree course, which also includes the internship activity and a language exam. A thesis is also required, in which the student must demonstrate the ability to reflect, with also original traits on a specific topic.
IV - Communication skills: The Master's Degree graduate in Administration, Economics and Finance has communication skills to communicate information, ideas, problems and solutions to specialist and non-specialist interlocutors in the business and economic-business area in the issues related to the typical problems of the direction and management of public and private bodies as well as in the carrying out of free professions. The Master's Degree graduate has communication skills of the knowledge acquired in order to adequately carry out tasks related to positions of responsibility and direction of private and public bodies in order to develop adequate solutions.
The possession of communication skills is achieved through the preparation and passing of the various exams that make up the Master's Degree course, which also includes the internship activity and a language exam. A thesis is also required, in which the student must demonstrate the ability to reflect, with also original traits on a specific topic.
V - Learning ability: The Master's Degree graduate in Administration, Economics and Finance has learning skills that allow him to continue studying independently or self-directed in the field of business and economic studies.
The possession of learning and self-learning skills is achieved through the preparation and passing of the various exams that make up the Master's Degree course, which also includes the internship activity and a language exam. A thesis is also required, in which the student must demonstrate the ability to reflect, with also original traits on a specific topic.
Function in a work context:
Function in a work context:
The Master's Degree graduate in Administration, Economics and Finance has a systematic ability to analyze the company both in its structural dimension and in its functional dynamics, also with regard to public bodies, financial institutions and the like. Therefore, the Master's Degree graduate can carry out functions of high consultancy, of direction of a company (private or public), of direction of personnel and of management of organizational and/or financial structures, as well as the development of company strategies.
The Master's Degree graduate in Administration, Economics and Finance carries out functions of responsibility within the company or consulting or freelance activities, due to the possession of specific skills with regard to the functions of business administration and control. The professional figure in question has a high level of competence in the field of business and tax consulting and carries out functions related to specialist positions aimed at analyzing the competition and the competitive capacity in any type of organization; managerial positions in profit and non-profit organizations, both in production and services, as well as managerial positions in the field of banking and financial institutions; positions of expert and consultant in the financial field and skills that allow him to hold positions of responsibility in the field of research in national and international bodies and agencies; managerial positions in companies engaged in European and international integration processes, as well as managerial positions in consulting and service companies for the production and commercial activities of companies operating in European and extra-European markets; managerial positions in public administration at national and local level, managerial positions in private and public companies operating in the field of public services and services to the public administration. The skills associated with the performance of the aforementioned functions are those of knowledge of the economic-business disciplines, the economic dynamics and the disciplines of business organization and management, also with regard to the legal and quantitative profiles.
In addition, the introduction of courses taught in English, possibly organized in a specific curriculum, aims to provide a preparation that allows the Master's Degree graduate to acquire a training profile suitable for effectively entering companies, non-profit organizations and institutions that operate on a supranational scale or that aim to extend their activities beyond domestic borders.
Skills associated with the function:
Skills associated with the function:
The skills associated with the aforementioned functions are those of knowledge of the economic-business disciplines, the main economic dynamics and the disciplines of business organization and management, also with regard to the legal and quantitative profiles. The expected professional opportunities are those related to: managerial positions in the private and public sectors; entrepreneurial positions in the industrial, commercial and service sectors; experts and consultants in business administration and management, and freelance certified public accountant and auditor; freelance certified public accountant (after passing the state exam); business consulting; managerial positions in profit and non-profit organizations, both in production and services; managerial positions in the field of banking and financial institutions; positions of expert and consultant in the financial field; positions of responsibility in the field of research in national and international bodies and agencies; managerial positions in companies engaged in European and international integration processes; managerial positions in consulting and service companies for the production and commercial activities of companies operating in European and extra-European markets; managerial positions in public administration at national and local level; managerial positions in private and public companies operating in the field of public services and services to the public administration. The Master's Degree graduate in Administration, Economics and Finance has knowledge and methodologies that allow him to carry out consulting activities for companies, as well as direction and management activities in private and public companies, as well as the carrying out of free professional activities typical of the economic, economic-business, legal-business area.

ITALIAN.
Specific learning objectives.
The Master's Degree in Psychology - class LM-51, qualifies students to practice as a Psychologist (as per articles 1 and 3 of Law 8 November 2021, n. 163).
The Master's Degree in Clinical, Applied Psychology and Intervention aims to train professionals with a solid cultural base and high levels of practical competence, who can perform roles with responsibilities, in accordance with the current regulations, in the fields of clinical and neuropsychological psychology, in contexts such as public and private healthcare organizations, and organizations and institutions providing care and assistance to individuals.
The Master's Degree in Clinical, Applied Psychology and Intervention also provides the theoretical and methodological knowledge necessary to design and conduct research activities, also in collaboration with other specialists, within the University and healthcare and scientific institutions.
The cultural, theoretical and practical profile of the graduate in Clinical, Applied Psychology and Intervention is also suitable for access to higher levels of university and specialist education.
These learning objectives are achieved through advanced training in the disciplines that characterize the LM-51 class (general psychology, psychobiology and physiological psychology, psychometrics, developmental psychology, clinical and dynamic psychology), and are completed with knowledge and skills acquired in related and complementary training activities, which develop specialist aspects of some scientific sectors that do not characterize the LM-51 degree class, but are consistent with the proposed objectives.
In particular, the learning objectives are achieved through an advanced course that includes training based on different areas of learning. These learning areas aim to acquire in-depth knowledge in the field of clinical and applied psychology in different contexts, in the methodological-statistical field and in the field of the psychobiological bases of cognition and behavior.
The learning areas are developed by providing both transversal training between curricula and more specific training for each curriculum. To this end, the learning areas are structured differently, assigning different weights to the scientific-disciplinary sectors that characterize the course. The different training paths also differ in the specificity of some courses related to related disciplines.
The common training will allow the graduate to possess:
- knowledge of the main forms of psychological suffering and rehabilitation interventions;
- in-depth knowledge of the tool of psychological interview and its applications;
- knowledge of the theoretical and methodological foundations of psychotherapeutic approaches;
- knowledge of the main theoretical models of typical and atypical development and their applications;
- knowledge of the methodologies of diagnostic assessment and treatment evaluation;
- in-depth knowledge of the alterations of cognitive functions caused by focal or diffuse lesions or dysfunctions of the central nervous system and their treatments, also in the context of normal and pathological aging.
In addition, the articulation of the Study Course into differentiated paths (curricula) will allow to deepen and integrate the professional aspects acquired in the common part, providing more specific knowledge and skills for some application/occupational areas of the graduate in Clinical, Applied Psychology and Intervention. This objective will be achieved both through some scientific-disciplinary sectors of the areas of the class, which already characterize the common path, but contribute to the specificity of the curriculum, and through areas of the class to which a different weight is given according to the specific skills proposed in the curricula. The specialist nature of the related and complementary activities can also contribute to the different curricular paths.
In particular, the graduate in Clinical, Applied Psychology and Intervention develops a solid scientific and professional preparation through training paths that have a more clinical character or are more focused on different application areas, including the neuroscientific one.
The more clinical character of the training will be characterized, mainly, by cultural and methodological aspects of the disciplines of the field of psychology and clinical psychophysiology (applied to the study of mental disorders, addictions, psychosomatic disorders, sexology, deviance), developmental psychology, and dynamic psychology of groups.
Instead, the application side related to the psychobiological-neuroscientific approach of the training will be mainly characterized by cultural and methodological aspects of the disciplines of the field of general psychology, physiological psychology and development applied to the study of processes of plasticity, cognitive, emotional and evolutionary and states of consciousness, also reserving an adequate space for the methodology of research and data analysis.
The training course provides a certain degree of flexibility in the choice of courses, among the activities included in the University's training offer, in order to integrate, in agreement with the learning objectives of the Course, the knowledge of advanced topics and specialized skills.
In addition, the training course provides, in the Further linguistic knowledge, a course in English, at least at level B2, which guarantees, to the student who does not have these skills upon entry, the achievement of an adequate level of understanding of the English language, with particular reference to the specific vocabulary of the psychological sciences, essential to integrate communication skills in the language most commonly used in the international scientific field.
The learning objectives are enriched with the professional training activities of the Practical Assessment Internship (PAI), internal to the course of study. The PAI consists of practical activities that are contextualized and supervised, which involve direct observation and the performance of activities aimed at situated learning and the development of the procedural and relational skills essential for the exercise of the professional activity. These skills refer to the typical and reserved acts, characterizing the profession of psychologist also in accordance with article 1 of Law 18 February 1989, n. 56, and include the use of the tools for knowledge and intervention for the prevention, diagnosis, rehabilitation and support activities in the psychological field aimed at the person, the group, social organizations and communities as well as activities of experimentation, research and teaching.
Finally, the learning objectives are completed with the practical activities provided for the preparation of the Final Thesis, presented in the final examination. In the preparation of the Final Thesis, the graduate student can contextualize the training experiences listed in the Course and the knowledge and skills acquired, in a laboratory/experimental/application context or in the construction of an original bibliographic research project.
Lessons, laboratory activities, consultation of teaching material, critical analysis and understanding of scientific literature, in-depth study through autonomous bibliographic research of articles and scientific texts with advanced content, open group discussions on topics of the course of study as integral parts of learning methods, as well as intermediate and final verification tests and the preparation/discussion of the Final Thesis, as methods of verification, will contribute to the development/exercise/verification of the ability to learn and deepen, also in an autonomous way, one's own knowledge, autonomy of judgment, aptitude for teamwork, acquisition of mastery and tools for communication and ability to present/transmit/disseminate one's knowledge.
Dublin Descriptors: I - Knowledge and understanding skills: The training course of the Master's Degree in Clinical, Applied Psychology and Intervention is structured in activities that allow the graduate to acquire new knowledge, to develop their understanding skills, and to apply this knowledge to different professional contexts.
Graduates in Clinical, Applied Psychology and Intervention will possess in-depth knowledge of the psychobiological and functional bases of cognitive and emotional activity, and of the mechanisms and processes of normal and pathological cognitive and psycholinguistic development. In addition, they will possess advanced knowledge of the genesis and dynamics of alterations and disorders of cognitive, communicative, emotional activity and behavioral sphere. The master's graduates will also have targeted operational skills for the design, implementation and evaluation of diagnostic, rehabilitation and psychological support interventions in a clinical setting, and for the promotion of psychophysical well-being and health. They will possess skills related to the methodologies of psychological and psychotherapeutic intervention based on scientific evidence, according to different theoretical approaches. They will also be able to use the tools of psychological-clinical assessment (interview, systematic observation of behavior, use of tests) applied to the individual and group clinical process. Finally, they will have methodological skills that will allow them to critically read, understand and use the results of psychological and neuroscientific research to plan and carry out adequate clinical and research activities. This knowledge and understanding skills are acquired through the study of texts with advanced content, scientific articles/reviews or teaching material provided by the teacher, both in the courses of the characterizing disciplines (general psychology, psychobiology and physiological psychology, psychometrics, developmental psychology and education, clinical and dynamic psychology), and in those that fall within the range of related disciplines, differentiated according to the path chosen by the student.
The acquisition of knowledge will be guaranteed by specific and differentiated learning methods, based on lectures (also with computer support), laboratory teaching activities with theoretical/practical lessons, seminar-type activities.
The acquisition of knowledge will be verified by the final examination for each training activity, the use of intermediate tests provided in some teaching/training units, the Practical Assessment Internship activity.
II - Ability to apply knowledge and understanding: Graduates in Clinical, Applied Psychology and Intervention must demonstrate that they are able to apply the knowledge acquired in the design and implementation of interventions focused on the person or groups, also in interdisciplinary contexts, for the promotion of health as well as for the prevention, diagnosis, support and psychological and cognitive rehabilitation.
They will be able to take charge, diagnose and direct to rehabilitation treatment individuals with cognitive alterations due to atypical development, a psychiatric disorder, a brain lesion or a cerebrovascular or degenerative disease.
They will be able to operate in collaboration with other specialists within multidisciplinary teams, providing a specific contribution to the design and implementation of interventions focused on the person or groups. They will also have the ability to use the knowledge acquired to critically analyze the scientific literature in the specific areas of interest, design and carry out research in the field of clinical psychology, applied psychology and neuroscience. The ability to translate the acquired skills into practical terms is strengthened through practical activities integrated with the characterizing and related teachings that allow the student to experience the application of tools for the detection and evaluation of psychological and clinical assessments, to participate in research with assignment of activities for the administration of tasks and evaluation scales, to come into contact with the main methods and techniques of research in behavioral and cognitive neuroscience, and to apply their ability to understand specific, highly advanced scientific content.
The ability to apply the knowledge acquired in the Master's Degree will be verified both through the approval of the practical and/or laboratory activities and, in particular, through the individual work carried out by the student for the preparation of the final examination. In addition, a particularly important moment at the training and professionalizing level will be the Practical Assessment Internship.
III - Autonomy of judgment: The Psychologist is able to elaborate complex analyses and to develop autonomous reflections on specific topics of in-depth study. In addition, he/she is able to formulate autonomous judgments regarding assessments of cognitive, emotional and behavioral functioning.
Autonomy of judgment is favored by a didactic approach aimed at acquiring the ability to exercise, in any work context, full professional autonomy, to assume responsibility for one's own work, even working in collaboration in multidisciplinary teams, to evaluate the quality, effectiveness and efficiency of the interventions implemented.
The Psychologist will therefore be able to formulate assessments based on observational or instrumental data relating to individual or group situations, always taking into account the principles of professional ethics; be able to make choices regarding interventions for cognitive and clinical psychological support, also taking into account the constraints deriving from contextual factors (family, school, hospitals, rehabilitation services); possess critical judgment skills in reading and interpreting the reference scientific literature.
Great importance is given to these aspects both in courses with a more theoretical character, and in methodological courses and in those with a more marked practical and applicative component. The courses present different theoretical and methodological approaches relating to each of the phenomena examined, favoring a critical and open attitude, aimed at identifying the most appropriate approach and tools for solving complex problems related to research, assessment and intervention.
The autonomy of judgment achieved by the student is evaluated in particular through: a) the ability to expose in a critical way, during the profit exams, the different theoretical positions relating to the specific topics covered, and to provide more interpretative hypotheses of the phenomena under examination, proposing the most appropriate methodologies for the evaluation of these hypotheses; b) the level of independence and the ability to work individually during the activity assigned in preparation for the final examination; c) the judgment of suitability of the Practical Assessment Internship.
IV - Communication skills: The Psychologist must be able to communicate effectively with individuals who are in situations of psychological distress and with their families, always referring to the principles of professional ethics; possess the communication skills that allow him/her to contribute with his/her skills to teamwork within multidisciplinary teams; be able to expose in writing and orally, in an effective way and with a language appropriate to different interlocutors, his/her conclusions regarding studies and analyses, clearly explaining his/her reasoning; be able to communicate the results of his/her research activity both within the scientific community using the vocabulary specific to the discipline, and externally through the channels of scientific dissemination.
These skills are strengthened through practical and applicative activities that involve the realization, presentation and discussion of clinical and psychometric reports or projects carried out individually or in small groups, role-playing, discussion of cases, reading and discussion of scientific articles, simulations, the development of a research project. Communication skills and the ability to synthesize are evaluated through oral interviews and/or written tests with open questions in the profit exams relating to the different teachings, as well as through the presentation and discussion of the final thesis.
V - Learning ability: The Psychologist will be able to use the tools of analysis and apply the learning methods developed in order to deepen and update his/her knowledge by independently following the new acquisitions of scientific research, using appropriate computer tools, including the use of tools for bibliographic consultation. The acquisition of effective and flexible learning skills will allow the graduate to continue training and updating independently even after obtaining the degree, knowing how to find and evaluate the different sources and materials useful for continuing education at a specialist level.
The achievement of this objective is achieved through the use and constant reference, within the curricular courses, to the most relevant and up-to-date national and international literature on the topics covered, in order to develop an attitude of constant comparison between one's own knowledge and the most recent developments in knowledge in the various areas of interest of psychology and neuroscience. This attitude is evaluated in particular in the individual work carried out by the student for the preparation of the final examination, through the evaluation of his/her ability to query databases, accessing an international bibliography on the proposed topics, to illustrate the novelties introduced by scientific research, to identify which problems, in the different areas of competence, pose further questions to the development of research and in which directions.
Function in the work context.
Function in the work context:
The knowledge and skills acquired allow the graduate to perform the following functions:
- Gather information and analyze the main forms of psychological distress and/or maladjustment through anamnetic interviews and collection of behavioral data.
- Move from diagnostic assessment to taking charge of the client/user, referring to different therapeutic models.
- Propose and negotiate concrete and achievable objectives with the client/user.
- Select and apply tools aimed at detecting indices of psychobiological, behavioral, cognitive and emotional functioning in counseling settings.
- Select and apply tools for identifying the modes of relationship of the individual with the reference groups, with particular attention to the effects produced by these relationships.
- Select and apply tools for the evaluation of communication and relational skills in different social and environmental contexts.
- Design prevention and health promotion interventions for individuals, groups or communities with integrated approaches, and analyze the results.
- Use techniques and application tools derived from the most recent contributions of clinical and experimental research.
These tasks involve synergistic collaboration with other professionals in the field of mental health in different application areas in public and private contexts.
Skills related to the function.
Skills related to the function:
The psychologist possesses:
- advanced and up-to-date knowledge of the main models of normal and pathological psychological functioning, and of the relationships between cognition and brain functions;
- the ability to administer and interpret tools for the assessment of cognitive and emotional functioning;
- the ability to conduct assessment and psychological support interviews, referring to different therapeutic models;
- the ability to administer and interpret the main tools of psychological assessment;
- the ability to design prevention and health promotion interventions aimed at individuals, groups or communities;
- the ability to collaborate with critical spirit, autonomy of judgment and recognition of specific professionalism with all the other figures involved in interventions on psychological well-being;
- the ability to constantly update their knowledge through the critical reading of scientific texts, also in English;
- adequate transversal skills of a communicative-relational, organizational-managerial and programming type, in accordance with the level of autonomy and responsibility assigned, with the organizational and working methods adopted and with the main interlocutors (colleagues, other professionals and clients/users).
Professional status conferred by the degree.
Job opportunities:
Pursuant to articles 1 and 3 of Law 8 November 2021, n. 163, and in accordance with DIM n. 654 of 05/07/2022, the final examination for the award of the Master's Degree in Clinical, Applied Psychology and Intervention (LM-51 class) qualifies to practice as a Psychologist.
The graduate in Clinical, Applied Psychology and Intervention will be able to use the knowledge and skills acquired in the training course in public and private healthcare organizations involved in the prevention, diagnosis and treatment of psychological distress (National Health Service, hospitals and clinics, territorial services, counseling centers, therapeutic communities, addiction services, residential homes, communities for minors, Prevention Departments, Public Health services, private third sector agencies such as cooperatives or volunteer associations), in organizations and institutions for care, rehabilitation and assistance to individuals, public and private. Further professional opportunities can be found in educational and school structures, in the University and in other institutions for scientific research. The Psychologist can carry out the profession and related functions also as a freelancer and within the framework of private consultancy (also as an expert) and training, with particular reference to the processes of assessment in different contexts, to the identification and design of change strategies.

Program, texts and objectives: Official language(s) of teaching and assessment.
ITALIAN.
Degree awarded: Master's Degree in DESIGN AND MANAGEMENT OF SOCIAL AND EDUCATIONAL SERVICES AND INTERVENTIONS.
Specific learning objectives: The chosen educational path focuses on the complexity of the interdisciplinary approach, not limiting itself to the usual disciplinary proximity between professional subjects and sociological and pedagogical subjects, but establishing, from the first year, the comparison on sociological and pedagogical subjects with a deliberately less theoretical approach, on the political science subjects, more attentive to local governments and intergovernmental relations. The common path of the first year includes, in fact, an in-depth study of pedagogical themes, through the provision of courses that allow the acquisition of educational research methodologies and an in-depth study of the themes of special education, as well as sociological themes, to which is added the study of the regulatory tools that govern the design in the social and educational sectors. The course is completed through the provision of optional courses that allow graduates of the class to deepen, alternatively, themes of a demo-ethno-anthropological nature or to acquire the fundamentals of financial management of companies.
In the second year, the course is structured around two educational curricula: the Specialist Social Worker (recognized in section A of the Register of Social Workers), and the Expert in the design of social policies.
In addition to the ability to work with users who turn to social services, the professional who is intended to be trained must acquire the professional skills necessary for him to carry out functions of programming, organization and management of socio-health services, of direction of work groups and coordination of the services provided and the personnel employed in these services; he must acquire the necessary skills for a specialist use of cognitive strategies, communication, inter-individual relationship with professional interlocutors and with users, moreover he must develop his organizational skills in micro-systems, in the regulation of educational interventions and in the management of change. The curricular path also aims at increasing professional skills in research, monitoring, protection of health and the environment.
For this reason, the two curricular paths, although with different contents, provide for the acquisition of the management tools - which focus on the programming and evaluation of social services (Specialist Social Worker Curriculum) and on the management of training activities (Expert in the design of social policies Curriculum) -; of the organization of human resources and economic resources and which presupposes a common basis, which deepens the tools for planning and organization of social policies, a necessary prerequisite for social design. Furthermore, an in-depth study of some pedagogical themes is planned to allow graduates to acquire advanced tools for design in the field of inclusion and cooperation.
The skills acquired and developed during the educational path can be used in the sectors of health, education, family, immigration, exclusion and social marginalization. And it is for these reasons that graduates of this course must possess advanced knowledge regarding the organization and functioning of social and educational services.
They must also know and be able to refer to the organizational, social and legislative framework within which intervention plans in the field of services are developed.
To this end, master's degree graduates must also develop skills aimed at reading the territory, the ability to know and interpret social phenomena and the trends of their evolution, in order to be able to form the necessary skills for the experimentation of new programs and new approaches not only with the users of social services and with situations of latent need, but also in the different realities that express training needs.
The acquisition of these skills will give graduates the possibility to develop skills that will allow them to enhance and develop the networking of existing and potentially activated resources, following innovative paths, already in use in other European experiences.
The verification of the learning objectives is based on assessment tests, intermediate and/or final, written and/or oral, of the courses and integrative activities that make up the study plan, in addition, of course, to the final test.
Dublin descriptors: I - Knowledge and understanding: Social intervention in general and design in particular presuppose that graduates acquire the ability to know and interpret social phenomena in order to identify the need and consequently plan and design interventions through the networking of existing resources and the activation of new resources. Hence the interdisciplinarity that characterizes the course and ensures that the knowledge that constitutes its core is acquired through the courses belonging to the sociological and social work, economic and statistical, legal and psycho-pedagogical disciplines.
The acquisition of these skills is verified through assessment tests, intermediate and/or final, written and/or oral, of the courses and integrative activities that make up the study plan, in addition, of course, to the final test.
II - Ability to apply knowledge and understanding: The master's degree graduate will acquire methodological, organizational and legal knowledge relating to the socio-health and educational services system, as well as knowledge of the most important forms of mental and social discomfort. This knowledge will allow him to achieve a high capacity for analysis and interpretation of social phenomena; advanced knowledge of the economic, historical and political framework, in relation to specific sectors of sociological and educational analysis applied, of reading the needs of the territory and of designing specific interventions. The ability to apply the acquired knowledge is verified through assessment tests, intermediate and/or final, and integrative activities that provide for the practical application of the theoretical knowledge acquired, in addition to the final test, which must be accompanied by an intervention project which, for the Specialist Social Worker path, must concern the thematic areas of the social service referred to in Law No. 328/2000.
III - Autonomy of judgment: The sensitivity of the professionals that the master's degree course intends to train must necessarily be built on a reflective habit on the methods of application of their own professional methodology and that of others. They must be able to place themselves at a higher level of complexity, essential for reconstructing and framing the action and professional strategies of colleagues, even in the function of case manager. This ability can only derive from a habit of very concrete critical analysis, applied to interventions. Skills that can be better developed thanks to the teaching and integrative teaching activities (in-depth seminars, indirect internship activities), within the master's degree course, of professionals with many years of experience in the design of social and educational policies (including European design), who are able to accompany the students of the class in the acquisition of the theoretical-practical tools for identifying needs and developing appropriate design solutions.
In particular, the master's degree graduate must be able to design and coordinate research in many areas of the social and educational fields; he must be able to analyze and read social problems with full autonomy of judgment, through the application of specific research methods, or through the empirical verification of his initial hypotheses; coordinate and design socio-health services and educational services in the area; design information, awareness and prevention programs with reference to the different forms of psycho-social discomfort; design and program services for the community according to the needs of the territory.
The verification of the acquisition of autonomy of judgment takes place through the evaluation of the courses of the individual student's study plan, and the evaluation of the degree of autonomy and ability to work, even in a group, during the seminar activities, the internship and the work of preparation of the final test.
IV - Communication skills: The ability to communicate with very different interlocutors, belonging to institutions, the third sector, volunteering, civil society, is crucial in the methodology of networking and working on projects: these remain fixed reference points of the course (in both its paths), also based on its previous tradition, but also the communication to the public of the results of the impact assessments of the interventions is an important skill necessary for all those involved in the design and management of social policies.
Internships, which have always been a crucial and strong point of the training paths, in both paths give students the opportunity to measure themselves against the social reality, understood not only as users of social workers, but as the presence and collaboration of different subjects (public and private) involved in the design and management of social and educational policies.
The verification of the acquisition of communication skills takes place through the evaluation of the student's expository and argumentative ability within the training and seminar activities and the final test itself, as well as through the evaluation of the reports and documents prepared within the individual activities that provide for it.
V - Learning ability: Graduates are guided in a learning path in which the interdisciplinary references around the themes that constitute the skeleton of the training path assume a central role.
Learning skills are acquired in the study path as a whole, with particular regard to the individual study provided, the preparation of individual projects, the internship experience and the activity carried out for the preparation of the final test and the project. The ability to learn is evaluated through continuous verification forms during the training activities, requiring the presentation of data independently obtained, through tutoring activities in the development of individual projects of internship and training, and through the evaluation of the learning ability acquired during the activity related to the final test.
Function in working context:
Function in working context:
- Specialist Social Worker: graduates may carry out functions of organization, management and consultancy to people, organizations and institutions in the field of social policies and services in the following areas: relational dynamics, management of human resources, organization of resources and structures and the economic management of bodies, services and organizations, as well as design of social and educational policies. Graduates may also carry out professional activities, including independent ones, in the prevention, management, research areas, as well as in helping processes of inclusion and social cohesion.
- Expert in the design of social policies: graduates may carry out functions of design, organization, management and consultancy in the field of social and educational policies, from early childhood to adulthood, also with reference to the disadvantaged groups of the population.
Skills associated with the function:
Skills associated with the function:
- Specialist Social Worker: Programming, organization and management of social services, direction of work groups and coordination of the services provided and the personnel employed in these services.
- Expert in the design of social policies: Design and consultancy in the field of social and educational policies.
Professional status conferred by the degree:
Employment opportunities:
- Specialist Social Worker: Graduates may carry out their functions within public and private bodies. Graduates may also carry out professional activities, including independent ones. As it is a regulated profession, the exercise of the functions is subject to passing the state examination and registration in Section A of the Order of Social Workers.
- Expert in the design of social policies: Graduates may carry out their functions within public and private bodies. Graduates may also carry out professional activities, including independent ones.

UNIVERSITY: UNIVERSITY OF STUDIES GABRIELE D'ANNUNZIO – CHIETI/PESCARA
COURSE: [0658] FOREIGN LANGUAGES AND LITERATURES
SECTION: INFORMATION ON STUDY PLANS
URL: https://unich.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/2

INFORMATION ON STUDY PLANS General information relating to the current academic year. Duration: 3 years. Admission: 2022. Status: Open. Credits: 180 CFU. Language: Italian. Course Type: Degree Course. Regulatory Reform: 270/04. Degree Class: L-11 - Class of degrees in Modern Languages and Cultures. Inter-university Course: No. Open Access. Other Locations: PESCARA (Sustainable capacity: 139). Department: DEPARTMENT OF LANGUAGES, LITERATURES AND MODERN CULTURES. Website: https://www.lingue.unich.it/didattica. Admission Requirements: Required knowledge for admission. Those who possess a five-year secondary school diploma or another equivalent qualification recognized abroad under current regulations are admitted to the L11 degree program. Access to the Course of Study is regulated by an assessment of knowledge and skills through a specific verification test. The methods for verifying these knowledge and skills will be determined in the didactic regulations of the Course of Study. In the event of a negative outcome of the verification, additional training obligations will be assigned to be fulfilled during the first year of the course through specific remedial activities established by the didactic regulations. Admission procedures: All students who possess a five-year secondary school diploma or another recognized equivalent qualification are admitted to the Course. At the time of registration, the student must indicate the chosen languages of study as LANGUAGE A and LANGUAGE B (one of which must be European) from those available in the Course Offer. The three-year language (both Language A and B) can only be changed at the time of registration for the second year. The Ministry of Education, University and Research (Article 6 of DM 270/2004) requires all Universities to verify the initial preparation of new students, in order to allow students to assess their personal preparation with respect to the basic knowledge required for university studies, and to identify, also with the help of tutor teachers, individual paths aimed at filling any initial gaps, thus favoring the student's good integration into the chosen course of study. The ministerial provision also clarifies that any training debts must be recovered during the first year of the course. For the L11 degree program, the Verification Test of the knowledge required for admission is mandatory for students enrolled in the first year. All students transferring from other universities and students enrolling in a second degree are exempt from the Test. The Verification Test is held according to a calendar indicated on the website of the Department of Languages, Literatures and Modern Cultures. The scheduled sessions are two: in September and in February. The Commission responsible for the Test is appointed by the Director of the Department. This Commission is made up of a minimum of three and a maximum of five permanent teachers. The Verification Test, lasting 60 minutes, consists of 30 multiple-choice questions aimed at ascertaining an adequate level of text comprehension, knowledge of the morphological-syntactic structures and the vocabulary of the Italian language. Each correct answer is awarded a score of 1 (one), while each unanswered or incorrect answer is awarded a score of 0 (zero). The test is considered passed if the student obtains a score of no less than 20/30. For the student who takes the Test and passes it, the Training Obligations will be considered fulfilled. A negative outcome of the test, however, entails the assignment of an Additional Training Obligation (ATO) to be fulfilled during the first year, by attending a mandatory 24-hour course in Italian language offered by the Department. At the end of the remedial procedures, the student is required to repeat the Test, in order to ascertain the required levels of competence. The debt must be fulfilled within the first year of the course. If the debt is not fulfilled, the Verification Test must be repeated in the following academic year. As per the University's didactic regulations, students who have not fulfilled the ATOs by October 31 of the year following enrollment cannot enroll in the courses of the second year, unless they have acquired, as an alternative, a number equal to at least eighteen CFU in the basic and characterizing courses of the first year. In addition to the Verification Test of the knowledge required for admission, a Placement Test is also administered to ascertain the level of linguistic competence in a language chosen from French, English, Spanish and German. This second Test is used to optimize the didactic organization of the courses and therefore does not entail Additional Training Obligations.

Course type: Degree course. Regulatory reform: 270/04. Degree class: L-12 - Class of degrees in Linguistic Mediation. Inter-university course: No. Open access: Yes. Admission requirements: Required knowledge for admission. Those who possess a high school diploma of five years' duration or another qualification obtained abroad, recognized as suitable according to current regulations, are admitted to the Course of Study. Access to the course of study is regulated by a specific verification test, the methods of which will be determined in the Didactic Regulations of the Course of Study. In the event of a negative outcome of the verification, additional training obligations will be assigned to be fulfilled during the first year of the course through specific remedial activities established by the Didactic Regulations.
Admission procedures: All students who possess a high school diploma of five years' duration or another equivalent qualification are admitted to the Course. At the time of registration, the student must indicate the languages of study chosen as LANGUAGE A and LANGUAGE B (one of which must be European), among those present in the Course Offer. The three-year language (both Language A and B) can only be changed at the time of registration for the second year.
The Ministry of Education, University and Research (Article 6 of DM 270/2004) requires all Universities to verify the initial preparation of new students, in order to allow freshmen to assess their preparation with respect to the basic knowledge required for university studies and to identify, also with the help of tutor teachers, individual paths aimed at filling any initial gaps, promoting the student's good integration into the chosen course of study. The ministerial provision also stipulates that any training debts must be recovered during the first year of the course.
For the L-12 Degree Course, the Verification Test of the knowledge required for admission is mandatory for students enrolled in the first year. All students transferring from other universities and students enrolling in a second degree are exempt from the Test.
The Verification Test will be held according to a calendar that will be published on the website of the Department of Languages, Literatures and Modern Cultures. The scheduled sessions are two: September and February.
The Commission responsible for the Test is appointed by the Director of the Department, after consulting the President of the Degree Course. This Commission is made up of a minimum of three up to a maximum of five tenured professors.
The Verification Test, lasting 60 minutes, includes thirty multiple-choice questions aimed at ascertaining an adequate level of text comprehension, knowledge of the morphological-syntactic structures and the vocabulary of the Italian language. Each correct answer will be awarded a score of 1 (ONE), while each unanswered or incorrect answer will be awarded a score of 0 (ZERO). A negative outcome of the test entails the assignment of an Additional Training Obligation (ATO) to be fulfilled during the first year, by compulsorily attending a 24-hour Italian language course offered by the Department.
At the end of the remedial procedures, the student will be required to repeat the Test, in order to ascertain the required levels of competence. The debt must be repaid within the first year of the course. If the debt is not repaid, the Verification Test must be repeated in the following academic year.
As per the University's didactic regulations, students who have not fulfilled the ATOs by October 31 of the year following enrollment will not be able to enroll in the courses of the second year, unless they have acquired, as an alternative, a number equal to at least eighteen CFU in the basic and characterizing courses of the first year.
In addition to the verification test of the knowledge required for admission, a Placement Test will also be carried out to ascertain the level of linguistic competence in a language chosen from French, English, Spanish and German. This second Test will be used to optimize the didactic organization of the courses and will therefore not entail any Additional Training Obligations.

INFO ON STUDY PLANS General information for the current academic year. Duration: 3 years. Program: 2017. Status: Open. Credits: 180 CFU. Language: Italian. Course Type: Degree Course. Regulatory Framework: 270/04 Reform. Degree Class: L-39 - Class of degrees in Social Work. Inter-university Course: No. Open Access: Yes. Location: CHIETI (Sustainable users: 93). Department: DEPARTMENT OF BUSINESS ECONOMICS. Website: https://class.unich.it/home-class-4001. Teaching Method: Conventional. Knowledge Verification Required for Access: Yes. Course Lecturers: View list. Admission Requirements: Knowledge required for access. With reference to the curricular requirements, all those who possess a secondary school diploma obtained in Italy or abroad and recognized as suitable, according to current regulations, may access the Social Work (L-39) degree program. Furthermore, possession of a good knowledge of spoken and written Italian, a good capacity for logical reasoning, and basic knowledge in social sciences and current affairs is also required. The methods for verifying these knowledge and skills will be determined in the didactic regulations of the degree program. Any identified learning gaps will result in the assignment of Additional Training Obligations (OFA) to be completed after enrollment, during the first year of the course, according to the methods indicated in the Didactic Regulations of the course of study. Admission Procedures: With reference to the curricular requirements, all those who possess a secondary school diploma obtained in Italy or abroad and recognized as suitable, according to current regulations, may access the Social Work (L-39) degree program. For the evaluation of adequate personal preparation, the Department Council appoints a Commission that verifies, through an interview, the possession of the required knowledge. If the Commission deems the candidate's level of knowledge to be sufficient, it expresses a judgment of suitability, which allows enrollment. Those who have obtained a score of at least the minimum threshold to ensure the possession of the required requirements and preparation are exempt from the interview. This minimum threshold is set at 70/100. If this threshold is not reached, the candidate will be required to take an evaluative interview by the Commission appointed to verify the possession of the necessary knowledge. Any learning gaps identified in one or more of the following areas of study: a) Basic knowledge in social sciences and current affairs (SSD SPS/07), b) Approach to the scientific methodology of social sciences (SSD SPS/07), c) Communicative and logical argumentation skills (SSD SPS/08) will result in the assignment of Additional Training Obligations (OFA) to be completed after enrollment, during the first year of the course, through tests or verification interviews entrusted to the individual Lecturers of the aforementioned areas of study. The OFA are considered fulfilled if the students, who have not passed or have not taken the interview, have obtained at least 18 CFU related to basic and characterizing courses in the first year of the course and can therefore be enrolled in the second year.

Admission Requirements: Required knowledge for admission. To access the degree course - Education Sciences program - students must possess adequate general knowledge and the basic knowledge required by the educational path of any upper secondary school or other degree obtained abroad, recognized as suitable. The degree course includes specific training activities for the acquisition of basic knowledge related to education and training sciences, aimed, in particular, at those students who have not studied them in upper secondary school.
The verification of the knowledge required for admission will take place through a multiple-choice test (and/or other type of test) for those enrolled in the Education Sciences program, which is not selective, on general culture content, on basic disciplinary content provided for in the educational paths of any upper secondary school, and on basic knowledge of the disciplines that characterize the degree course. Any negative results will not affect the possibility of enrolling in the course. To compensate for any learning gaps, specific additional activities are planned in the disciplines that characterize the degree course, to be followed in the first year of the course in support of the ordinary training activities.
To access the degree course - Philosophy program - students must possess adequate general knowledge and the basic knowledge required by the educational path of any upper secondary school and certified by the corresponding degree obtained in Italy, or by another degree obtained abroad and recognized as equivalent. At the beginning of the course of study, the possession and extent, within the scope of the general culture required for admission, of the most elementary philosophical notions and skills will be verified, in particular, through an interview and/or a written test. Any negative outcome of the verification will not affect enrollment in the course. If total absence or insufficiency of even minimal basic philosophical culture is ascertained, specific additional teaching activities will be offered on the disciplines that characterize the degree course, which the student must follow in support of the ordinary training activities.

UNIVERSITY: UNIVERSITÀ DEGLI STUDI GABRIELE D'ANNUNZIO – CHIETI/PESCARA
COURSE: [610L] ECONOMIA AZIENDALE
SECTION: INFO PIANI DI STUDIO
URL: https://unich.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/564

INFO PIANI DI STUDIO General information regarding the current academic year.
Duration: 3 years
Program: 2012
Status: Open
Credits: 180 CFU
Language: Italian
Course Type: Laurea (Bachelor's Degree)
Regulation: Riforma 270/04
Degree Class: L-18 - Class of degrees in Economics and Business Management Sciences
Inter-university Course: No
Open Admission: Yes
Other Locations: PESCARA (Sustainable capacity: 109)
Department: DIPARTIMENTO DI ECONOMIA
Website: https://clea.unich.it
Teaching Method: Conventional
Verification of knowledge required for access: Yes
Course Lecturers: View list
Admission Requirements: Knowledge required for access. To be admitted to the Bachelor's Degree program, it is generally necessary to have a five-year secondary school diploma or another equivalent qualification obtained abroad, or a four-year secondary school diploma and the related supplementary year.
Specifically, the following are required for admission to the Bachelor's Degree program in Business Economics:
- knowledge of the Italian language and possession of related language skills as contained in the curricula of all types of secondary schools;
- a general culture that allows understanding and contextualization of the fundamental phenomena of the society in which economic entities operate;
- inclination towards economic and business disciplines;
- basic knowledge of English;
- basic logical-mathematical and computer skills.
The Bachelor's Degree program includes an admission test as provided for in Article 6 of Decree 270/2004.
The test for verifying the knowledge required for admission to the Bachelor's Degree program is considered passed if the student obtains a score equal to or greater than a minimum score set by the Board of the School of Economics, Business, Legal and Social Sciences. In the absence of an explicit decision, the minimum score set in the previous year is considered adopted.
A negative result in the knowledge verification test leads to the assignment of an Additional Training Obligation (OFA), which consists of attending a remedial course offered on the knowledge required for access, held in the first semester.
Verification of the completion of the OFA takes place with the passing of a minimum of 18 CFU, related to courses provided in the first year of the study plan, within the scope of basic, characterizing and related subjects, by the extraordinary examination session of the first academic year.
In the event of failure to complete the OFA within the established deadline, students must still complete the OFA and re-enroll in the first year of the course.
Transfers, changes of course, and admission to individual exams are subject to approval by the Course Council. The Council may grant full or partial recognition of the academic career pursued up to that point, with the validation of exams taken and credits acquired, and indicates the year of the course to which the student is enrolled and any OFA to be completed.

SECTION: INFO PIANI DI STUDIO
URL: https://unich.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/566

INFO PIANI DI STUDIO General information regarding the current academic year. Duration: 3 years. Program start year: 2011. Status: Open. Credits: 180 CFU. Language: Italian. Course type: Laurea (Bachelor's Degree). Regulatory framework: Reform 270/04. Degree class: L-33 - Class of degrees in Economics. Inter-university course: No. Open access: Yes. Other locations: PESCARA (Sustainable capacity: 83). Department: DIPARTIMENTO DI ECONOMIA. Website: https://clec.unich.it/home-clec-66. Teaching method: Conventional. Verification of knowledge required for access: Yes. Course lecturers: View list. Admission requirements: Knowledge required for access. To be admitted to the Bachelor's Degree in Economics and Commerce, applicants must have obtained a high school diploma or another equivalent qualification obtained abroad and recognized as valid. To be admitted to the Bachelor's Degree in Economics and Commerce, applicants must also pass an initial knowledge verification test. The didactic regulations of the course of study govern the methods of verifying the required knowledge and the additional training obligations to be fulfilled in the event of a negative outcome of the verification. In particular:
1. The test for verifying the knowledge required for access to the degree course, pursuant to Article 6 of Decree 270/2004, is considered passed if the student obtains a score equal to or greater than the minimum set by the Board of the School of Economics, Business, Legal and Social Sciences. In the absence of an explicit decision, the minimum set in the previous year is considered adopted.
2. A negative outcome of the knowledge verification test results in the assignment of an additional training obligation (OFA), which consists of attending a remedial course offered on the knowledge required for access, held in the first semester.
3. Verification of the fulfillment of the OFA is carried out by passing a minimum of 18 CFU, related to courses provided in the first year of the study plan, within the scope of basic, characterizing and related subjects, by the extraordinary examination session of the first academic year.
4. In the event of failure to fulfill the OFA within the deadline referred to in paragraph 3 above, students must still fulfill the OFA and re-enroll in the first year of the course.

Admission requirements: Knowledge required for access: To enroll in the Degree Course in Design, applicants must possess a high school diploma obtained in Italy or another equivalent qualification obtained abroad. If the verification of the knowledge required for access is not positive, the didactic regulations of the course will also indicate any additional training obligations that must be completed in the first year of the course. Admission method: The Degree Course in Design has programmed access and requires a mandatory entrance exam, which will be held online via the 'Cineca QUID from home' platform. For the academic year 2024/2025, there are 80 places available for admission to the Degree Course in Design, of which: - 75 places are reserved for EU students, as well as non-EU students residing in Italy. - 5 places are reserved for non-EU students residing abroad, with the possibility of reintegrating EU and Italian students if no eligible non-EU students are found. The selection of candidates and the merit ranking are based on the following evaluation elements: - result of the test - academic record (final exam grade) The test consists of a series of multiple-choice questions with four possible answers, only one of which is correct. The test consists of 40 questions divided into 5 sections to verify the candidates' knowledge in the following subject areas: - Mathematical analysis and Geometry (5 questions) - Drawing and Representation (5 questions) - History of art and design (10 questions) - Logic (5 questions) - General culture and verbal comprehension (15 questions) The points awarded for each answer are: - correct answer: 1 (one) - unanswered or multiple answer: 0 (zero) - incorrect answer: - 0.25 (minus zero point twenty-five) The evaluation of the academic record, which is added to the score obtained in the test, considers the grade obtained in the final exam. The conversion of the final exam grade, obtained by July 2024 and valid for enrollment in a first-level degree course, is obtained according to the following table: - for grades from 70 to 74: 1 point - for grades from 75 to 79: 2 points - for grades from 80 to 84: 4 points - for grades from 85 to 89: 6 points - for grades from 90 to 94: 8 points - for grades from 95 to 100: 10 points - for a grade of 100 with honors: 12 points The merit score of the entrance test also serves as a verification of the knowledge required for access and for the assignment of any additional training obligations (ATO). ATOs are assigned based on the failure to achieve a minimum score in the following subject areas: Mathematical analysis and Geometry: minimum score of 1.5 out of a maximum of 5 points. Drawing and Representation: minimum score of 1.5 out of a maximum of 5 points. History of art and design: minimum score of 3 out of a maximum of 10 points. The ATOs will be fulfilled by participating in individual training activities assigned directly by the reference lecturer or by participating in supplementary teaching courses held by tutors with expertise in the subject areas of the ATOs, or through one-on-one in-depth tutoring within the reference courses. In all cases, a final evaluation is provided through a test or interview with the reference lecturer. The deadline for completing the ATOs assigned in the subject areas of Geometry, Drawing and Representation, and History of Art and Design is set for October 31, 2025. The ATOs assigned in one or more subject areas are considered fulfilled with the passing of the exams in the 1st year of: - Geometry for Design for the subject area of Mathematical Analysis and Geometry - Drawing for Design for the subject area of Drawing and Representation - History of Design for the subject area of History of Art and Design. Enrollment in the second year is allowed, but there is no possibility of taking exams in the second year before completing any assigned ATOs. For students who enroll directly in the 2nd year, the ATOs are considered fulfilled with the achievement of at least 36 CFU in the TAF AeB courses.

Admission Requirements: Required knowledge for admission. To be admitted to the Bachelor's Degree program, applicants must hold a high school diploma or an equivalent qualification obtained abroad, recognized as suitable. In addition, the following are required: a good knowledge of the Italian language, logical reasoning skills, and knowledge and ability to use the main results of elementary mathematics and the fundamentals of experimental sciences. Adequate initial preparation is verified according to the methods described in the Didactic Regulations of the Courses of Study; if this verification is not positive, as can be ascertained through the evaluation of the CISIA tests, specific additional training obligations will be assigned to be completed within the first year of the course.
